stem: Which of the following statements describe a valid test objective?

options.a: To prove that there are no unfixed defects in the system under test
options.b: To prove that there will be no failures after the implementation of the system into production
options.c: To reduce the risk level of the test object and to build confidence in the quality level
options.d: To verify that there are no untested combinations of inputs

explanation:
a) Is not correct. It is impossible to prove that there are no defects anymore in the system under test. See testing principle 1.
b) Is not correct. See testing principle 7.
c) Is correct. Testing finds defects and failures which reduces the level of risk and at the same time gives more confidence in the quality level of the test object.
d) Is not correct. It is impossible to test all combinations of inputs (see testing principle 2).

stem: Which of the following is a typical test objective?

options.a: Validating that documented requirements are met
options.b: Causing failures and identifying defects
options.c: Initiating errors and identifying root causes
options.d: Verifying the test object meets user expectations

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Validation is concerned with meeting user requirements and expectations, while verification is concerned with meeting specified requirements, so this would be correct if we replaced 'validating' with 'verifying'.
b) Is correct. Causing failures and identifying defects is probably the most common objective of dynamic testing.
c) Is not correct. Testers do not initiate errors, they try to cause failures. Errors are typically made by developers (and cannot really be initiated) and result in defects, which testers attempt to identify either directly through static testing or indirectly through failures with dynamic testing. Identifying root causes is useful but is part of debugging, which is a separate activity from testing.
d) Is not correct. Verification is concerned with checking specified (documented) requirements are met, while validation is concerned with meeting user requirements and expectations, so this would be correct if we replaced 'verifying' with 'validating'.

stem: Which of the following is a typical test objective?

options.a: Finding and fixing defects in the test object
options.b: Maintaining effective communications with developers
options.c: Validating that legal requirements have been met
options.d: Building confidence in the quality of the test object

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Finding and fixing defects in the test object is not a typical test objective as although identifying defects is an objective of testing, fixing defects is not a test activity.
b) Is not correct. Maintaining effective communications with developers is not a typical test objective although it is useful in achieving other objectives of testing, such as providing stakeholders with information that enables them to make informed decisions. It is not a primary reason for performing testing.
c) Is not correct. Validating that legal requirements have been met is not a typical test objective because validation is concerned with checking whether the system meets users' and other stakeholders' needs in its operational environment. Checking that legal requirements have been met is a form of verification.
d) Is correct. Building confidence in the quality of the test object is achieved by executing tests that passed.

stem:
A project manager asks what the testing of a new online booking system is meant to achieve. Which of the following is a typical test objective?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Guaranteeing that the booking system will contain no defects once it is in production
options.b: Providing information to stakeholders so that they can make informed decisions about the release
options.c: Locating the faulty source code that causes a failure and correcting it
options.d: Executing every possible combination of input values and preconditions

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Testing cannot prove the absence of defects (principle 1), so this cannot be an objective.
b) Is correct. Giving stakeholders information that supports their decisions is one of the typical test objectives.
c) Is not correct. Finding and fixing the cause of a failure is debugging, not testing.
d) Is not correct. Exhaustive testing is impossible (principle 2) except in trivial cases.

stem:
Which TWO of the following are typical test objectives?

Select TWO options.

options.a: Evaluating work products such as requirements, user stories and designs
options.b: Proving that the test object is free of defects before release
options.c: Removing the root causes of defects from the development process
options.d: Building confidence in the quality of the test object
options.e: Measuring the individual productivity of developers by counting their defects

explanation:
a) Is correct. Evaluating work products (including via static testing) is a typical test objective.
b) Is not correct. Testing shows the presence, not the absence, of defects.
c) Is not correct. Process improvement based on root cause analysis is a quality assurance concern, not a test objective.
d) Is correct. Building confidence in the quality of the test object is a typical test objective.
e) Is not correct. Using defect counts to judge individuals is not a test objective and damages team relationships.

stem:
Consider the following statements:

i. Validating whether the test object works as the stakeholders expect
ii. Verifying that the test object complies with legal and regulatory requirements
iii. Deciding the release budget for the next product version
iv. Ensuring the required coverage of a test object
v. Demonstrating that no failures will occur in operation

Which of these are typical test objectives?

Select ONE option.

options.a: i, iii and v
options.b: ii, iv and v
options.c: i, ii and iv
options.d: i, ii and iii

explanation:
i, ii and iv are typical test objectives (validation against stakeholder expectations, verifying compliance, ensuring coverage). iii is a project management decision. v is not achievable, because testing can only show the presence of defects.
a) Is not correct. iii is a management decision and v is impossible to demonstrate (principle 1).
b) Is not correct. v cannot be achieved by testing: testing cannot show the absence of defects or failures.
c) Is correct. i, ii and iv are all on the list of typical test objectives.
d) Is not correct. iii (deciding a budget) is not a test objective.

stem:
You were given a task to analyze and fix causes of failures in a new system to be released.

Which activity are you performing?

options.a: Debugging
options.b: Software testing
options.c: Requirement elicitation
options.d: Defect management

explanation:
a) Is correct. Debugging is the process of finding, analyzing, and removing the causes of failures in a component or system.
b) Is not correct. Testing is concerned with planning, preparation and evaluation of a component or system and related work products to determine that they satisfy specified requirements, demonstrate fitness for purpose and detect defects. It is not related to fixing causes of failures.
c) Is not correct. Requirement elicitation is gathering, capturing, and consolidating requirements. It is not related to fixing causes of failures.
d) Is not correct. Defect management is recognizing, recording, classifying, investigating, resolving, and disposing of defects. It is not related to fixing causes of failures.

stem: Which of the following statements BEST describes the difference between testing and debugging?

options.a: Testing causes failures while debugging fixes failures
options.b: Testing is a negative activity while debugging is a positive activity
options.c: Testing determines that defects exist while debugging removes defects
options.d: Testing finds the cause of defects while debugging fixes the cause of defects

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Dynamic testing does cause failures (from which defects can then be located and fixed). However, debugging is concerned with locating defects and fixing these defects. Therefore, debugging does not fix failures.
b) Is not correct. Both testing and debugging contribute to improving the quality of the test object, so both should be considered positively. Dynamic testing does involve intentionally causing the test object to fail, which is why some people consider it a negative activity, but that is a very narrow view. Both positive and negative test cases are possible.
c) Is correct. Testing determines that defects exist either directly through observation of the defect in reviews (or by a tool in static analysis), or indirectly by causing a failure in dynamic testing. Debugging is a separate activity from testing (normally performed by developers) and is concerned with locating defects (only for dynamic testing) and fixing the defects.
d) Is not correct. The causes of defects are typically human errors. Testing finds defects either directly through static testing, or indirectly by causing failures in dynamic testing, and debugging fixes defects. So, testing does not find the cause of defects and debugging does not fix the causes of defects.

stem:
A tester executes a test on a checkout page and sees that the order total is wrong. The tester raises a defect report. A developer reproduces the problem, finds that a rounding function is faulty and corrects it. The tester then reruns the original test, which now passes.

Which of the following activities in this scenario are part of debugging?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Executing the original test and observing the wrong order total
options.b: Rerunning the original test after the fix to check that it passes
options.c: Writing the defect report that describes the wrong order total
options.d: Reproducing the failure, diagnosing its cause and fixing the faulty rounding function

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Executing tests that trigger failures is dynamic testing, not debugging.
b) Is not correct. Rerunning the test after the fix is confirmation testing, which is a testing activity.
c) Is not correct. Reporting the anomaly is part of test execution and defect management, not debugging.
d) Is correct. Debugging consists of reproducing the failure, diagnosis (finding the cause) and fixing it.

stem:
During a review of a design document, a reviewer finds that two sections specify contradictory timeout values. Which statement BEST describes the debugging that follows?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Debugging consists of removing the defect; reproduction and diagnosis are not needed because static testing finds defects directly
options.b: Debugging must start by executing the design document to reproduce a failure caused by the contradiction
options.c: No debugging is needed because defects in documents are not real defects until the code is written
options.d: The reviewer must debug the document because whoever finds a defect is responsible for diagnosing it

explanation:
a) Is correct. When static testing finds a defect, debugging is concerned with removing it; there is no failure to reproduce or diagnose.
b) Is not correct. A design document cannot be executed, and static testing finds defects rather than failures.
c) Is not correct. A defect in a work product is still a defect and should be removed, ideally early.
d) Is not correct. Testing and debugging are separate activities; the reviewer is not responsible for fixing the author's work product.

stem: Which of the following options shows an example of test activities that contribute to success?

options.a: Having testers involved during various software development lifecycle (SDLC) activities will help to detect defects in work products
options.b: Testers try not to disturb the developers while coding, so that the developers write better code
options.c: Testers collaborating with end users help to improve the quality of defect reports during component integration and system testing
options.d: Certified testers will design much better test cases than non-certified testers

explanation:
a) Is correct. It is important that testers are involved from the beginning of the SDLC. It will increase understanding of design decisions and will detect defects early.
b) Is not correct. Both developers and testers will have more understanding of each other's work products and how to test the code.
c) Is not correct. End users will not help the testers in increasing the quality of defect reports; also, users usually do not participate in low-level testing levels like integration testing.
d) Is not correct. Being certified does not automatically mean that the tester will be better in test design.

stem: Which of the following is an example of why testing is necessary?

options.a: Dynamic testing increases quality by causing test objects to fail in ways that could never be achieved by the users
options.b: Static testing is used by developers to identify failures in their code earlier than can be achieved through dynamic testing
options.c: Static analysis provides evidence to customers that the elements of the system that provide no outputs are fit for release
options.d: Reviews increase the quality of requirements specifications and lead to fewer changes being needed in derived work products

explanation:
a) Is not correct. It is often possible to use dynamic testing to cause a test object to fail in ways that could never be achieved by the users, such as by using fault injection. However, if the failure can never occur with real end users, then identifying it is not especially valuable as testing is ultimately aimed at improving the work product for the end users. Spending time testing for failures that cannot occur with real users is not an efficient use of a tester's time.
b) Is not correct. Static testing in the form of static analysis is used by developers to identify defects in their code earlier than can be achieved through dynamic testing. However, static testing is used to detect defects, not failures, which are found by dynamic testing. It is the use of the term 'failures' that makes this an incorrect option.
c) Is not correct. Static analysis directly detects defects in code, and this is normally information for the developer, not the customer.
d) Is correct. Reviews are a form of static testing that can be applied from the very start of the SDLC and are used to find defects that can be removed before subsequent development activities waste effort on faulty requirements. If the defects are not detected and removed early on, then when the defect is found in derived work products, such as the design and code, the requirements will need to be changed.

stem:
Which of the following is the BEST example of testing contributing to the success of a project?

Select ONE option.

options.a: A thorough final system test makes reviews of requirements and designs unnecessary
options.b: Testers are kept separate from developers so that developers can concentrate on writing code
options.c: Testers taking part in story refinement detect ambiguous acceptance criteria before any code is written
options.d: Fixing every defect found during testing guarantees that the system will meet user needs

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Dynamic testing does not replace static testing; each finds different kinds of defects.
b) Is not correct. Isolation hinders collaboration; it is not an example of testing adding value.
c) Is correct. Early involvement lets testers find defects in the test basis when they are cheapest to fix, which contributes to success.
d) Is not correct. This is the absence-of-defects fallacy: fixing defects does not guarantee the system meets user needs.

stem:
A team builds an app for elderly users. Involving real users in every iteration is too costly, so testers use personas and carry out usability evaluations themselves. Which reason why testing is necessary does this BEST illustrate?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Testing can represent the users' perspective indirectly when involving users throughout the project is not feasible
options.b: Testing is necessary because it proves that the app is suitable for every possible user
options.c: Testing is necessary mainly to evaluate the performance of the development team
options.d: Testing is required because regulators always demand usability evaluations for apps

explanation:
a) Is correct. Testers can act as indirect representatives of users, which is one of the reasons testing is necessary.
b) Is not correct. Testing cannot prove suitability for every user; it reduces risk and provides information.
c) Is not correct. Testing is not intended to evaluate people's performance.
d) Is not correct. There is no general regulatory requirement for usability testing of apps; the scenario is about representing users.

stem:
A company developing software for infusion pumps must submit evidence of testing to a national authority before the product can be sold. Which statement BEST explains why testing is necessary in this case?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Testing is needed to prove that the pump software contains no remaining defects
options.b: Testing may be needed to meet contractual, legal or regulatory requirements or standards
options.c: Testing is needed so that developers do not have to review their own code
options.d: Testing is needed because the authority will perform the debugging of any failures

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Testing cannot prove there are no defects (principle 1).
b) Is correct. Testing can be necessary to satisfy contractual, legal or regulatory requirements, as in this scenario.
c) Is not correct. Testing does not replace developers' own quality activities such as code reviews.
d) Is not correct. Authorities do not debug the product; debugging is a development activity.

stem: In many software organizations the test department is called the Quality Assurance (QA) department. Is this sentence correct or not and why?

options.a: It is correct. Testing and QA mean exactly the same thing
options.b: It is correct. These names can be used interchangeably because both testing and QA focus their activities on the same quality issues
options.c: It is not correct. Testing is something more; testing includes all activities with regard to quality. QA focuses on quality-related processes
options.d: It is not correct. QA is focused on quality-related processes while testing concentrates on demonstrating that a component or system is fit for purpose and to detect defects

explanation: Testing and quality assurance are not the same. Testing is the process consisting of all SDLC activities, both static and dynamic, concerned with planning, preparation and evaluation of a component or system and related work products to determine that they satisfy specified requirements, to demonstrate that they are fit for purpose and to detect defects. Quality assurance is focused on establishing, introducing, monitoring, improving, and adhering to the quality-related processes. Thus d) is correct.

stem: Which of the following statements about quality assurance (QA) and/or quality control (QC) is correct?

options.a: QA is performed as part of testing
options.b: Testing is performed as part of QC
options.c: Testing is another term for QC
options.d: Testing is performed as part of QA

explanation:
a) Is not correct. QA concentrates on process improvement and implementation, using a preventive approach to avoid errors and defects, while testing is a form of QC that is used to detect defects.
b) Is correct. QC aims to achieve appropriate levels of quality by focusing on identifying and correcting product defects. Testing is a significant part of QC and helps to uncover these defects.
c) Is not correct. Although testing is a significant part of QC, other (non-testing) techniques utilized in QC include formal methods like model checking and proof of correctness, as well as simulation and prototyping.
d) Is not correct. QA concentrates on process improvement and implementation, using a preventive approach, while testing is a form of QC that is used to detect defects.

stem:
Which of the following statements about testing and quality assurance (QA) is correct?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Testing and QA are the same thing, which is why test teams are often called QA teams
options.b: QA is product-oriented and corrective, whereas testing is process-oriented and preventive
options.c: QA is performed only by the test team after testing has finished
options.d: Testing is a form of quality control, which is product-oriented and corrective, whereas QA is process-oriented and preventive

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Testing and QA are not the same; using the terms interchangeably is a common mistake.
b) Is not correct. The orientations are reversed.
c) Is not correct. QA applies to development and testing processes and is the responsibility of everyone on the project.
d) Is correct. Testing is a major form of QC (product-oriented, corrective); QA focuses on establishing and improving processes (process-oriented, preventive).

stem:
How are test results used in quality assurance (QA)?

Select ONE option.

options.a: They are used only to fix defects in the test object
options.b: They replace process audits, which are no longer needed once testing is done
options.c: They provide feedback on how well the development and test processes are performing
options.d: They are used by the QA department to decide which tester caused each failure

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Using test results to fix defects is their use in quality control, not QA.
b) Is not correct. Test results complement other QA activities; they do not replace them.
c) Is correct. In QA, test results give feedback on the effectiveness of the development and test processes.
d) Is not correct. Testers do not cause failures, and QA is not about assigning blame.

stem:
A phone ringing in a neighboring cubicle distracts a programmer causing him to improperly program the logic that checks the upper boundary of an input variable. Later, during system testing, a tester notices that this input field accepts invalid input values.

Which of the following correctly describes an incorrectly coded upper bound?

options.a: The root cause
options.b: A failure
options.c: An error
options.d: A defect

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The root cause is the distraction that the programmer experienced while programming.
b) Is not correct. Accepting invalid inputs is a failure.
c) Is not correct. The error is the mistake in thinking that put the defect in the code.
d) Is correct. The problem in the code is a defect.

stem:
A designer documents a design for a user interface that does not suitably address disabled users because the designer is tired. The programmer implements the user interface in line with the design but as they are working under severe time pressure, they do not include suitable exception handling in their program code for bonus calculations. When the operational system is used, complaints are made by some disabled users about the interface and the company is subsequently fined by the relevant regulatory authority. No one notices that bonus calculations are sometimes incorrect.

Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

options.a: The miscalculation of bonuses is a defect that occasionally occurs
options.b: The fine received for failing to address some disabled users is a failure
options.c: The programmer working under severe time pressure is a root cause
options.d: The design of the user interface includes a designer error

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The miscalculation of bonuses is a failure by the system, not a defect.
b) Is not correct. The system not suitably supporting disabled users is a failure which eventually results in a fine, but the fine itself is not a failure (it appears to be the correct functioning of the regulatory system).
c) Is correct. The error is made by the programmer and this mistake is caused by them working under severe time pressure, which is the root cause of the subsequent defect.
d) Is not correct. The poor design of the user interface, which does not suitably address disabled users, is a design defect caused by the designer error. Thus the design of the user interface includes a design defect not a designer error.

stem:
Under heavy time pressure, a business analyst misreads a new VAT rule and writes an incorrect formula into the specification. The formula is implemented as specified, and customers receive invoices showing the wrong VAT amount.

Match the following terms with the elements of the scenario:

1. Root cause
2. Error
3. Defect
4. Failure

A. The heavy time pressure on the analyst
B. The analyst misreading the VAT rule
C. The incorrect formula in the specification
D. Invoices showing the wrong VAT amount

Select ONE option.
explanation:
A root cause is the fundamental reason for a problem (time pressure). An error (mistake) is a human action that produces an incorrect result (misreading the rule). A defect is the resulting flaw in a work product (the wrong formula in the specification and code). A failure is the observable deviation when the system runs (wrong VAT on invoices).
a) Is not correct. Time pressure is the fundamental reason (root cause); the misreading is the human error.
b) Is correct. The CORRECT match is 1A, 2B, 3C, 4D.
c) Is not correct. The misreading is the error (a human action); the wrong formula is the defect it produced.
d) Is not correct. The wrong VAT on invoices is an observed failure, not a defect, and time pressure is not a failure.

stem:
Which of the following statements about errors, defects and failures is correct?

Select ONE option.

options.a: A defect in the code does not always lead to a failure, for example when the defective code is never executed
options.b: Every failure is caused by a defect in the code of the test object
options.c: An error is the result of executing a defect and is observed by the tester
options.d: Root cause analysis is performed to find failures before the software is executed

explanation:
a) Is correct. Defects cause failures only when the defective code is executed under particular conditions.
b) Is not correct. Failures can also be caused by environmental conditions, e.g. radiation or electromagnetic fields.
c) Is not correct. An error is a human mistake that can produce a defect; the observed result is a failure.
d) Is not correct. Root cause analysis identifies the fundamental reasons for failures or defects so that similar ones can be prevented.

stem: You have been assigned as a tester to a team producing a new system incrementally. You have noticed that no changes have been made to the existing regression test cases for several iterations and no new regression defects were identified. Your manager is happy, but you are not. Which testing principle explains your skepticism?

options.a: Tests wear out
options.b: Absence-of-defects fallacy
options.c: Defects cluster together
options.d: Exhaustive testing is impossible

explanation:
a) Is correct. This principle means that if the same tests are repeated over and over again, eventually these tests no longer find any new defects. This is probably why the tests all passed in this release as well.
b) Is not correct. This principle is about the mistaken belief that just finding and fixing a large number of defects will ensure the success of a system.
c) Is not correct. This principle says that a small number of components usually contain most of the defects.
d) Is not correct. This principle states that testing all combinations of inputs and preconditions is not feasible.

stem: One of the ‘principles of testing’ states that exhaustive testing is impossible. Which of the following is an example of addressing this principle in practice?

options.a: Creating test cases that cover every possible specified output
options.b: Documenting all possible test input variations and prioritizing these based on importance
options.c: Starting testing as early as possible with reviews and other static testing approaches
options.d: Using equivalence partitioning and boundary value analysis to generate test cases

explanation:
The 'exhaustive testing is impossible' principle is concerned with the fact that it is not feasible to test every possible variation of inputs in all different circumstances, except in trivial cases. Instead, testing utilizes test techniques, test case prioritization, and risk-based testing to sample from the set of possibilities and focus test efforts.
a) Is not correct. Testing every possible expected result will not address this problem as the relationship between inputs and expected results can be different for each test object; sometimes there may be a practically infinite number of possible expected results (e.g., several variables representing real numbers), at other times just two (e.g., a single true/false variable).
b) Is not correct. For non-trivial systems there is a practically infinite number of input variations, so documenting all of them would be impractical as it would take an infinite length of time.
c) Is not correct. Starting testing early with reviews and other static testing will not address the problem of there being too many possible test cases. The 'early testing saves time and money' principle is concerned with fixing defects early to prevent subsequent defects in derived work products.
d) Is correct. Equivalence partitioning and boundary value analysis provide a systematic way to derive a finite subset of all possible test cases.

stem: The 'absence-of-defects fallacy' is one of the principles of testing. Which of the following is an example of addressing this principle in practice?

options.a: Explaining that it is not possible for testing to show the absence of defects
options.b: Supporting the end users to perform acceptance testing
options.c: Ensuring that no implementation defects remain in the delivered system
options.d: Modifying tests that cause no failures to ensure few defects remain

explanation:
The 'absence-of-defects fallacy' is concerned with the idea that ensuring correctness in accordance with the requirements (i.e., verifying the absence of implementation defects) does not guarantee user satisfaction with the system. To address this it is also necessary to validate that the system meets users' needs and expectations, fulfills business objectives, and outperforms competing systems.
a) Is not correct. This partially addresses the 'testing shows the presence, not the absence of defects' principle, not the 'absence-of-defects' fallacy.
b) Is correct. By supporting the end user to perform acceptance testing it should be possible to validate that the system meets users' needs and expectations.
c) Is not correct. It is not possible to ensure that no implementation defects remain in the delivered system ('testing shows the presence, not the absence of defects').
d) Is not correct. Modifying tests that cause no failures is one way to address the 'tests wear out' principle. This will not validate that the system meets users' needs and expectations.

stem: Test conditions are being used by testers to generate test cases and execute tests. Even though the test conditions remain the same, the test cases are varied each time. Which of the following 'principles of testing' is being addressed through the variation of test cases?

options.a: Tests wear out
options.b: Absence-of-defects fallacy
options.c: Early testing saves time and money
options.d: Defects cluster together

explanation:
a) Is correct. The 'tests wear out' principle is concerned with the idea that repeating identical tests on unaltered code is unlikely to uncover novel defects and therefore, modifying tests may be essential. By using test conditions to generate new tests each time, the tests will not be identical and the risk of the tests wearing out is reduced.
b) Is not correct. The 'absence-of-defects fallacy' principle is concerned with ensuring that users' needs are fulfilled even if lots of testing is done and no defects are found (i.e., validation is also necessary). The use of test conditions to generate test cases and execute tests does not directly address this concern.
c) Is not correct. The 'early testing saves time and money' principle is concerned with fixing defects early on to prevent the occurrence of subsequent defects in derived work products, thereby reducing costs and the likelihood of failures. This is typically addressed by starting testing (both static and dynamic) as early as possible, but not by using test conditions to generate test cases and execute tests.
d) Is not correct. The 'defects cluster together' principle is concerned with the distribution of defects in a system, which typically follows a Pareto distribution. The use of test conditions to generate test cases and execute tests does not address this concern, which is typically addressed by risk-based testing.

stem:
Analysis of the last three releases shows that most of the defects reported in production came from two of the fifteen modules. The test manager therefore plans more test effort for these two modules. Which testing principle is being applied?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Tests wear out
options.b: Testing is context dependent
options.c: Exhaustive testing is impossible
options.d: Defects cluster together

explanation:
a) Is not correct. This principle is about repeated tests losing their ability to find new defects.
b) Is not correct. This principle is about adapting the approach to the context, not about the distribution of defects.
c) Is not correct. Although focusing effort helps because exhaustive testing is impossible, the use of defect distribution data is defect clustering.
d) Is correct. A small number of components usually contain most of the defects; predicted clusters are an input to risk-based testing.

stem:
Testers review user stories and acceptance criteria in refinement sessions before development starts, and the defects they find are corrected before any code is written. Which testing principle does this practice MOST directly reflect?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Early testing saves time and money
options.b: Testing shows the presence, not the absence of defects
options.c: Defects cluster together
options.d: Absence-of-defects fallacy

explanation:
a) Is correct. Removing defects early prevents them from causing derived defects later, reducing cost.
b) Is not correct. This principle is about what testing can prove, not about when to test.
c) Is not correct. Nothing in the scenario relates to the distribution of defects.
d) Is not correct. This principle warns that defect-free software may still fail to meet user needs.

stem:
A team building a small marketing website copies the test approach of a safety-critical avionics project, including formal test documentation and full branch coverage. The overhead delays the launch without noticeably improving quality. Which testing principle has the team MOST clearly ignored?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Tests wear out
options.b: Testing is context dependent
options.c: Early testing saves time and money
options.d: Defects cluster together

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The problem is not repetition of the same tests.
b) Is correct. There is no single universal approach to testing; testing must be adapted to the context, such as the criticality of the product.
c) Is not correct. The problem is not the timing of testing but its unsuitable rigor.
d) Is not correct. The scenario does not concern the distribution of defects across components.

stem:
After all 640 regression tests passed, a product owner states: "The release is now free of defects." Which statement BEST reflects the testing principles?

Select ONE option.

options.a: The statement is correct, because a large regression test suite is equivalent to exhaustive testing
options.b: The statement is correct only if the regression tests have been changed in this release
options.c: Passing tests reduce the probability of undiscovered defects remaining but cannot prove that there are none
options.d: The statement is incorrect, because passing tests show that the tests were badly designed

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Exhaustive testing is impossible; 640 tests are far from all combinations of inputs and preconditions.
b) Is not correct. Even updated tests (addressing test wear-out) cannot prove the absence of defects.
c) Is correct. Testing shows the presence, not the absence, of defects; it reduces the probability of undiscovered defects.
d) Is not correct. Passing tests do not imply poor test design; they simply cannot prove the absence of defects.

stem:
You work in a team that develops a mobile application for food ordering. In the current iteration the team decided to implement the payment functionality.

Which of the following activities is a part of test analysis?

options.a: Estimating that testing the integration with the payment service will take 8 person-days
options.b: Deciding that the team should test if it is possible to properly share payment between many users
options.c: Using boundary value analysis (BVA) to derive the test data for the test cases that check the correct payment processing for the minimum allowed amount to be paid
options.d: Analyzing the discrepancy between the actual result and expected result after executing a test case that checks the process of payment with a credit card, and reporting a defect

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Estimating the test effort is part of test planning.
b) Is correct. This is an example of defining test conditions which is a part of test analysis.
c) Is not correct. Using test techniques to derive coverage items is a part of test design.
d) Is not correct. Reporting defects found during dynamic testing is a part of test execution.

stem: Which test activity involves working with test data requirements, test conditions, test environment requirements and test cases?

options.a: Test design
options.b: Test execution
options.c: Test analysis
options.d: Test implementation

explanation:
a) Is correct. Test design involves using test conditions to create test cases and other necessary testware, such as test data requirements and test charters for exploratory testing. Test environment requirements are also specified, including the necessary infrastructure and tools.
b) Is not correct. Test execution involves executing test cases (as part of test procedures), however it does not directly cover the other testware mentioned, such as test data requirements, test environment requirements and test conditions.
c) Is not correct. Test analysis identifies the features that require testing; the test basis is analyzed and defined as test conditions, which are prioritized along with related risks. It does not cover test data requirements, test environment requirements and test cases.
d) Is not correct. Test implementation includes creating test procedures/scripts from test cases, assembling test suites, the test execution schedule, creating test data and building the test environment. While it works explicitly with test cases, and may use test data requirements and test environment requirements, it does not cover test conditions.

stem: Which of the following test activities are MOST likely to involve the application of boundary value analysis and equivalence partitioning?

options.a: Test implementation
options.b: Test design
options.c: Test execution
options.d: Test monitoring
options.e: Test analysis

explanation:
During test analysis the test basis is analyzed and defined as test conditions; the systematic identification of test conditions as coverage items often involves using test techniques both during test analysis and as part of test design. Boundary value analysis and equivalence partitioning are test techniques.
a) Is not correct. Test implementation is mostly concerned with assembling test cases into test procedures, while test techniques create test cases.
b) Is correct. Test design is likely to involve the use of test techniques to create test cases from test conditions and coverage items.
c) Is not correct. Test execution is mostly concerned with executing test procedures (and so test cases), while test techniques create test cases.
d) Is not correct. Test monitoring is mostly concerned with ongoing checks to ensure the plan is being followed.
e) Is correct. Test analysis is likely to involve the use of test techniques to identify test conditions.

stem:
Given the following test tasks:

1. Derive test cases from test conditions
2. Identify reusable testware
3. Organize test cases into test procedures
4. Evaluate the test basis and the test object

And the following test activities:

A. Test analysis
B. Test design
C. Test implementation
D. Test completion

Which of the following BEST matches the tasks with the activities?
explanation:
A. Test analysis - the test basis is analyzed and defined as test conditions, which are prioritized along with related risks; defects in the test basis are typically uncovered and the test object's testability may be assessed (Task 4).
B. Test design - involves using test conditions to create test cases and other necessary testware, such as test data requirements and test charters (Task 1).
C. Test implementation - test procedures (manual and automated test scripts) are created from test cases and may be assembled into test suites, prioritized and arranged in a test execution schedule (Task 3).
D. Test completion - occurs at project milestones; testware is identified and archived or handed to the appropriate teams for reuse, the test environment is shut down, and lessons learned are analyzed (Task 2).
Thus:
a) Is not correct.
b) Is correct. The CORRECT match is: 1B, 2D, 3C, 4A.
c) Is not correct.
d) Is not correct.

stem:
Given the following test tasks:

1. Identifying and prioritizing test conditions based on the test basis
2. Creating test data and setting up the test environment
3. Comparing actual results with expected results and logging anomalies
4. Archiving testware and analyzing lessons learned

And the following test activities:

A. Test completion
B. Test implementation
C. Test analysis
D. Test execution

Which of the following BEST matches the tasks with the activities?

Select ONE option.
explanation:
Test analysis identifies and prioritizes test conditions from the test basis (1). Test implementation creates the testware needed for execution, such as test data, and builds the test environment (2). Test execution runs tests, compares actual and expected results and logs anomalies (3). Test completion archives testware and analyzes lessons learned (4).
a) Is not correct. Creating test data and the environment is implementation, while comparing results is execution.
b) Is not correct. Identifying test conditions is analysis and creating test data is implementation.
c) Is correct. The CORRECT match is 1C, 2B, 3D, 4A.
d) Is not correct. Comparing results is execution, and archiving testware is completion.

stem:
A tester is elaborating prioritized test conditions into test cases, identifying the coverage items and specifying the test data requirements. Which test activity is the tester performing?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Test analysis
options.b: Test implementation
options.c: Test monitoring and control
options.d: Test design

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Test analysis identifies and prioritizes the test conditions, which are the input to this work.
b) Is not correct. Test implementation creates test procedures, test data and the environment, rather than specifying test cases.
c) Is not correct. Monitoring and control compares progress against the plan and takes corrective actions.
d) Is correct. Test design elaborates test conditions into test cases and other testware, including coverage items and test data requirements.

stem:
Halfway through a test cycle, the test manager sees that the defect density in the reporting module is far higher than expected and reassigns two testers to that module. Which test activity does this BEST describe?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Test monitoring and control
options.b: Test planning
options.c: Test completion
options.d: Test analysis

explanation:
a) Is correct. Checking progress against the plan and taking actions to meet the test objectives is test monitoring and control.
b) Is not correct. Test planning defines objectives and the approach before testing; this is a reaction during testing.
c) Is not correct. Test completion happens at milestones such as the end of a cycle or release, not halfway through.
d) Is not correct. Test analysis defines what to test (test conditions); it does not reallocate resources.

stem:
Consider the following tasks:

i. Evaluating the test basis to identify defects and assess testability
ii. Defining and prioritizing test conditions together with related risks
iii. Assembling test procedures into test suites
iv. Identifying the features to be tested
v. Preparing the test completion report

Which of these tasks are part of test analysis?

Select ONE option.

options.a: ii, iii and iv
options.b: i, ii and iv
options.c: i, iv and v
options.d: i, ii and iii

explanation:
Test analysis analyzes the test basis to identify testable features (iv) and to define and prioritize test conditions with the related risks (ii); the test basis and test object are also evaluated for defects and testability (i). Assembling test suites (iii) is test implementation and the test completion report (v) is produced in test completion.
a) Is not correct. iii belongs to test implementation.
b) Is correct. i, ii and iv are test analysis tasks.
c) Is not correct. v belongs to test completion.
d) Is not correct. iii belongs to test implementation.

stem:
Which of the following factors have a SIGNIFICANT influence on the test approach?

i. The SDLC
ii. The number of defects detected in previous projects
iii. The identified product risks
iv. New regulatory requirements forcing formal white-box testing
v. The test environment setup

options.a: i, ii have significant influence
options.b: i, iii, iv have significant influence
options.c: ii, iv, v have significant influence
options.d: iii, v have significant influence

explanation:
i. True. The SDLC has an influence on the test approach.
ii. False. The number of defects detected in previous projects may have some influence, but this is not as significant as i, iii and iv.
iii. True. The identified product risks are one of the most important factors influencing the test approach.
iv. True. Regulatory requirements are important factors influencing the test approach.
v. False. The test environment has no significant influence on the test approach.
Thus b) is correct.

stem: Which of the following is MOST likely to impact how testing is performed for a given test object?

options.a: The average level of experience of the organization’s marketing team
options.b: The knowledge of users that a new system is being developed for them
options.c: The number of years’ experience of the members of the test team
options.d: The end user’s organizational structure for a commercial music streaming application

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The organization's marketing team is unlikely to perform much testing (although in some organizations they may be involved with acceptance testing), so their average level of experience is not likely to impact how testing is performed for a given test object.
b) Is not correct. The level of knowledge of users that a new system is being built for them is unlikely to affect how testing is performed. Any user involvement that could affect testing is more likely to result from decisions made by the testers, customer and project manager.
c) Is correct. The number of years' experience of the members of the test team will help to determine the capabilities and knowledge (e.g., of different tools and defect types) that the team members will apply when they are testing.
d) Is not correct. The organizational structure of the different end users (who may be varied) will change between users, so it may not even be known when the application is being tested, and can thus have little effect on how the testing is performed.

stem:
Which of the following is the BEST example of how context influences the test process?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Because ISTQB defines the test techniques, they are applied in the same way in every project
options.b: Because testing is an independent process, it is not affected by the chosen SDLC
options.c: Because exit criteria are fixed by the test tool, they cannot be adapted to the project
options.d: Because the bank must comply with financial regulations, test cases and their results are documented in detail and traced to requirements

explanation:
a) Is not correct. There is no single universal approach; techniques are selected according to the context.
b) Is not correct. The SDLC (engineering practices, development methods) is an important context factor.
c) Is not correct. Exit criteria are defined in test planning according to the context, not by the tool.
d) Is correct. Legal and regulatory needs of the business domain are a context factor that affects documentation and traceability.

stem:
Consider the following factors:

i. The skills and availability of team members
ii. The time and budget available to the project
iii. The order in which the testing principles are listed in the syllabus
iv. The product architecture and technology used
v. The numbering scheme used for test case identifiers

Which of these are context factors that significantly influence the test process?

Select ONE option.

options.a: i, ii and iv
options.b: i, iii and v
options.c: ii, iv and v
options.d: i, ii and iii

explanation:
Context factors include stakeholders, team members (i), business domain, technical factors such as architecture and technology (iv), project constraints such as scope, time and budget (ii), organizational factors, the SDLC and tools. iii and v are trivial details that do not significantly affect testing.
a) Is correct. i (team members), ii (project constraints) and iv (technical factors) are context factors.
b) Is not correct. iii and v have no significant influence on the test process.
c) Is not correct. v is an administrative detail without significant influence.
d) Is not correct. iii is irrelevant to how testing is performed.

stem:
Team X develops a casual mobile game with weekly releases. Team Y develops railway signalling software. Which statement BEST explains how their test processes are likely to differ?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Both teams should use the same test process, because testing principles apply to all projects
options.b: Team Y is likely to need more rigorous techniques, higher coverage and more formal documentation because its business domain is safety-critical
options.c: Team X is likely to need more formal documentation because it releases more frequently
options.d: Team Y needs less testing because signalling software is usually certified by an authority

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Principles are general, but the test process must be adapted to the context.
b) Is correct. The criticality and risks of the business domain strongly influence test rigor, coverage and formality.
c) Is not correct. Frequent releases usually favour lightweight documentation and automation, not more formality.
d) Is not correct. Certification increases, rather than reduces, the need for thorough, documented testing.

stem:
Consider the following testware.

> **Test Charter #04.018** — Session time: 1h
> **Explore:** Registration page
> **With:** Different sets of incorrect input data
> **To discover:** Defects related to accepting the registration process with the incorrect input

Which test activity produces this testware as an output?

options.a: Test planning
options.b: Test monitoring and test control
options.c: Test analysis
options.d: Test design

explanation: The testware under consideration is a test charter. Test charters are the output from test design. Thus d) is correct.

stem:
Given the following testware:
1. Coverage items
2. Change requests
3. Test execution schedule
4. Prioritized test conditions

And the following test activities:
A. Test analysis
B. Test design
C. Test implementation
D. Test completion

Which of the following BEST shows the testware produced by the activities?
explanation:
A. Test analysis - prioritized test conditions (4) (e.g., acceptance criteria), and defect reports for defects identified in the test basis.
B. Test design - prioritized test cases, test charters, coverage items (1), test data requirements, and test environment requirements.
C. Test implementation - test procedures, automated test scripts, test suites, test data, test execution schedule (3), and test environment elements such as stubs, drivers, simulators, and service virtualizations.
D. Test completion - test completion report, documented lessons learned, action items for improvement, and change requests (2) (as product backlog items).
Thus: a) Is correct. The correct match is 1B, 2D, 3C, 4A. b), c), d) Are not correct.

stem:
Given the following testware:

i. Test completion report
ii. Data held in a database used for test inputs and expected results
iii. The list of elements needed to build the test environment
iv. Documented sequences of test cases in execution order
v. Test cases

Which of the following BEST shows the testware produced as a result of performing test implementation?

options.a: ii, iv
options.b: iii, v
options.c: i, ii, v
options.d: i, iii, iv

explanation:
i. The test completion report is an output of test completion.
ii. Data held in a database used for inputs and expected results is the test data - output of test implementation.
iii. The list of elements needed to build the test environment is the test environment requirements - output of test design.
iv. Documented sequences of test cases in execution order are the test procedures - output of test implementation.
v. Test cases - output of test design.
Test implementation produces: test procedures (iv), automated test scripts, test suites, test data (ii), test execution schedule, and test environment elements such as stubs, drivers, simulators, and service virtualizations.
Thus:
a) Is correct. Items ii and iv are produced as a result of test implementation.
b) Is not correct.
c) Is not correct.
d) Is not correct.

stem:
Given the following testware:

1. Test charters
2. Stubs and service virtualizations
3. Test logs
4. Documentation of control directives

And the following test activities:

A. Test monitoring and control
B. Test design
C. Test implementation
D. Test execution

Which of the following BEST matches the testware with the activity that produces it?

Select ONE option.
explanation:
Test design produces test cases, test charters, coverage items and data/environment requirements (1). Test implementation produces test procedures, scripts, suites, test data and test environment elements such as stubs, drivers, simulators and service virtualizations (2). Test execution produces test logs and defect reports (3). Test monitoring and control produces progress reports, documentation of control directives and risk information (4).
a) Is not correct. Test charters come from test design; environment elements such as stubs from test implementation.
b) Is not correct. Test logs are produced during test execution and control directives during monitoring and control.
c) Is not correct. Stubs are created in test implementation, and test logs in test execution.
d) Is correct. The CORRECT match is 1B, 2C, 3D, 4A.

stem:
Which of the following work products is typically produced during test completion?

Select ONE option.

options.a: The test execution schedule
options.b: Coverage items and test data requirements
options.c: Documented lessons learned and action items for improvement of later projects
options.d: The risk register and entry criteria

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The test execution schedule is produced during test implementation.
b) Is not correct. These are produced during test design.
c) Is correct. Test completion produces the test completion report, action items for improvement, lessons learned and change requests.
d) Is not correct. These are produced during test planning.

stem: Which of the following is the BEST example of how traceability supports testing?

options.a: Performing the impact analysis of a change will give information about the completion of the tests
options.b: Analyzing the traceability between test cases and test results will give information about the estimated level of residual risk
options.c: Performing the impact analysis of a change will help selecting the right test cases for regression testing
options.d: Analyzing the traceability between the test basis, the test objects and the test cases will help in selecting test data to achieve the assumed coverage of the test object

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Performing the impact analysis will not give information about completeness of tests; it helps to select the right test cases for execution.
b) Is not correct. Traceability does not give information about the estimated level of residual risk if the test cases are not traced back to risks.
c) Is correct. Performing the impact analysis of the changes helps in selecting the test cases for the regression test.
d) Is not correct. Traceability between test basis, test objects and test cases does not help in selecting test data; selecting test data is more related to test analysis and test implementation.

stem: Which of the following statements is a CORRECT example of the value of traceability?

options.a: Traceability between the mitigated risks and test cases that passed provides a means of determining the level of residual risk
options.b: Traceability between user requirements and test results provides a means of measuring project progress against business goals
options.c: Traceability between testers and test cases that failed provides a means of determining the skill level of the testers
options.d: Traceability between the identified risks and written test conditions provides a means of determining which risks are worth testing

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Traceability between mitigated risks and passed test cases provides little information, because to be mitigated (by testing) the risks would need a corresponding passing test case anyway. To assess residual risk, traceability between all risks and test results is needed, so that risks without a corresponding passing test can be identified as residual risks.
b) Is correct. Traceability between user requirements and test results indicates which user requirements have been tested and so provides a means of measuring project progress (in the context of testing) against business goals.
c) Is not correct. Failed test cases do not indicate testers' skills any more than passed ones; it would partly depend on the test objective. Such measurement can also be counter-productive, causing testers to optimize their testing for the metric rather than the test objective.
d) Is not correct. Traceability between identified risks and written test conditions shows which further test conditions need to be written. Determining which risks are worth testing is part of risk management (risk mitigation in particular).

stem:
Late in an iteration the business changes requirement REQ-27 on discount calculation. Bidirectional traceability is maintained between requirements, test cases and test results. How does this traceability help the team MOST?

Select ONE option.

options.a: It allows the team to identify which test cases are affected by the change and need to be updated and rerun
options.b: It ensures that the change to REQ-27 will not introduce any regression defects
options.c: It removes the need to review the changed requirement
options.d: It reduces the number of test cases needed to cover the changed requirement

explanation:
a) Is correct. Traceability supports impact analysis of changes by linking test basis elements to the testware that covers them.
b) Is not correct. Traceability supports analysis; it cannot prevent or exclude defects.
c) Is not correct. The changed requirement should still be reviewed; traceability does not replace static testing.
d) Is not correct. Traceability shows coverage; it does not reduce the number of test cases needed.

stem:
Which TWO of the following are benefits of maintaining traceability between the test basis, testware and test results?

Select TWO options.

options.a: It guarantees that each requirement is covered by exactly one test case
options.b: It allows evaluation of the level of residual risk in the test object by linking test results to risks
options.c: It removes the need for configuration management of testware
options.d: It makes test execution faster because tests no longer need expected results
options.e: It makes test progress reports more understandable to stakeholders by relating results to business requirements

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Traceability shows coverage but does not require or guarantee one test case per requirement.
b) Is correct. Tracing test results to risks enables the residual risk to be evaluated.
c) Is not correct. Configuration management is still needed to identify and version testware.
d) Is not correct. Expected results are still required; traceability does not affect execution speed in this way.
e) Is correct. Traceability lets status be expressed in terms stakeholders understand, such as which requirements have passed tests.

stem: Which TWO of the following tasks belong MAINLY to a testing role?

options.a: Configure test environments
options.b: Maintain the product backlog
options.c: Design solutions to new requirements
options.d: Create the test plan
options.e: Analyze the test basis

explanation:
a) Is correct. This is done by the testers.
b) Is not correct. The product backlog is built and maintained by the product owner.
c) Is not correct. This is done by the development team.
d) Is not correct. This is a managerial role.
e) Is correct. This is done by the testers since it is a technical task done as part of test analysis.

stem: Which of the following statements about the different testing roles is MOST likely to be CORRECT?

options.a: In Agile software development, the test management role is the primary responsibility of the team, while the testing role is primarily the responsibility of a single individual from outside the team
options.b: The testing role is primarily responsible for test monitoring and test control, while the test management role is primarily responsible for test planning and test completion
options.c: In Agile software development, test management activities that span multiple teams are handled by a test manager outside the team, while some test management tasks are handled by the team itself
options.d: The test management role is primarily responsible for test analysis and test design, while the testing role is primarily responsible for test implementation and test execution

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Some test management tasks may be handled by the Agile team itself, but the testing role is not primarily the responsibility of a single individual from outside the team; testing is more likely performed by various team members following the whole-team approach.
b) Is not correct. The test management role primarily involves test planning, test monitoring and test control, and test completion. So it is wrong to say that the testing role is primarily responsible for test monitoring and test control.
c) Is correct. In Agile software development, some of the test management tasks may be handled by the Agile team itself. However, for test activities that span multiple teams within an organization, test managers outside of the development team may perform these tasks.
d) Is not correct. The testing role is primarily responsible for the technical and engineering aspects of testing (test analysis, test design, test implementation, and test execution). The test management role is not normally responsible for test analysis and test design.

stem: Which of the following is MOST likely to describe a task performed by someone in a test management role?

options.a: Evaluate the test basis and the test object
options.b: Define test environment requirements
options.c: Assess testability of the test object
options.d: Create the test completion report

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The testing role is primarily responsible for the technical and engineering aspects of testing (test analysis, design, implementation, execution). Evaluating the test basis for defects and the test object for testability are tasks performed as part of test analysis, so they are likely performed by the testing role.
b) Is not correct. Defining the test environment requirements is a task performed as part of test design, so it is likely to be performed by the testing role.
c) Is not correct. Assessing the testability of a test object is a task performed as part of test analysis, so it is likely to be performed by the testing role.
d) Is correct. The test management role primarily involves test planning, test monitoring and test control, and test completion. Creating the test completion report, the prime output from test completion, is likely to be a task performed by the test management role.

stem:
In an organization using Agile development, how are the tasks of the test management role MOST likely to be handled?

Select ONE option.

options.a: All test management tasks are performed by the product owner
options.b: Some tasks are handled by the Agile team itself, while tasks spanning several teams may be performed by test managers outside the team
options.c: The test management role is not needed, because Agile teams do not plan or monitor testing
options.d: Each tester performs all test management tasks for the whole organization

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The product owner does not take over all test management tasks.
b) Is correct. In Agile, some test management tasks are taken by the team; cross-team or organization-wide tasks may be done by test managers outside it.
c) Is not correct. Testing is still planned, monitored and controlled in Agile projects.
d) Is not correct. Organization-wide tasks are not performed by every individual tester.

stem:
Which TWO of the following tasks belong MAINLY to the test management role?

Select TWO options.

options.a: Designing test cases from prioritized test conditions
options.b: Executing tests and comparing actual with expected results
options.c: Producing the test completion report at the end of a release
options.d: Implementing automated test scripts for regression testing
options.e: Taking corrective actions when test progress deviates from the test plan

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Test design is mainly a task of the testing role.
b) Is not correct. Test execution is mainly a task of the testing role.
c) Is correct. Test completion is mainly the responsibility of the test management role.
d) Is not correct. Test implementation is mainly a task of the testing role.
e) Is correct. Test monitoring and control is mainly a task of the test management role.

stem:
Which of the following statements about the testing role and the test management role is correct?

Select ONE option.

options.a: The test management role can only be performed by a person with the job title test manager
options.b: The testing role is concerned only with test execution
options.c: The same person may take on the testing role and the test management role at different times
options.d: The test management role is mainly responsible for designing test cases

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The role can be taken by team leaders, development managers or the team itself, depending on context.
b) Is not correct. The testing role covers test analysis, design, implementation and execution.
c) Is correct. Roles are not job titles; one person can perform different roles at different times.
d) Is not correct. Test design is mainly a task of the testing role; test management focuses on planning, monitoring, control and completion.

stem:
Which of the following skills (i-v) are the MOST important skills of a tester?

i. Having domain knowledge
ii. Creating a product vision
iii. Being a good team player
iv. Planning and organizing the work of the team
v. Critical thinking

options.a: ii and iv are important
options.b: i, iii and v are important
options.c: i, ii and v are important
options.d: iii and iv are important

explanation:
i. True. Having domain knowledge is an important tester skill.
ii. False. This is a task of the business analyst together with the business representative.
iii. True. Being a good team player is an important skill.
iv. False. Planning and organizing the work of the team is a task of the test manager or, mostly in an Agile software development project, the whole team and not just the tester.
v. True. Critical thinking is one of the most important skills of testers.
Thus b) is correct.

stem: Which of the following is MOST likely to be an example of a tester using a generic skill when testing?

options.a: The tester’s deep knowledge of a variety of computer games meant that they got on well with one of the developers who was also into gaming
options.b: The tester was a former pilot and was better able to understand the acceptance criteria for the helicopter control system
options.c: The tester previously worked as a programmer and used their skills in this area to better communicate with the business analysts
options.d: The tester was very careful not to make mistakes when they methodically generated test cases prior to starting their exploratory testing session

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Strong communication skills, active listening and teamwork enable a tester to interact effectively with all stakeholders, however a deep knowledge of computer games that allowed them to get on well with one developer is not an example of a generic skill useful to testers.
b) Is correct. Domain knowledge that can be used to understand and communicate with end users and business representatives is one of the generic skills required by testers. Experience as a pilot makes the tester better able to appreciate the acceptance criteria for the helicopter control system.
c) Is not correct. Programming skills could be considered technical knowledge which can increase efficiency when using some test tools, but it is unlikely they would improve communication with business analysts.
d) Is not correct. Thoroughness, attention to detail and a methodical approach are useful generic skills, but it is doubtful they would be generating test cases prior to exploratory testing, since in exploratory testing the test cases are generated during the testing, not scripted in advance.

stem:
A tester has found a serious defect in a module written by a developer who is very proud of the code. Which generic skill is MOST important for reporting this defect effectively?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Programming skills, so that the tester can rewrite the module
options.b: Domain knowledge, so that the tester can decide whether to report the defect
options.c: Knowledge of test tools, so that the report can be submitted automatically
options.d: Good communication skills, delivering the bad news in a constructive and diplomatic way

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Rewriting the module is not the tester's task and would not improve the relationship.
b) Is not correct. A serious defect should be reported regardless; the challenge here is communication.
c) Is not correct. Tool knowledge does not address how the message is received by the developer.
d) Is correct. Information about defects can be perceived as criticism, so it must be communicated constructively.

stem:
Consider the following:

i. Knowledge of testing, e.g. test techniques
ii. Thoroughness, curiosity and attention to detail
iii. Authority to approve the release budget
iv. Analytical thinking, critical thinking and creativity
v. Responsibility for the product vision

Which of these are generic skills required for testing?

Select ONE option.

options.a: ii, iii and iv
options.b: i, iv and v
options.c: i, ii and v
options.d: i, ii and iv

explanation:
Generic skills for testing include testing knowledge (i), thoroughness, carefulness, curiosity, attention to detail and being methodical (ii), good communication and active listening, analytical and critical thinking and creativity (iv), technical knowledge and domain knowledge. Approving budgets (iii) and owning the product vision (v) are not tester skills.
a) Is not correct. iii is a management authority, not a skill.
b) Is not correct. v is a responsibility of the product owner, not a testing skill.
c) Is not correct. v is not a generic testing skill.
d) Is correct. i, ii and iv are generic skills of testers.

stem:
A tester who previously worked as a nurse joins a team building a hospital medication management app. Which is the MOST likely benefit of this tester's background?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Domain knowledge helps the tester to understand and communicate with end users and business representatives
options.b: Domain knowledge allows the tester to skip test design and rely on intuition only
options.c: Domain knowledge makes technical knowledge of tools unnecessary
options.d: Domain knowledge ensures the tester will find all defects in the app

explanation:
a) Is correct. Domain knowledge supports understanding of, and communication with, end users and business representatives.
b) Is not correct. Domain knowledge supports test techniques; it does not replace test design.
c) Is not correct. Technical knowledge is still needed, e.g. to use test tools effectively.
d) Is not correct. No skill makes it possible to find all defects.

stem: How is the whole team approach present in the interactions between testers and business representatives?

options.a: Business representatives decide on test automation approaches
options.b: Testers help business representatives to define a test strategy
options.c: Business representatives are not part of the whole team approach
options.d: Testers help business representatives to create suitable acceptance tests

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The test automation approach is defined by testers with the help of developers and business representatives.
b) Is not correct. The test strategy is decided in collaboration with the developers.
c) Is not correct. Testers, developers, and business representatives are part of the whole team approach.
d) Is correct. Testers will work closely with business representatives to ensure that the desired quality levels are achieved. This includes supporting and collaborating with them to help them create suitable acceptance tests.

stem: Which of the following is an advantage of the whole-team approach?

options.a: It allows team members to take on any role at any time
options.b: It only needs a single team to support the complete development project
options.c: It embeds business representatives alongside developers in the same team
options.d: It generates a team synergy that benefits the entire project

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The whole-team approach allows any team member with the requisite skills and knowledge to undertake any task, but that does not mean team members can take on any role at any time. Typically, they only take on roles in which they are competent.
b) Is not correct. The whole-team approach applies to how a single team (typically in Agile software development) works; it does not cover how multiple teams work on larger projects, and does not suggest that only one 'whole' team is needed for a complete project.
c) Is not correct. The whole-team approach does not expect every team member to be involved in every important decision. For instance, there is no need for the business representative (i.e., the Product Owner) to be involved in every technical decision that does not affect the business outcome, and doing so would unnecessarily slow down the team's progress.
d) Is correct. By leveraging the diverse skill sets of each team member most effectively, the whole-team approach fosters superior team dynamics, promotes robust communication and collaboration, and generates a team synergy that benefits the entire project.

stem: Which of the following is an advantage of the whole-team approach?

options.a: Teams with no testers
options.b: Improved team dynamics
options.c: Specialist team members
options.d: Larger team sizes

explanation:
a) Is not correct. In the whole-team approach, testers play a vital role by sharing their testing expertise with the team and guiding product development; they collaborate with other team members, business representatives and developers.
b) Is correct. By leveraging the diverse skill sets of each team member most effectively, the whole-team approach fosters superior team dynamics, promotes robust communication and collaboration, and generates a synergistic effect that benefits the entire project.
c) Is not correct. The whole-team approach allows any team member with the requisite skills and knowledge to undertake any task, thus specialist team members are not an advantage of this approach.
d) Is not correct. There is no specific guidance on the optimum size of teams using the whole-team approach, and no suggestion that larger teams are better.

stem: Which of the following is an advantage of the whole team approach?

options.a: Improved communication between team members
options.b: Decreased individual accountability for quality
options.c: Faster deployment of deliverables to the end users
options.d: Reduced collaboration with external business users

explanation:
a) Is correct. The whole team approach promotes robust communication and collaboration between the team members.
b) Is not correct. While the whole team approach prioritizes collective accountability for quality, each individual team member is still equally accountable for quality.
c) Is not correct. The whole team approach is about how the team works together, with the aim of higher quality deliverables, but it does not necessarily result in faster deployment to end users.
d) Is not correct. When using the whole team approach, testers work with business representatives to create acceptance tests. There is no suggestion that the approach will reduce collaboration with external business users.

stem:
Which of the following is an advantage of the whole team approach?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Testers no longer need to collaborate with business representatives
options.b: The various skill sets within the team can be leveraged for the benefit of the project
options.c: Quality becomes the sole responsibility of the testers in the team
options.d: Independent test teams become mandatory for every product

explanation:
a) Is not correct. In the whole team approach, testers work closely with business representatives, e.g. on acceptance tests.
b) Is correct. Leveraging the team's various skill sets is an advantage of the whole team approach.
c) Is not correct. Everyone is responsible for quality in the whole team approach.
d) Is not correct. The whole team approach does not mandate independent test teams.

stem:
Which of the following statements about the whole team approach is correct?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Everyone in the team is responsible for quality, not only the testers
