options.b: It always replaces the need for independent testing, even for safety-critical systems
options.c: It requires the testers to work in a separate test team outside the development team
options.d: It means that developers perform all testing so testers are no longer needed

explanation:
a) Is correct. Making everyone responsible for quality is a central advantage of the whole team approach.
b) Is not correct. In some contexts, such as safety-critical systems, a high level of test independence may still be needed.
c) Is not correct. The approach places testers within the team, working closely with other members.
d) Is not correct. Testers remain important team members who share testing knowledge and work with others.

stem:
Which of the following is an advantage of the whole team approach?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Reduced need for testers to understand the business domain
options.b: Elimination of all defects before system testing begins
options.c: Improved communication and collaboration within the team
options.d: A clear separation between the people who develop and the people who test

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Testers still need domain understanding to work with business representatives.
b) Is not correct. No approach can eliminate all defects.
c) Is correct. Improved communication and collaboration are advantages of the whole team approach.
d) Is not correct. Separation is a feature of independent testing, not of the whole team approach.

stem:
Which TWO of the following are advantages of the whole team approach?

Select TWO options.

options.a: Testers transfer testing knowledge to other team members and influence product development
options.b: Developers can skip component testing because the testers write all the tests
options.c: A high level of test independence is achieved without any further measures
options.d: Testers work closely with business representatives to create suitable acceptance tests
options.e: Defects can no longer escape into production

explanation:
a) Is correct. Sharing testing knowledge across the team is an advantage of the whole team approach.
b) Is not correct. Everyone shares responsibility for quality; developers still test their components.
c) Is not correct. The whole team approach typically gives lower independence; more may be needed in some contexts.
d) Is correct. Collaboration with business representatives on acceptance tests is an advantage of the whole team approach.
e) Is not correct. No approach guarantees that defects do not reach production.

stem: Which of the following BEST explains a benefit of independence of testing?

options.a: The use of an independent test team allows project management to assign responsibility for the quality of the final deliverable to the test team
options.b: If a test team external to the organization can be afforded, then there are distinct benefits in terms of this external team not being so easily swayed by the delivery concerns of project management and the need to meet strict delivery deadlines
options.c: An independent test team can work separately from the developers, need not be distracted with project requirement changes, and can restrict communication with the developers to defect reporting through the defect management system
options.d: When specifications contain ambiguities and inconsistencies, assumptions are made on their interpretation, and an independent tester can be useful in questioning those assumptions and the interpretation made by the developer

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Quality should be the responsibility of everyone working on the project and not the sole responsibility of the test team.
b) Is not correct. It is not a benefit if an external test team does not meet delivery deadlines, and there is no reason to believe external test teams will feel they do not have to meet strict deadlines.
c) Is not correct. It is bad practice for the test team to work in complete isolation; we would expect an external test team to be concerned with changing requirements and to communicate well with developers.
d) Is correct. Specifications are never perfect, so the developer has to make assumptions. An independent tester can challenge and verify the assumptions and the subsequent interpretation made by the developer.

stem: Which of the following statements about the independence of testing is CORRECT?

options.a: Independent testers will find defects due to their different technical perspective from developers, but their independence may lead to an adversarial relationship with the developers
options.b: Developers' familiarity with their own code means they only find a few defects in it, however their shared software background with testers means these defects would also be found by the testers
options.c: Independent testing requires testers who are outside the developer's team and ideally from outside the organization, however these testers find it difficult to understand the application domain
options.d: Testers from outside the developer's team are more independent than testers from within the team, but the testers from within the team are more likely to be blamed for delays in product release

explanation:
a) Is correct. The primary benefit of independence of testing is that testers are more likely to identify different types of failures and defects compared to developers, due to their varied backgrounds, technical viewpoints, and potential biases. The main disadvantage is that testers may become isolated from the development team, leading to communication problems, lack of collaboration, and potentially an adversarial relationship, with testers being blamed for delays and bottlenecks.
b) Is not correct. A developer's familiarity with the code means they can efficiently find many defects in their own code. And developers having a different background to testers is normally cited as the reason that testers and developers find different kinds of defects.
c) Is not correct. Testing can be performed at different levels of independence; testers can be in the developer's team and do not need to come from outside the organization. Knowledge of the application domain is not dependent on the level of independence.
d) Is not correct. Testers from outside the team are generally more independent, but they are likely to be more isolated from the developers and so are more likely to be blamed for delays in product release.

stem:
Given the following benefits and drawbacks of the independence of testing:

i. The testers work in a different location from the developers
ii. Testers question the assumptions programmers make while writing code
iii. A confrontational dynamic has been established between testers and developers
iv. Developers have convinced themselves that testers are mostly accountable for quality
v. Testers have different biases than those held by the developers

Which are MOST likely to be considered benefits?

options.a: i, iv
options.b: ii, v
options.c: i, iii, iv
options.d: ii, iii, v

explanation:
i. Ideally, we want close collaboration between testers and developers, which is not increased by isolation. Thus, this is a disadvantage.
ii. Testers and developers have varied backgrounds, technical viewpoints, and potential biases, allowing testers to usefully challenge assumptions made by stakeholders during specification and implementation. Thus, this is an advantage.
iii. The main disadvantage of independence is that testers may become isolated from the development team, leading to communication problems, lack of collaboration and potentially an adversarial relationship. Thus, this is a disadvantage.
iv. Isolation of testers may lead to developers feeling less accountable for quality. Thus, this is a disadvantage.
v. The primary benefit of independence is that testers are more likely to identify different types of failures and defects compared to developers, due to their varied backgrounds, technical viewpoints, and potential biases, including cognitive bias. Thus, this is an advantage.
Thus:
a) Is not correct.
b) Is correct. The list entries showing benefits are ii and v.
c) Is not correct.
d) Is not correct.

stem:
An organization moves all system testing to an external test lab in another city, and the developers no longer take part in testing. Which drawback of test independence is MOST likely to occur?

Select ONE option.

options.a: The external testers will share the developers' assumptions and biases
options.b: The external testers will find the same kinds of defects as the developers
options.c: Developers may feel less responsible for the quality of their code
options.d: Testing will automatically become cheaper because of the higher independence

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Different assumptions and biases are a benefit of independence, not a drawback.
b) Is not correct. Independent testers tend to find different kinds of failures than developers.
c) Is correct. Isolation of testing can make developers lose their sense of responsibility for quality.
d) Is not correct. Higher independence does not automatically reduce cost; it may even add communication overhead.

stem:
Consider the following statements about independence of testing:

i. Independent testers have different technical perspectives and biases, so they tend to find different kinds of failures
ii. Independent testers may be seen as a bottleneck or blamed for delays in the release
iii. Independent testers can verify and challenge the assumptions stakeholders made during specification
iv. Isolation from the development team may lead to communication problems

Which of the following correctly classifies these statements?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Benefits: i, ii; Drawbacks: iii, iv
options.b: Benefits: i, iii; Drawbacks: ii, iv
options.c: Benefits: i, iv; Drawbacks: ii, iii
options.d: Benefits: iii only; Drawbacks: i, ii, iv

explanation:
Benefits of independence: testers recognize different kinds of failures because of different backgrounds, perspectives and biases (i), and they can verify, challenge or disprove stakeholder assumptions (iii). Drawbacks: isolation can cause communication problems and an adversarial relationship (iv), and independent testers may be seen as a bottleneck or blamed for delays (ii).
a) Is not correct. ii is a drawback and iii is a benefit.
b) Is correct. i and iii are benefits; ii and iv are drawbacks.
c) Is not correct. iv is a drawback and iii is a benefit.
d) Is not correct. i is the main benefit of independence.

stem: You are working as a tester in the team that follows the V-model. Which of the following activities CAN be performed in the initial phases of the SDLC?

options.a: Dynamic test execution
options.b: Static testing
options.c: Test planning
options.d: Acceptance test execution
options.e: Maintenance testing

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The executable code is usually created in the later phases, so dynamic test execution cannot be performed early in the SDLC.
b) Is correct. In sequential development models, in the initial phases, testers participate in requirement reviews, which is a form of static testing.
c) Is correct. Test planning can be performed early in the SDLC before the test project begins, together with test analysis and test design.
d) Is not correct. Acceptance test execution can be performed when there is a working product, which in sequential models is usually delivered later.
e) Is not correct. Maintenance testing requires a working and deployed product, which is not available in the early phases of any SDLC.

stem: Which of the following statements about the chosen software development lifecycle is CORRECT?

options.a: If agile software development is used, automation of system tests replaces the need for regression testing
options.b: If a sequential development model is used, then the dynamic testing is typically restricted to later in the lifecycle
options.c: If an iterative development model is used, then component testing is typically performed manually by developers
options.d: If an incremental development model is used, then static testing is done in early increments and dynamic testing in later increments

explanation:
a) Is not correct. In agile software development, frequent delivery of increments necessitates extensive regression testing. Although some or all of it may be automated, regression testing cannot be replaced by automation of system tests.
b) Is correct. In a sequential development model, early in the SDLC no code is available for execution, so static testing (e.g., reviews) is performed; later, when code is available, dynamic testing is possible. Note that preparation for dynamic testing will often occur early in any SDLC.
c) Is not correct. In an iterative model (e.g., agile), component tests may well be used for regression testing in each iteration, so there is a strong argument for automating them, and unlikely to be a strong argument for developers performing them manually.
d) Is not correct. In most incremental development models, deliverables are produced in each increment, requiring both static and dynamic testing at all test levels for each increment delivered.

stem:
A bank builds its new loan-approval system using a strictly sequential development model. Which of the following statements BEST describes the impact of this choice on testing?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Testers can review the requirements and design documents early, but dynamic testing of the system typically cannot begin until later in the SDLC, once code exists
options.b: Each short iteration delivers a working increment, so testers execute a growing regression suite at the end of every iteration
options.c: Test levels overlap heavily and experience-based techniques dominate because specifications are deliberately kept lightweight
options.d: Dynamic testing starts on the first day of the project because a prototype of the whole system is available from the beginning

explanation:
a) Is correct. In sequential models, testers take part in early static testing (e.g., requirement reviews) while executable code, and therefore dynamic testing, only becomes available later.
b) Is not correct. Delivering a working increment every iteration describes iterative/incremental models, not a strictly sequential one.
c) Is not correct. Overlapping levels and lightweight documentation with heavy use of experience-based testing are typical of Agile/iterative development.
d) Is not correct. A sequential model does not provide an executable prototype at the start; executable code appears only in later phases.

stem:
A product team switches from a sequential model to an iterative and incremental model with two-week iterations. Which change to testing is the team MOST likely to experience?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Static testing becomes unnecessary because each increment is tested dynamically anyway
options.b: A greater need for fast feedback and extensive regression testing, which makes test automation more important
options.c: Each test level is executed only once, at the end of the project, after all increments are complete
options.d: Fewer regression tests are needed because each increment changes only a small part of the system

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Static testing (e.g., reviews of user stories) remains valuable in every SDLC; it is not replaced by dynamic testing.
b) Is correct. Frequent changes delivered in each increment increase the need for regression testing and fast feedback, so automation becomes important.
c) Is not correct. Executing each test level once at the end is a sequential-model characteristic, the opposite of iterative development.
d) Is not correct. Small, frequent changes actually raise the regression risk across increments, so more regression testing is needed, not less.

stem: Consider the following rule: “for every SDLC activity there is a corresponding test activity”. In which SDLC models does this rule hold?

options.a: Only in sequential development models
options.b: Only in iterative development models
options.c: Only in iterative and incremental development models
options.d: In sequential, incremental, and iterative development models

explanation: d) Is correct. This rule holds for all SDLC models. a), b) and c) are not correct.

stem: Which of the following is a good testing practice that applies to all software development lifecycles?

options.a: Testers should review work products as part of the next development phase
options.b: Testers should review work products as soon as drafts are available
options.c: Testers should review work products before test analysis and test design begin
options.d: Testers should review work products immediately after they are published

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Testers should review work products as soon as drafts are available (shift-left). If they waited until the next development phase, unnecessary development (and test) work could be started on unreviewed, flawed work products.
b) Is correct. Testers should review work products as soon as drafts are available to enable early testing as part of a shift-left approach.
c) Is not correct. Testers typically review work products that form the test basis as part of test analysis, not before test analysis and test design.
d) Is not correct. Waiting until work products are published means that any defects that could be found by the tester's review will be in the published document.

stem: Which of the following is a good testing practice that applies to all software development lifecycles?

options.a: For each test level, there is a corresponding development level
options.b: For each test objective, there is a corresponding development objective
options.c: For every test activity, there is a corresponding user activity
options.d: For every development activity, there is a corresponding test activity

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Every software development activity has a corresponding test activity, but there is no common understanding of the term 'development level'.
b) Is not correct. Test objectives are quite different; e.g., a test objective of adhering to a contractual requirement for a certain type of testing has no corresponding development objective.
c) Is not correct. The same symmetry does not apply to testing and user activities; for some systems it is difficult to even identify the end users, and some test activities are focused on developers (e.g., testing for maintainability).
d) Is correct. Quality control applies to all development activities, meaning that every software development activity has a corresponding test activity.

stem: Which of the following is a good testing practice that applies to all software development lifecycles?

options.a: Each test level has specific and distinct test objectives
options.b: Test implementation and execution for a given test level should start during the corresponding development phase
options.c: Testers should start test design as soon as drafts of the relevant work products become available
options.d: Every dynamic testing activity has a corresponding static testing activity

explanation:
a) Is correct. Each test level has specific and distinct test objectives as a different form of test object (e.g., single component and complete system) is tested at each test level and overlapping test objectives would lead to unnecessary duplication.
b) Is not correct. Test analysis and test design for a given test level should start during the corresponding development phase to facilitate early testing (e.g., acceptance test analysis and design should begin during requirements analysis). Test implementation will generally start later, and test execution will start during the test level.
c) Is not correct. Test design should start during the corresponding development phase, however test design (e.g., test case generation) needs to be based on an agreed test basis, not an early draft, otherwise significant test effort may be wasted on test cases for a design that later changes.
d) Is not correct. Every software development activity has a corresponding test activity. However, the same symmetry does not apply to dynamic and static testing. There are some static testing activities (e.g., static analysis) for which there is no obvious corresponding dynamic testing activity.

stem:
Which of the following is a good testing practice that applies to ALL software development lifecycles?

Select ONE option.

options.a: All test levels are executed in each iteration to ensure full regression coverage
options.b: Testers join the project once the first executable build is available so that their effort is not wasted
options.c: Test analysis and design for a given test level begin during the corresponding development phase
options.d: Each test level shares the same test objectives so that testing is consistent across levels

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Executing all test levels in each iteration is not a universal good practice; it is neither feasible nor required in every SDLC.
b) Is not correct. Good practice is the opposite: testers should be involved in reviewing work products as soon as drafts are available.
c) Is correct. This is one of the good practices listed for all SDLCs: early test analysis and design aligned with the corresponding development activity.
d) Is not correct. Good practice states that each test level has its own specific test objectives, not identical ones.

stem:
Which TWO of the following are good testing practices that apply regardless of the chosen SDLC?

Select TWO options.

options.a: For every software development activity there is a corresponding test activity
options.b: Test cases are written only after the test object has been delivered to the test environment
options.c: Testers are involved in reviewing work products as soon as drafts of them are available
options.d: Different test levels are merged into one to avoid duplicated testing effort
options.e: Test automation is applied to every test case so that manual testing can be eliminated

explanation:
a) Is correct. This is a good practice for all SDLCs: every development activity is subject to quality control.
b) Is not correct. Waiting for delivery delays test design; good practice is to start test analysis and design early.
c) Is correct. Early tester involvement in reviewing drafts supports shift left and is listed as a good practice for all SDLCs.
d) Is not correct. Good practice keeps separate test levels with specific objectives while avoiding redundancy; merging them is not a recommended practice.
e) Is not correct. Full automation is neither always feasible nor a universal good practice; manual testing still has value.

stem:
Why does the syllabus recommend that each test level has specific test objectives?

Select ONE option.

options.a: So that the same test cases can be reused unchanged at every test level
options.b: So that each test level can be performed by the same independent test team
options.c: So that test levels can be skipped when the previous level passed without failures
options.d: So that testing is comprehensive while avoiding unnecessary redundancy between levels

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Specific objectives imply different focuses per level, not reuse of identical test cases at all levels.
b) Is not correct. Objectives are not about who performs the testing; different levels are often performed by different people.
c) Is not correct. Specific objectives are not a mechanism for skipping levels.
d) Is correct. Specific objectives per level ensure appropriate coverage of different aspects while avoiding redundancy.

stem:
A team writes the acceptance test conditions for a feature while the business analyst is still refining the related requirements. Which good testing practice is the team applying?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Test analysis and design for a test level begin during the corresponding development phase
options.b: For every test level there is a matching development level of equal duration
options.c: Each test level is planned only after the preceding test level has been completed
options.d: Test cases are derived exclusively from the source code to ensure accuracy

explanation:
a) Is correct. Starting test analysis while the requirements are being refined is exactly this practice, supporting the principle of early testing.
b) Is not correct. There is no such practice; the good practice is that every development activity has a corresponding test activity.
c) Is not correct. This would delay testing; it is not one of the good practices.
d) Is not correct. Acceptance test conditions are derived from requirements/test basis, not from code; this is not a listed practice.

stem: Which of the following statements BEST describes the acceptance test-driven development (ATDD) approach?

options.a: In ATDD, acceptance criteria are typically created based on the given/when/then format
options.b: In ATDD, test cases are mainly created at component testing and are code-oriented
options.c: In ATDD, tests are created, based on acceptance criteria to drive the development of the related software
options.d: in ATDD, tests are based on the desired behavior of the software, which makes it easier for team members to understand them

explanation:
a) Is not correct. It is more often used in behavior-driven development (BDD).
b) Is not correct. It is the description of test-driven development (TDD).
c) Is correct. In ATDD tests are written from acceptance criteria as part of the design process.
d) Is not correct. It is used in BDD.

stem: Which of the following is an example of a test-first approach to development?

options.a: Test-Driven Development
options.b: Coverage-Driven Development
options.c: Quality-Driven Development
options.d: Feature-Driven Development

explanation:
a) Is correct. Test-Driven Development (TDD) is a well-known example of a test-first approach to development.
b) Is not correct. Coverage-Driven Development is not a correct example of a test-first approach.
c) Is not correct. Quality-Driven Development is not a correct example of a test-first approach.
d) Is not correct. Feature-Driven Development is not a test-first approach but an agile software development methodology based around delivering features (as opposed to user stories in Scrum).

stem: Which of the following is an example of a test-first approach to development?

options.a: Component Test-Driven Development
options.b: Integration Test-Driven Development
options.c: System Test-Driven Development
options.d: Acceptance Test-Driven Development

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Component Test-Driven Development is not a correct example of a test-first approach to development.
b) Is not correct. Integration Test-Driven Development is not a correct example of a test-first approach to development.
c) Is not correct. System Test-Driven Development is not a correct example of a test-first approach to development.
d) Is correct. Acceptance Test-Driven Development (ATDD) is a well-known example of a test-first approach to development.

stem: Which of the following is an example of a test-first approach to development?

options.a: Behavior-Driven Development
options.b: Test Level Driven Development
options.c: Function-Driven Development
options.d: Performance-Driven Development

explanation:
a) Is correct. Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) is a well-known example of a test-first approach to development.
b) Is not correct. Test Level Driven Development is not a correct example of a test-first approach to development.
c) Is not correct. Function-Driven Development is not a correct example of a test-first approach to development.
d) Is not correct. Performance-Driven Development is not a correct example of a test-first approach to development.

stem:
Which of the following is a test-first approach to development?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Exploratory testing
options.b: Behavior-driven development (BDD)
options.c: Continuous delivery
options.d: Static analysis

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Exploratory testing is an experience-based test technique, not a development approach.
b) Is correct. BDD is one of the three test-first approaches named in the syllabus, together with TDD and ATDD.
c) Is not correct. Continuous delivery is a DevOps practice for deploying software; it is not a test-first approach.
d) Is not correct. Static analysis is a form of static testing performed by tools, not a test-first development approach.

stem:
Which statement BEST describes test-driven development (TDD)?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Tests are derived from acceptance criteria as part of system design before the feature is developed
options.b: Desired behavior is expressed in Given/When/Then format so that it is understandable to all stakeholders
options.c: Tests are written first, then the code is written to pass them, and then the tests and the code are refactored
options.d: Tests are written after coding, by an independent tester, to avoid author bias

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Deriving tests from acceptance criteria describes ATDD.
b) Is not correct. Given/When/Then expressions of desired behavior characterize BDD.
c) Is correct. This is the TDD cycle: coding is directed by test cases instead of extensive up-front design.
d) Is not correct. Writing tests after coding is not a test-first approach at all.

stem:
Match the test-first approaches (1-3) with their descriptions (A-C).

1. TDD
2. ATDD
3. BDD

A. Desired behavior is expressed in simple natural language, typically Given/When/Then, and then translated into executable tests
B. Tests are derived from acceptance criteria as part of the system design process before the part of the application is developed
C. Coding is directed by test cases written before the code, followed by refactoring of tests and code

Select ONE option.
explanation:
a) Is not correct. This swaps TDD and ATDD; acceptance criteria drive ATDD, not TDD.
b) Is not correct. This swaps ATDD and BDD; Given/When/Then is characteristic of BDD.
c) Is not correct. This swaps TDD and BDD; refactoring of tests and code is the TDD cycle.
d) Is correct. TDD drives coding through tests (C), ATDD derives tests from acceptance criteria (B), BDD uses natural-language Given/When/Then behavior (A).

stem:
Consider the following statements about test-first approaches:

i. In ATDD, tests are written before the part of the application they cover is developed.
ii. In BDD, test cases are always executed manually because they are written in natural language.
iii. TDD is mainly applied to component (unit) level tests.
iv. Test-first approaches require that all tests are written by business representatives.

Which statements are TRUE?

Select ONE option.

options.a: i and iii
options.b: ii and iv
options.c: i and ii
options.d: iii and iv

explanation:
a) Is correct. ATDD tests are written before development (i) and TDD is code-oriented, typically at component level (iii).
b) Is not correct. Both are false: BDD scenarios are usually translated into executable tests, and tests are not written solely by business representatives.
c) Is not correct. ii is false: BDD natural-language scenarios are typically automated.
d) Is not correct. iv is false: developers write TDD tests and teams collaborate in ATDD/BDD.

stem:
Which of the following are advantages of DevOps?

i. Faster product release and faster time to market
ii. Increases the need for repetitive manual testing
iii. Constant availability of executable software
iv. Reduction in the number of regression tests associated with code refactoring
v. Setting up the test automation framework is inexpensive since everything is automated

options.a: i, ii, iv are advantages
options.b: iii, v are advantages
options.c: i, iii are advantages
options.d: ii, iv, v are advantages

explanation:
i. True. Faster product release and faster time to market is an advantage of DevOps.
ii. False. Typically, less effort is needed for manual tests because of the use of test automation.
iii. True. Constant availability of executable software is an advantage.
iv. False. More regression tests are needed.
v. False. Not everything is automated and setting up a test automation framework is expensive.
Thus c) is correct.

stem: Which of the following statements about DevOps is CORRECT?

options.a: To speed up releases, continuous integration is used to encourage developers to submit code quickly without the need to complete component testing
options.b: To be able to update and release systems on a more frequent basis, many automated regression tests are required to reduce the risk of regression
options.c: To treat both developers and operations equally, the testers will allocate more effort to release testing by operations using a shift-right approach
options.d: To create increased synergy between testers, developers and operations, the testing must become fully automated with no manual testing

explanation:
a) Is not correct. DevOps promotes a shift-left approach with high-quality code submission and component tests. In continuous integration developers submit component (unit) tests with their new code, which must pass for the code to be admitted to the build, so developers do need to complete component testing.
b) Is correct. DevOps enhances testing by providing fast feedback on code quality, automated regression testing that minimizes regression risk, and promoting a shift-left approach with high-quality code submission and component tests.
c) Is not correct. Testers do not attempt to treat developers and operations equally by spending more time on release testing, although a shift-right approach (testing in production) may well be used.
d) Is not correct. CI/CD in DevOps facilitates stable test environments and reduces the need for manual testing, however there is a risk of overlooking the importance of manual testing, especially from a user's perspective.

stem: Which of the following is MOST likely to be a challenge encountered when implementing DevOps?

options.a: Making sure that non-functional quality characteristics are not overlooked
options.b: Managing continuously changing test environments
options.c: The need for more manual testers with suitable experience
options.d: Setting up the test automation as part of the delivery pipeline

explanation:
a) Is not correct. DevOps generally increases the visibility of non-functional quality characteristics, such as performance and reliability.
b) Is not correct. Automated processes like continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) used in DevOps facilitate stable test environments.
c) Is not correct. Automated processes like CI/CD used in DevOps generally reduce the need for manual testing.
d) Is correct. DevOps implementation can pose several risks and challenges, including the need to define and set up the delivery pipeline, introduce and maintain CI/CD tools, and establish and maintain test automation.

stem:
An organization adopts DevOps with a continuous integration and delivery pipeline. Which of the following is the MOST likely impact on testing?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Manual testing from the user's perspective is no longer needed
options.b: Developers get fast feedback on code quality and on whether changes adversely affect existing code
options.c: Non-functional quality characteristics receive less attention because the pipeline focuses on functionality
options.d: The number of automated regression tests decreases because changes are released in small batches

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Even with a high level of automation, manual testing from the user's perspective is still needed.
b) Is correct. Fast feedback through the pipeline is one of the main benefits of DevOps for testing.
c) Is not correct. DevOps actually increases the view on non-functional characteristics such as performance and reliability.
d) Is not correct. DevOps relies on extensive automated regression testing to minimize regression risk; the number does not decrease.

stem:
Which TWO of the following are challenges or risks for testing when introducing DevOps?

Select TWO options.

options.a: Developers receive feedback on their code changes much later than before
options.b: The delivery pipeline must be defined and established
options.c: Stable test environments are harder to establish because processes become automated
options.d: Test automation requires additional resources and may be difficult to establish and maintain
options.e: Regression risk increases because fewer tests are run per change

explanation:
a) Is not correct. DevOps gives faster feedback, not slower; this is the opposite of an impact of DevOps.
b) Is correct. Defining and establishing the delivery pipeline is listed as a DevOps risk/challenge.
c) Is not correct. Automated processes such as CI/CD actually help establish stable test environments.
d) Is correct. This is a DevOps risk/challenge listed in the syllabus.
e) Is not correct. With a broad automated regression suite, regression risk is reduced, not increased.

stem: Which of the following is NOT an example of the shift-left approach?

options.a: Reviewing the user requirements before they are formally accepted by the stakeholders
options.b: Writing a component test before the corresponding code is written
options.c: Executing a performance efficiency test for a component during component testing
options.d: Writing a test script before setting up the configuration management process

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Early review is an example of the shift-left approach.
b) Is not correct. TDD is an example of the shift-left approach.
c) Is not correct. Early non-functional testing is an example of the shift-left approach.
d) Is correct. Test scripts should be subject to configuration management, so it makes no sense to create the test scripts before this process is set up.

stem: Which of the following provides the BEST description of shift-left?

options.a: When agreed by the developers, manual activities on the left-hand side of the test process are automated to support the principle of 'early testing saves time and money'
options.b: Where cost-effective, test activities are moved earlier in the software development lifecycle (SDLC) to reduce the total cost of quality by reducing the number of defects found later in the SDLC
options.c: When they have spare time available, testers are required to automate tests for regression testing, starting with component tests and component integration tests
options.d: When available, testers are trained to perform tasks early in the SDLC to allow more test activities to be automated later in the SDLC

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Shift left is aimed at implementing more test activities in the early phases of the SDLC, portraying the SDLC as moving from left to right. There is no such thing as the left-hand side of the test process.
b) Is correct. Shift left emphasizes the importance of starting testing earlier in the SDLC. It necessitates additional training, and increased effort and costs during the early phases of the SDLC; nevertheless, overall savings should be higher.
c) Is not correct. Automated component and component integration tests for regression testing are generally valuable (and normally the developers' responsibility), but this is not part of shift left, which moves testing earlier in the SDLC.
d) Is not correct. Training testers to perform tasks early in the SDLC would support shift left, but automating more test activities to be performed later in the SDLC is not part of shift-left.

stem:
Which of the following activities is an example of shift left?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Postponing performance testing until the full system is deployed in production-like hardware
options.b: Writing the test completion report at the end of the release
options.c: Running static analysis on the source code as part of the automated build, before dynamic testing starts
options.d: Adding beta testing at customer sites after system testing

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Delaying non-functional testing is the opposite of shift left; it should start at component level where possible.
b) Is not correct. Test completion reporting is a closing activity, not about moving testing earlier.
c) Is correct. Completing static analysis before dynamic testing, or as part of an automated process, is an example of shift left.
d) Is not correct. Beta testing happens late in the SDLC; it does not move testing earlier.

stem:
A project manager is concerned that applying shift left will increase costs in the early stages of the project. Which statement BEST addresses this concern?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Shift left does not cause any additional effort, because it only reorders existing test activities
options.b: Shift left reduces the cost of testing by removing the need for system and acceptance testing
options.c: Shift left only affects developers, so the testing budget is not influenced
options.d: Shift left may require extra training, effort and costs early, but it is expected to save effort and costs later in the process

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Shift left may result in extra training, effort and costs early; claiming no extra effort is incorrect.
b) Is not correct. Shift left does not remove later test levels; it moves testing activities earlier.
c) Is not correct. Shift left involves testers too (e.g., reviews of specifications from a testing perspective) and influences test effort.
d) Is correct. The syllabus notes exactly this trade-off; stakeholder buy-in is important because the savings come later.

stem:
Consider the following practices:

i. Reviewing a specification from the perspective of testing
ii. Running regression tests on the production system after each release
iii. Performing non-functional testing starting at the component test level
iv. Writing test cases before the code is written and running the code in a test harness during implementation
v. Waiting for a stable build before designing any test cases

Which of these practices support shift left?

Select ONE option.

options.a: i, iii and iv
options.b: i, ii and v
options.c: ii, iii and iv
options.d: iii, iv and v

explanation:
a) Is correct. Reviewing specifications from a testing perspective, early non-functional testing and test-first with harness execution are all shift-left examples.
b) Is not correct. ii and v do not move testing earlier; v explicitly delays test design.
c) Is not correct. ii (testing in production after release) is not a shift-left practice.
d) Is not correct. v delays test design, which contradicts shift left.

stem: Which of the arguments below would you use to convince your manager to organize retrospectives at the end of each release cycle?

options.a: Retrospectives are very popular these days and clients would appreciate it if we added them to our processes
options.b: Organizing retrospectives will save the organization money because without them end user representatives do not provide immediate feedback about the product
options.c: Process weaknesses identified during the retrospective can be analyzed and serve as a to do list for the organization’s continuous process improvement program
options.d: Retrospectives embrace five values including courage and respect, which are crucial to maintain continuous improvement in the organization

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Retrospectives are more useful for identifying improvement opportunities and have little importance for clients.
b) Is not correct. Retrospectives are not aimed to collect feedback about the product, but about the process. Additionally, retrospectives are an internal activity for the team and should not include end user representatives.
c) Is correct. Regularly conducted retrospectives, when appropriate follow-up activities occur, are critical to continual improvement of development and testing.
d) Is not correct. Courage and respect are values of Extreme Programming and are not closely related to retrospectives.

stem: Which of the following is LEAST likely to occur as a result of a retrospective?

options.a: The quality of future test objects improves by identifying improvements in development practices
options.b: Test efficiency improves by speeding up the configuration of test environments through automation
options.c: End users' understanding of the development and test processes is improved
options.d: Automated test scripts are enhanced through feedback from developers

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Retrospectives identify potential process improvements which, if put into practice, should result in higher quality of future test objects. So, this is likely to occur.
b) Is not correct. A benefit of retrospectives for testing includes increased test efficiency through process improvements. So, this is likely to occur.
c) Is correct. Participants at retrospectives typically include testers, developers, architects, product owners, and business analysts, but end users are rarely invited and are unlikely to receive any reports from these meetings. So, it is very unlikely that they will understand more about the development and test processes through retrospectives.
d) Is not correct. A benefit of retrospectives for testing includes improved quality of testware (including automated test scripts) through joint reviews with developers. So, this is likely to occur.

stem: Which of the following BEST describes retrospectives?

options.a: Retrospectives allow team members to identify other team members who did not fully contribute to achieving quality as required by the whole team approach
options.b: Retrospectives give testers an opportunity to identify activities that were successful so that these are retained when potential improvements are made in the future
options.c: Retrospectives are where agile team members are allowed to voice their concerns about management and customers in a blameless environment
options.d: Retrospectives give agile team members a forum where they focus on discussing the plan and technical decisions for the next iteration

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The benefits of retrospectives include team bonding, learning from sharing issues, and better collaboration through reviewing and improving working practices. Calling out individuals who a team member feels did not fully contribute will not contribute to this team bonding and collaboration.
b) Is correct. During the retrospective, the group discusses what aspects of the project were successful and should be retained, as well as areas that could be improved, and how to do so.
c) Is not correct. The benefits of retrospectives are based on increased effectiveness and efficiency through process improvements; they are not an opportunity to let off steam and criticize management and customers. Also, the results are recorded, usually in the test completion report, so anything said could be read by other stakeholders.
d) Is not correct. Retrospectives are typically held at the end of an iteration and focus on quality-related issues that occurred in the current iteration. They are not used for making plans or technical decisions for the next iteration; this is done in the iteration planning meeting.

stem:
Which of the following questions is typically discussed in a retrospective?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Which team member caused the largest number of defects in this iteration?
options.b: What was not successful and could be improved in our way of working?
options.c: Which features should the customer add to the product backlog for the next release?
options.d: What is the remaining test effort, calculated with the three-point technique?

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Retrospectives focus on process improvement, not on blaming or evaluating individuals.
b) Is correct. Retrospectives discuss what was successful, what was not and could be improved, and how to incorporate improvements.
c) Is not correct. Adding features to the backlog is product planning, not the purpose of a retrospective.
d) Is not correct. Effort estimation is part of test planning, not of a retrospective.

stem:
In a retrospective, the team realizes that many defects were caused by vague acceptance criteria in user stories. The team agrees to hold short story refinement sessions with testers. Which benefit of retrospectives for testing does this BEST exemplify?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Team bonding and learning
options.b: Increased quality of testware through joint review of test processes
options.c: Improved quality of the test basis
options.d: Reduced need for confirmation testing

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Team bonding is a benefit but the scenario focuses on improving the requirements used as test basis.
b) Is not correct. The improvement concerns user stories (test basis), not testware such as test cases or scripts.
c) Is correct. Addressing deficiencies in the extent and quality of requirements improves the test basis, a listed benefit of retrospectives.
d) Is not correct. This is not one of the listed benefits of retrospectives.

stem:
Where are the results of retrospectives in a project NORMALLY recorded?

Select ONE option.

options.a: In the defect reports raised during the iteration
options.b: In the test plan of the next project
options.c: In the requirements specification
options.d: In the test completion report

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Defect reports document individual defects, not process improvement results.
b) Is not correct. Improvements may influence future plans, but results are normally recorded in the test completion report.
c) Is not correct. The requirements specification describes the product, not process lessons learned.
d) Is correct. Retrospective results should be recorded and are normally part of the test completion report.

stem:
Which types of failures (1-4) fit which test levels (A-D) BEST?

1. Failures in system behavior as it deviates from the user’s business needs
2. Failures in communication between components
3. Failures in logic in the code
4. Failures in not correctly implemented business rules

A. Component testing
B. Component integration testing
C. System testing
D. Acceptance testing
explanation: The test basis for acceptance testing is the user’s business needs (1D). Communication between components is tested during component integration testing (2B). Failures in logic can be found during component testing (3A). Business rules are the test basis for system testing (4C). Thus a) is correct.

stem: Which of the following is MOST likely to be performed as part of system testing?

options.a: Security testing of a credit management system by an independent test team
options.b: Testing the interface of a currency exchange system with an external banking system
options.c: Beta testing of a remote learning system by courseware developers
options.d: Testing interactions between the user interface and database of a human resources system

explanation:
a) Is correct. System testing examines the behavior and capabilities of the complete system and covers non-functional testing of quality characteristics, which includes security testing. It is often performed by an independent test team based on system specifications.
b) Is not correct. System integration testing examines the interfaces with other systems and external services.
c) Is not correct. Beta testing is a type of acceptance testing performed at an external site by roles outside the development organization.
d) Is not correct. Component integration testing involves testing the interfaces and interactions between components of a system, such as the user interface and database.

stem: Which of the following test levels is MOST likely being performed if the testing is focused on validation and is not being performed by testers?

options.a: Component testing
options.b: Component integration testing
options.c: System integration testing
options.d: Acceptance testing

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Component testing is mostly verification against a specification, rather than validation against user needs (although it is normally performed by developers rather than testers).
b) Is not correct. Component integration testing is mostly verification against a specification, rather than validation against user needs (although it is normally performed by developers).
c) Is not correct. System integration testing is mostly verification against a specification, and is most often performed by testers.
d) Is correct. Acceptance testing focuses on validating that the system meets the user's business needs and is ready for deployment. Ideally, this testing is carried out by the end users.

stem:
A developer of a parking-fee calculator writes tests for the fee-calculation module using a unit test framework and stubs replacing the payment module. Which test level is being performed?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Component testing
options.b: Component integration testing
options.c: System testing
options.d: System integration testing

explanation:
a) Is correct. Testing a single module in isolation with a unit test framework and stubs is component (unit) testing.
b) Is not correct. The payment module is replaced by a stub, so interactions between real components are not being tested.
c) Is not correct. System testing evaluates the behavior of the whole system, not a single isolated module.
d) Is not correct. System integration testing focuses on interfaces with other systems and external services.

stem:
Match the test levels (1-4) with the testing focus that BEST fits them (A-D).

1. Component integration testing
2. System testing
3. System integration testing
4. Acceptance testing

A. The interface between an online shop and an external payment provider
B. Validation that the delivered system meets the business needs of the warehouse staff
C. End-to-end processing of an order, including performance under expected load, in a representative test environment
D. The interaction between the shopping-cart component and the pricing component

Select ONE option.
explanation:
a) Is not correct. Swaps component integration and system integration; an external payment provider is another system (A belongs to 3).
b) Is correct. Component interactions = component integration (D); end-to-end and non-functional behavior of the whole system = system testing (C); external interface = system integration (A); validation of business needs = acceptance (B).
c) Is not correct. Swaps system and acceptance testing; validation of business needs by users is acceptance testing.
d) Is not correct. Component interactions (D) are component integration, not system testing.

stem:
A software vendor gives early versions of its photo-editing app to a group of selected customers who use it at their own premises and report problems before the official release. Which test level is this?

Select ONE option.

options.a: System testing performed by an independent test team
options.b: System integration testing
options.c: Acceptance testing (beta testing)
options.d: Component integration testing

explanation:
a) Is not correct. System testing is typically performed by testers in a test environment, not by customers at their own sites.
b) Is not correct. The focus is not on interfaces with other systems.
c) Is correct. Beta testing by potential users at their own locations is a form of acceptance testing.
d) Is not correct. Customers do not test interactions between individual components.

stem:
Which of the following attributes is used to distinguish test levels from each other?

Select ONE option.

options.a: The test technique used to derive the test cases
options.b: Whether the tests are functional or non-functional
options.c: Whether the tests are automated or executed manually
options.d: The specific test objectives, test basis and test object

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Techniques (black-box, white-box, experience-based) can be applied at every test level, so they do not distinguish levels.
b) Is not correct. Functional and non-functional test types can be performed at any test level.
c) Is not correct. Automation is possible at every test level and does not distinguish them.
d) Is correct. Test levels are characterized by test object, test objectives, test basis, defects and failures, and approach and responsibilities.

stem:
You work as a tester on a project on a mobile application for food ordering for one of your clients. The client sent you a list of requirements. One of them, with high priority, says
“The order must be processed in less than 10 seconds in 95% of the cases”.

You created a set of test cases in which a number of random orders were made, the processing time measured, and the test results were checked against the requirements.

What test type did you perform?

options.a: Functional, because the test cases cover the user’s business requirement for the system
options.b: Non-functional, because they measure the system’s performance
options.c: Functional, because the test cases interact with the user interface
options.d: White-box, because we need to know the internal structure of the program to measure the order processing time

explanation:
a) Is not correct. That the performance requirement comes from the client and is important from the business point of view does not make these tests functional: they check “how” (how fast orders are processed), not “what” the system does.
b) Is correct. This is an example of testing for performance efficiency, a type of non-functional testing.
c) Is not correct. We do not know if interacting with the UI is part of the test conditions; even if it were, the main test objective is to check performance, not usability.
d) Is not correct. Performance efficiency tests can be executed without structural knowledge of the code.

stem: Which of the following tests is MOST likely to be performed as part of functional testing?

options.a: The test checks that the sort function puts the elements of the list or array in ascending order
options.b: The test checks whether the sort function completes sorting within one second of starting
options.c: The test checks how easily the sort function can be changed from sorting ascending to sorting descending
options.d: The test checks that the sort function still functions correctly when moved from a 32-bit to a 64-bit architecture

explanation:
a) Is correct. Checking that the sort function puts the elements in ascending order is evaluating the functional correctness of the sort function, which is part of functional testing.
b) Is not correct. Assessing whether the sort function completes within one second is testing its performance efficiency, which is part of non-functional testing.
c) Is not correct. Evaluating the ease of modifying the sort function from ascending to descending is testing its modifiability, a form of maintainability testing, which is non-functional testing.
d) Is not correct. Assessing that the sort function still functions correctly when moved from a 32-bit to a 64-bit architecture is testing its adaptability, a form of portability testing, which is non-functional testing.

stem:
Which TWO of the following are examples of non-functional testing?

Select TWO options.

options.a: Checking that a booking for three nights calculates the correct total price
options.b: Checking that the hotel booking website still responds within 2 seconds when 5,000 users search simultaneously
options.c: Checking that a cancelled booking no longer appears in the customer's booking list
options.d: Checking that all decision outcomes in the discount-calculation code are exercised
options.e: Checking that the booking website can be used with assistive technologies such as screen readers

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Correctness of a calculation is functional correctness, part of functional testing.
b) Is correct. Response time under load is performance efficiency, a non-functional quality characteristic.
c) Is not correct. This checks what the system does, so it is functional testing.
d) Is not correct. Covering decision outcomes is white-box testing based on code structure, not non-functional testing.
e) Is correct. Accessibility belongs to usability, a non-functional quality characteristic.

stem:
Which statement about test types is CORRECT?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Functional, non-functional, black-box and white-box testing can all be applied at every test level
options.b: White-box testing can only be applied at the component test level because it requires access to the code
options.c: Non-functional testing should only start once functional testing has been completed at system level
options.d: Black-box testing is based on the internal structure and implementation of the test object

explanation:
a) Is correct. The syllabus states that all four test types can be applied to all test levels, with different focus.
b) Is not correct. White-box testing can be based on any structure (e.g., system architecture, menu structure), so it applies at all levels.
c) Is not correct. Non-functional testing can and should start early; it is not restricted to after system-level functional testing.
d) Is not correct. That describes white-box testing; black-box testing is specification-based.

stem:
You are testing a user story with three acceptance criteria: AC1, AC2 and AC3. AC1 is covered by test case TC1, AC2 by TC2, and AC3 by TC3. The test execution history had three test runs on three consecutive versions of the software as follows:

| | Execution 1 | Execution 2 | Execution 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC1 | (1) Failed | (4) Passed | (7) Passed |
| TC2 | (2) Passed | (5) Failed | (8) Passed |
| TC3 | (3) Failed | (6) Failed | (9) Passed |

Tests are repeated once you are informed that all defects found in the test run are corrected and a new version of the software is available.

Which of the above tests are executed as regression tests?

options.b: Only 5, 7
options.d: Only 5, 6

explanation: Because TC1 and TC3 failed in Execution 1 (tests (1) and (3)), tests (4) and (6) are confirmation tests. Because TC2 and TC3 failed in Execution 2 (tests (5) and (6)), tests (8) and (9) are also confirmation tests. TC2 passed in Execution 1 (test (2)), so test (5) is a regression test. TC1 passed in Execution 2 (test (4)), so test (7) is also a regression test. Thus b) is correct.

stem: Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

options.a: Regression tests increase in number as the project progresses, whereas the number of confirmation tests decreases as the project progresses
options.b: Regression tests are created and run when the test object is fixed, whereas confirmation tests are run whenever the test object is enhanced
options.c: Regression testing is concerned with checking that the operational environment remains unchanged, whereas confirmation testing is concerned with testing changes to the test object
options.d: Regression testing is concerned with adverse effects in unchanged code, whereas confirmation testing is concerned with testing changed code

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Regression tests increase in number as the project progresses, but the number of confirmation tests also typically increases, as new confirmation tests are needed for each fix.
b) Is not correct. It is the other way round: confirmation tests are created and run when the test object is fixed, and regression tests are (ideally) run whenever the test object is enhanced (changed).
c) Is not correct. Confirmation testing is concerned with testing changes to the test object, but regression testing ensures that changes (including changes to the operational environment) do not have negative effects on unchanged software; it does not check that the operational environment remains unchanged.
d) Is correct. Regression testing ensures that changes do not have negative effects on unchanged software. Confirmation testing verifies that a defect has been fixed, and so is concerned with changed code.

stem: The navigation system software has been updated due to it suggesting routes that break traffic laws, such as driving the wrong way down one-way streets. Which of the following BEST describes the testing that will be performed?

options.a: Only confirmation testing
options.b: Confirmation testing then regression testing
options.c: Only regression testing
options.d: Regression testing then confirmation testing

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Confirmation testing is necessary, however it would then be sensible to perform regression testing to ensure that no defects have been introduced or uncovered in unchanged areas of the system.
b) Is correct. Confirmation testing will check that the updates have resulted in a correct implementation, and then regression testing will be used to ensure that no defects have been introduced or uncovered in unchanged areas of the system.
c) Is not correct. Regression testing is needed, but it is also necessary to perform confirmation testing to check that the updates have resulted in a correct implementation.
d) Is not correct. Both are needed, but confirmation testing precedes regression testing.

stem:
A defect in the tax calculation of a payroll system was fixed. The tester re-executes the test case that previously failed, and it now passes. What type of testing has been performed?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Regression testing
options.b: Confirmation testing
options.c: Maintenance testing triggered by retirement
options.d: Acceptance testing

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Regression testing checks that the change has not caused adverse effects elsewhere, not that the fix itself works.
b) Is correct. Re-executing the previously failing test to check that the defect has been fixed is confirmation testing.
c) Is not correct. Retirement of a system is not involved here.
d) Is not correct. Acceptance testing validates readiness for deployment; it is not specifically about confirming a fix.

stem:
Which of the following statements about regression testing is CORRECT?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Regression testing is performed only on the component that was changed
options.b: Regression test suites are poor candidates for automation because they change after every release
options.c: Impact analysis is recommended to optimize the extent of regression testing
options.d: Regression testing is only needed when a defect has been fixed, not after a new feature is added

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Regression testing checks that the change did not adversely affect other parts, including connected systems and the environment.
b) Is not correct. Regression suites are run many times and change slowly, so they are strong candidates for automation.
c) Is correct. Impact analysis helps identify which parts of the software might be affected and thus which regression tests are needed.
d) Is not correct. Any change (fixes, new features, environment changes) can introduce regressions.

stem:
Consider the following statements:

i. Confirmation testing may be restricted to repeating the steps that reproduced the failure when time is short.
ii. Regression testing aims to confirm that the original defect has been successfully fixed.
iii. Regression testing may also need to cover the test environment, not only the test object.
iv. Confirmation testing is a strong candidate for automation because it is repeated in every iteration.

Which statements are TRUE?

Select ONE option.

options.a: i and ii
options.b: ii and iv
options.c: iii and iv
options.d: i and iii

explanation:
a) Is not correct. ii is false: confirming that the defect was fixed is the purpose of confirmation testing, not regression testing.
b) Is not correct. Both are false: ii describes confirmation testing; iv describes regression testing, which is the strong automation candidate.
c) Is not correct. iv is false: regression testing, not confirmation testing, is repeated many times and suits automation.
d) Is correct. Confirmation testing can be limited to reproducing the failure steps (i), and adverse effects may also affect the environment, so regression testing may cover it (iii).

stem:
In a team using continuous integration, a developer changes the date-formatting library used by several modules. What is the BEST testing response?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Run the automated regression tests in the CI pipeline to detect unintended side effects in the modules using the library
options.b: Run only confirmation tests, because no defect has been reported
options.c: Skip testing, because a library change is a technical change without business impact
options.d: Re-execute only the tests of the date-formatting library itself

explanation:
a) Is correct. A shared change can cause regressions in other modules; including automated regression tests in CI is good practice.
b) Is not correct. Confirmation testing requires a fixed defect; here the risk is regression across modules.
c) Is not correct. Library changes can break dependent functionality; skipping testing is risky.
d) Is not correct. This ignores the modules that use the library, where regressions are likely.

stem: Your organization’s test strategy suggests that once a system is going to be retired, data migration shall be tested. As part of what test type is this testing MOST likely to be performed?

options.a: Maintenance testing
options.b: Regression testing
options.c: Reliability testing
options.d: Integration testing

explanation:
a) Is correct. When a system is retired, this can require testing of data migration, which is a form of maintenance testing.
b) Is not correct. Regression testing verifies whether a fix accidentally affected the behavior of other parts of the code; here we are talking about data migration.
c) Is not correct. (Official rationale: portability testing focuses on transferring the system to another environment — not data migration on retirement.)
d) Is not correct. Integration testing focuses on interactions between components and/or systems, not on data migration. Also, it is a test level, not a test type.

stem: Which of the following is MOST likely to be a trigger that leads to maintenance testing of a currency exchange system?

options.a: The developers reported that changing the currency exchange system was difficult and the testers decided to check if this was true
options.b: The refund option of the currency exchange system was removed as it did not always repay the correct amount to customers
options.c: The agile team has started developing a user story that adds a new customer loyalty feature to the currency exchange system
options.d: The language support option of the currency exchange system was used to enable both English and local language currency transactions

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Checking the ease of changing the system would be done by maintainability testing rather than maintenance testing, so this is not a trigger for maintenance testing.
b) Is correct. A system modification (such as a fix or enhancement) is a trigger for maintenance testing. The removal of the refund option was a fix that would lead to maintenance testing.
c) Is not correct. Developing a user story that adds a new customer loyalty feature will result in testing the new feature and then regression testing. No maintenance testing is required in this situation.
d) Is not correct. Reconfiguration of the system to support both local language and English currency transactions is not a system modification, a change to the operational environment, or a system retirement, which are the three triggers for maintenance testing.

stem:
Which of the following is a trigger for maintenance testing?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Developing the first version of a new mobile app
options.b: Migrating an operational system's database to a new database management system
options.c: Conducting a retrospective at the end of an iteration
options.d: Writing user stories for a product that has not yet been released

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Maintenance testing concerns systems already in operation, not first-time development.
b) Is correct. Upgrades or migrations of the operational environment trigger maintenance testing, possibly including data conversion tests.
c) Is not correct. Retrospectives are process-improvement meetings, not triggers for testing a changed system.
d) Is not correct. Maintenance testing applies to operational systems; this is new development.

stem:
Consider the following situations for a library-management system that is in production:

i. A hot fix is applied to correct a fine-calculation failure
ii. The system is retired and its data must be archived for ten years
iii. A tester performs exploratory testing on a prototype of a new, unrelated app
iv. The server operating system is upgraded to a new major version

Which situations trigger maintenance testing of the library-management system?

Select ONE option.

options.a: i and iii only
options.b: ii, iii and iv
options.c: i, ii and iv
options.d: i and iv only

explanation:
a) Is not correct. iii concerns a new, unrelated app, so it is not maintenance testing; ii and iv are missing.
b) Is not correct. iii is not related to maintenance of the operational system, and i is missing.
c) Is correct. Modifications (hot fix), retirement (data archiving) and environment upgrades are all maintenance testing triggers.
d) Is not correct. Retirement (ii) is also a trigger, requiring testing of data archiving and retrieval.

stem:
The following is a list of the work products produced in the SDLC.

i. Business requirements
ii. Schedule
iii. Test budget
iv. Third-party executable code
v. User stories and their acceptance criteria

Which of them can be reviewed?

options.a: i and iv can be reviewed
options.b: i, ii, iii and iv can be reviewed
options.c: i, ii, iii, and v can be reviewed
options.d: iii, iv, v can be reviewed

explanation: Only third-party executable code cannot be reviewed. Thus c) is correct.

stem: Which of the following CANNOT be examined by static testing?

options.a: Contract
options.b: Test plan
options.c: Encrypted code
options.d: Test charter

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Most work products can be examined using some form of static testing, and a contract must be interpretable by humans and so could be reviewed, which is a form of static testing.
b) Is not correct. A test plan must be interpretable by humans and so could be reviewed, which is a form of static testing.
c) Is correct. Static testing is not suitable for work products that are too complex for human interpretation and should not be analyzed by tools; encrypted code is too complex for humans and, if properly encrypted, will not be analyzable by most tools.
d) Is not correct. A test charter must be interpretable by humans and so could be reviewed, which is a form of static testing.

stem:
Which of the following work products can be examined by static testing?

Select ONE option.

options.a: The response time of a web page measured under load
options.b: The memory consumption of a running application
options.c: The behavior of a deployed system when the network fails
options.d: A test charter for an exploratory testing session

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Response time can only be evaluated by executing the software (dynamic testing).
b) Is not correct. Memory consumption at runtime requires execution of the software.
c) Is not correct. Observing runtime behavior under failure conditions is dynamic testing.
d) Is correct. Almost any work product that can be read and understood can be examined statically, including test charters.

stem:
Consider the following work products:

i. Product backlog items
ii. Contracts
iii. Third-party executable code that may not be analyzed for legal reasons
iv. Architecture models
v. Test plans

Which are appropriate for static testing?

Select ONE option.

options.a: i, ii, iv and v
options.b: i, ii, iii and iv
options.c: ii, iii, iv and v
options.d: i, iii, iv and v

explanation:
a) Is correct. Backlog items, contracts, models and test plans can all be read and examined; third-party executable code that may not be analyzed for legal reasons is not appropriate.
b) Is not correct. iii is the example given of a work product not appropriate for static testing.
c) Is not correct. iii is not appropriate for static testing, and i is missing.
d) Is not correct. iii is not appropriate, and contracts (ii) can be reviewed.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of static testing?

options.a: Having less expensive defect management due to the ease of detecting defects later in the SDLC
options.b: Fixing defects found during static testing is generally much less expensive than fixing defects found during dynamic testing
options.c: Finding coding defects that might not have been found by only performing dynamic testing
options.d: Detecting gaps and inconsistencies in requirements

explanation:
a) Is correct. Defect management is no less expensive. Finding and fixing defects later in the SDLC is more costly.
b) Is not correct. This is a benefit of static testing.
c) Is not correct. This is a benefit of static testing.
d) Is not correct. This is a benefit of static testing.

stem: Which of the following statements about the value of static testing is CORRECT?

options.a: The defect types found by static testing are different from the defect types that can be found by dynamic testing
options.b: Dynamic testing can detect the defect types that can be found by static testing plus some additional defect types
options.c: Dynamic testing can identify some of the defects that can be found by static testing but not all of them
options.d: Static testing can identify the defect types that can be found by dynamic testing as well as some extra defect types

explanation:
Some defect types can only be detected by static testing, such as unreachable code, design patterns not implemented as desired and defects in non-executable work products. Some defect types can be found by both static and dynamic testing, such as a programming defect that can be observed by a reviewer in a code review and which causes an observable failure during dynamic testing. And some defect types can only be detected by dynamic testing, such as performance issues or memory issues that can only be observed when executing the code or system.
Thus:
a) Is not correct.
b) Is not correct.
c) Is correct.
d) Is not correct.

stem:
Which of the following BEST explains why static testing can find defects that dynamic testing cannot?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Static testing always finds more defects than dynamic testing because it is performed earlier
options.b: Static testing can find defects in non-executable work products and in code that is unreachable at runtime
options.c: Static testing executes the code with more test data than dynamic testing
options.d: Static testing measures performance efficiency more accurately than dynamic testing

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Static testing complements dynamic testing; it does not always find more defects.
b) Is correct. Defects in non-executable work products and unreachable code cannot be found by executing the software.
c) Is not correct. Static testing does not execute the code at all.
d) Is not correct. Performance efficiency depends on execution and is measured by dynamic testing.

stem:
A project manager argues that reviews are too expensive and should be dropped. Which argument BEST describes the value of static testing?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Reviews cost nothing because they do not require any test environment
options.b: Reviews replace dynamic testing, so the system test budget can be removed
