options.c: Although reviews cost effort, they detect defects early, which typically lowers overall project costs because fixing those defects later would be more expensive
options.d: Reviews guarantee that the requirements are complete, so no changes will be needed later

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Reviews require effort and time from participants; they are not free.
b) Is not correct. Static and dynamic testing complement each other; neither replaces the other.
c) Is correct. Static testing has implementation costs, but defects found early are cheaper to fix, so overall costs are usually lower.
d) Is not correct. No review technique can guarantee completeness; testing can show presence of defects, not their absence.

stem:
Decide which of the following statements (i-v) are true for static testing.

i. Abnormal external behaviors are easier to identify with this testing
ii. Discrepancies from a coding standard are easier to find with this testing
iii. It identifies failures caused by defects when the software is run
iv. Its test objective is to identify defects as early as possible
v. Missing coverage for critical security requirements is easier to find and fix

options.a: i, iv, v are true for static testing
options.b: i, iii, iv are true for static testing
options.c: ii, iii are true for static testing
options.d: ii, iv, v are true for static testing

explanation:
i. Abnormal behaviors are easily detectable while the software is running; dynamic testing should be used to identify them.
ii. Deviations from standards are a typical defect that is easier found with static testing.
iii. If the software is executed during the test, it is dynamic testing.
iv. Identifying defects as early as possible is the test objective of both static testing and dynamic testing.
v. This is an example of gaps in test basis traceability or coverage, a typical defect easier found with static testing.
Thus d) is correct.

stem: Which of the following is an example of a defect that can be found by static testing but NOT by dynamic testing?

options.a: Lack of usability provided through the user interface
options.b: Code with no path that reaches it
options.c: Poor response times for most of the expected users
options.d: Required features that are not implemented in the code

explanation:
a) Is not correct. A lack of usability can be detected through a review using a suitable checklist, but it can also be identified by getting several typical users to dynamically test the user interface.
b) Is correct. A code review can detect code that cannot be reached by any path, whereas dynamic tests can only exercise reachable code and cannot determine that code is unreachable without running every possible combination of inputs and states, which is impractical.
c) Is not correct. Poor response times are difficult to determine without executing the code, so dynamic testing could find this defect, but static testing is unlikely to.
d) Is not correct. A review of the code by someone aware of the required features could detect that they were not implemented, and dynamic testing could also determine this.

stem:
Given the following example defects:
i. Two different parts of the design specification disagree due to the complexity of the design
ii. A response time is too long and so makes users lose patience
iii. A path in the code cannot be reached during execution
iv. A variable is declared but never subsequently used in the program
v. The amount of memory needed by the program to generate a report is too high

Which of the following BEST identifies example defects that could be found by static testing (rather than dynamic testing)?

options.a: ii, v
options.b: iii, v
options.c: i, ii, iv
options.d: i, iii, iv

explanation:
i. A specification defect (inconsistencies, ambiguities, contradictions, omissions, inaccuracies, duplications) - most easily found by static testing.
ii. A response time defect - can only be detected in practice by executing the program and measuring the response time - dynamic testing.
iii. A coding defect (unreachable code) - most easily found by static testing.
iv. A coding defect (variable declared but never used) - most easily found by static testing.
v. A performance defect - can only be detected in practice by executing the program and measuring the memory used - dynamic testing.
Thus: d) Is correct (i, iii, iv). a), b), c) Are not correct.

stem:
Which statement CORRECTLY compares static testing and dynamic testing?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Static testing can only be applied to source code, whereas dynamic testing can be applied to any work product
options.b: Dynamic testing is better suited to measuring maintainability, whereas static testing is better suited to measuring performance efficiency
options.c: Static and dynamic testing have different objectives: only dynamic testing aims to detect defects
options.d: Static testing finds defects directly, whereas dynamic testing causes failures from which the associated defects are determined through subsequent analysis

explanation:
a) Is not correct. It is the other way round: static testing applies to non-executable work products too, dynamic testing only to executable ones.
b) Is not correct. Reversed: maintainability is measured statically, performance efficiency dynamically.
c) Is not correct. Both static and dynamic testing aim to detect defects and evaluate quality.
d) Is correct. This is a key difference described in the syllabus.

stem:
Which TWO of the following defects are typically easier and cheaper to find by static testing than by dynamic testing?

Select TWO options.

options.a: A variable that is used before a value has been assigned to it
options.b: A memory leak that only appears after the system has run for several days
options.c: A slow response time when many users access the database at the same time
options.d: A function called with its parameters in the wrong order according to the interface specification
options.e: A failure caused by an incompatible browser version

explanation:
a) Is correct. Variables with undefined values are a typical coding defect found by static analysis.
b) Is not correct. Memory leaks over long runs show up as failures during execution (e.g., reliability testing).
c) Is not correct. Performance problems under load are found by dynamic (performance) testing.
d) Is correct. Incorrect interface specifications/mismatched parameter order are typically found by static testing.
e) Is not correct. Compatibility problems manifest when executing the software in the target environment.

stem:
During a code review, a reviewer notices that a branch of an error-handling routine can only be reached when two rare hardware faults occur at the same time. Why is static testing particularly useful here?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Static testing can more easily detect defects in code paths that are rarely executed or hard to reach with dynamic testing
options.b: Static testing can measure the execution time of the error-handling routine
options.c: Static testing automatically generates the hardware faults needed to execute the branch
options.d: Static testing ensures that the error-handling routine passes all dynamic tests

explanation:
a) Is correct. The syllabus notes that static testing may more easily detect defects on paths that are rarely executed or hard to reach.
b) Is not correct. Execution time requires running the code.
c) Is not correct. Static testing does not execute code or generate runtime conditions.
d) Is not correct. Static testing cannot ensure dynamic test outcomes; the two are complementary.

stem: Which of the following is a benefit of early and frequent feedback?

options.a: It improves the test process for future projects
options.b: It forces customers to prioritize their requirements based on agreed risks
options.c: It provides a measure for the quality of changes
options.d: It helps avoid requirements misunderstandings

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Feedback can improve the test process, but if one only wants to improve future projects, the feedback does not need to come early or frequently.
b) Is not correct. Feedback is not used to prioritize requirements.
c) Is not correct. There is no one recommended way to measure quality of changes. Also, this is not one of the benefits of early feedback mentioned in syllabus section 3.2.1.
d) Is correct. Early and frequent feedback can prevent misunderstandings about requirements.

stem: Which of the following is a benefit of early and frequent stakeholder feedback?

options.a: Managers are aware of which developers are less productive
options.b: It allows project managers to prioritize their stakeholder interactions
options.c: It facilitates early communication of potential quality issues
options.d: End users better understand why the delivery of the work product is delayed

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The feedback is from stakeholders (e.g., business representatives and end users), not about developers, so it is not likely to inform managers which developers are more or less productive.
b) Is not correct. Early and frequent stakeholder feedback is not used by project managers to prioritize how they interact with stakeholders.
c) Is correct. Early and frequent stakeholder feedback facilitates early communication of potential quality issues, can prevent misunderstandings about requirements, and ensures that changes in stakeholder requirements are understood and implemented sooner.
d) Is not correct. Early and frequent feedback can prevent costly rework and missed deadlines, so ideally there should be no delay. Also, the feedback is from stakeholders (not to them), so end users providing feedback will not aid their own understanding.

stem: Which of the following is a benefit of early and frequent stakeholder feedback?

options.a: Changes to requirements are understood and implemented earlier
options.b: It ensures business stakeholders understand user requirements
options.c: It allows product owners to change their requirements as often as they want
options.d: End users are told which requirements will not be implemented prior to release

explanation:
a) Is correct. Early and frequent feedback from stakeholders facilitates early communication of potential quality issues, can prevent misunderstandings about requirements, and ensures that any changes in stakeholder requirements are understood and implemented sooner.
b) Is not correct. The feedback is from stakeholders, so providing feedback is unlikely to improve their understanding of their own user requirements.
c) Is not correct. Because changes in requirements can be understood and implemented sooner, it does not mean that unlimited changes to requirements are encouraged.
d) Is not correct. The feedback is from stakeholders and does not cover communication to them. Telling end users which requirements will not be implemented prior to release should ideally not happen at all.

stem:
Which of the following is a benefit of early and frequent stakeholder feedback?

Select ONE option.

options.a: The need for regression testing is eliminated
options.b: Potential quality problems are communicated early
options.c: Stakeholders no longer need to prioritize requirements
options.d: The test plan can be finalized before the project starts

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Feedback does not remove the need for regression testing.
b) Is correct. Early and frequent feedback allows early communication of potential quality problems.
c) Is not correct. Feedback helps focus on valuable features, it does not remove prioritization.
d) Is not correct. Feedback is about the product under development, not about freezing the test plan.

stem:
What is a likely consequence when stakeholders do NOT provide feedback during development?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Higher test coverage of the requirements
options.b: Fewer defects in the requirements
options.c: Costly rework, missed deadlines and possible project failure
options.d: Faster delivery of the features with the most value

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Lack of feedback does not increase coverage.
b) Is not correct. Without feedback, misunderstandings in requirements are more likely, not less.
c) Is correct. Lack of frequent feedback can lead to costly rework, missed deadlines, blame games and even project failure.
d) Is not correct. Feedback is what helps the team focus on the most valuable features.

stem:
A product owner shows a working increment to business users every week and collects their comments. Which benefit of early and frequent stakeholder feedback is this practice MOST likely to bring?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Test effort can be estimated with greater accuracy using the ratio-based technique
options.b: Developers no longer need to perform component testing
options.c: The independence of testing is increased
options.d: Changes in stakeholders' understanding of their needs are implemented sooner

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Estimation techniques are unrelated to stakeholder feedback.
b) Is not correct. Feedback does not replace component testing.
c) Is not correct. Independence of testing is not a benefit of stakeholder feedback.
d) Is correct. Frequent feedback ensures that changes in stakeholder understanding are reflected sooner.

stem:
Which statement BEST describes how early and frequent stakeholder feedback helps a development team?

Select ONE option.

options.a: It helps the team focus on the features that deliver the most value to stakeholders and have the most positive impact on identified risks
options.b: It guarantees that no defects will remain in the delivered product
options.c: It allows stakeholders to take over the tester's role in system testing
options.d: It removes the need to document acceptance criteria

explanation:
a) Is correct. This is one of the listed benefits of early and frequent feedback.
b) Is not correct. No activity can guarantee absence of defects.
c) Is not correct. Feedback does not replace testers or system testing.
d) Is not correct. Acceptance criteria are still needed; feedback complements them.

stem: Which of the following statements about formal reviews is TRUE?

options.a: Some reviews do not require more than one role
options.b: The review process has several activities
options.c: Documentation to be reviewed is not distributed before the review meeting, with the exception of the work product for specific review types
options.d: Defects found during the review are not reported since they are not found by dynamic testing

explanation:
a) Is not correct. In all types of reviews there is more than one role, even in informal ones.
b) Is correct. There are several activities during the formal review process.
c) Is not correct. Documentation to be reviewed should be distributed as early as possible.
d) Is not correct. Defects found during the review should be reported.

stem:
Given the following task descriptions:

1. The quality characteristics to be evaluated and the exit criteria are selected
2. Everyone has access to the work product
3. Anomalies are identified in the work product
4. Anomalies are discussed

And the following review activities:

A. Individual review
B. Review initiation
C. Planning
D. Communication and analysis

Which of the following BEST matches the task descriptions and activities?
explanation:
1. Quality characteristics and exit criteria selected – Planning (C): defining the review scope, purpose, work product, quality characteristics to be evaluated, areas of focus, exit criteria, supporting information, effort and timeframes.
2. Everyone has access to the work product – Review initiation (B): ensuring all participants have access to the work product and necessary resources, and clarifying roles and responsibilities.
3. Anomalies are identified – Individual review (A): evaluating the work product's quality, identifying and logging anomalies, recommendations and questions using review techniques such as checklist-based and scenario-based reviewing.
4. Anomalies are (analyzed and) discussed – Communication and analysis (D): analyzing and discussing each anomaly, determining its status, ownership and required actions, and making review decisions, normally in a meeting.
Thus a), b), c) are not correct; d) is correct: 1C, 2B, 3A, 4D.

stem:
Given the following descriptions of review activities:

1. Detected anomalies are deliberated upon, and determinations are reached regarding their status, ownership, and any further steps needed
2. Defects are recorded, and any needed updates are addressed prior to the acceptance of the work product
3. Reviewers employ techniques to come up with suggestions and questions about the work product and to spot anomalies
4. The objective of the review and its schedule are established to ensure a focused and efficient review
5. Participants are provided with access to the item being reviewed

Which of the following is the CORRECT sequence in the review process of the activities that correspond to the descriptions?
explanation:
1. Part of the 'communication and analysis' activity.
2. Part of the 'fixing and reporting' activity.
3. Part of the 'individual review' activity.
4. Part of the 'planning' activity.
5. Part of the 'review initiation' activity.
The generic review process from ISO/IEC 20246 comprises, in this logical order: Planning (4), Review initiation (5), Individual review (3), Communication and analysis (1), Fixing and reporting (2).
Thus:
a) Is not correct.
b) Is correct. The correct sequence of activities is: 4 – 5 – 3 – 1 – 2.
c) Is not correct.
d) Is not correct.

stem:
In which activity of the review process are the purpose of the review, the work product to be reviewed, the quality characteristics to be evaluated and the exit criteria defined?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Review initiation
options.b: Planning
options.c: Individual review
options.d: Communication and analysis

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Review initiation makes sure everyone is prepared (access to the work product, roles understood), not defining the scope.
b) Is correct. During planning, the scope of the review is defined: purpose, work product, quality characteristics, focus areas, exit criteria, effort and timeframes.
c) Is not correct. In individual review, reviewers assess the work product and log anomalies.
d) Is not correct. This activity analyzes and discusses identified anomalies.

stem:
Consider the following review activities:

i. Fixing and reporting
ii. Individual review
iii. Planning
iv. Communication and analysis
v. Review initiation

Which sequence shows the activities in the order defined by the generic review process?

Select ONE option.

options.a: iii, ii, v, iv, i
options.b: v, iii, ii, i, iv
options.c: iii, v, ii, iv, i
options.d: iii, v, iv, ii, i

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Review initiation comes before individual review, so that reviewers are ready.
b) Is not correct. Planning comes first, and communication and analysis precedes fixing and reporting.
c) Is correct. The generic order is planning, review initiation, individual review, communication and analysis, fixing and reporting.
d) Is not correct. Anomalies must be found in individual review before they can be communicated and analyzed.

stem: What task may management take on during a formal review?

options.a: Taking overall responsibility for the review
options.b: Deciding what is to be reviewed
options.c: Ensuring the effective running of review meetings, and moderating, if necessary
options.d: Recording review information such as review decisions

explanation:
a) Is not correct. This is the task of the review leader.
b) Is correct. This is the task of management in a formal review.
c) Is not correct. This is the task of the moderator.
d) Is not correct. This is the task of the scribe.

stem:
Given the following roles in reviews:

1. Scribe
2. Review leader
3. Facilitator
4. Manager

And the following responsibilities in reviews:

A. Ensures the effective running of review meetings and the setting up a safe review environment
B. Records review information, such as decisions and new anomalies found during the review meeting
C. Decides what is to be reviewed and provides resources, such as staff and time for the review
D. Takes overall responsibility for the review such as organizing when and where the review will take place

Which of the following BEST matches the roles and responsibilities?
explanation:
1. Scribe (recorder) – gathers feedback and documents review information such as decisions and new anomalies found during the review meeting (B).
2. Review leader – oversees the review process, e.g., selecting the review team, scheduling review meetings and ensuring the review is completed successfully; takes overall responsibility (D).
3. Facilitator (moderator) – ensures review meetings run effectively (managing time, mediating discussions) and creates a safe environment where everyone can voice their opinions (A).
4. Manager – decides what is to be reviewed and allocates resources such as staff and time (C).
Thus a), b), d) are not correct; c) is correct: 1B, 2D, 3A, 4C.

stem: Which participant in the review process is responsible for ensuring that the review meetings run effectively and that everyone at the meetings can voice their opinions freely?

options.a: Manager
options.b: Moderator
options.c: Chairperson
options.d: Review Leader

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The manager is responsible for deciding what needs to be reviewed and allocating resources, such as staff and time, for the review.
b) Is correct. The moderator (or facilitator) is responsible for ensuring that the review meetings run effectively, including managing time, mediating discussions, and creating a safe environment where everyone can voice their opinions freely.
c) Is not correct. The chairperson is not a recognized role in reviews.
d) Is not correct. The review leader is responsible for overseeing the review process, such as selecting the review team members, scheduling review meetings, and ensuring that the review is completed successfully.

stem:
Which review role is responsible for creating the work product under review and fixing it afterwards?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Scribe
options.b: Review leader
options.c: Moderator
options.d: Author

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The scribe collates anomalies and records review information.
b) Is not correct. The review leader takes overall responsibility for the review, e.g., who is involved, when and where.
c) Is not correct. The moderator ensures effective running of review meetings.
d) Is correct. The author creates and fixes the work product under review.

stem:
Which review role decides who will be involved in a review and organizes when and where it will take place?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Review leader
options.b: Manager
options.c: Scribe
options.d: Author

explanation:
a) Is correct. The review leader takes overall responsibility, including deciding who is involved and organizing when and where.
b) Is not correct. The manager decides what is to be reviewed and provides resources such as staff and time.
c) Is not correct. The scribe records anomalies and review decisions.
d) Is not correct. The author creates and fixes the work product.

stem:
The reviews being used in your organization have the following attributes:

• There is the role of a scribe
• The main purpose is to evaluate quality
• The meeting is led by the author of the work product
• There is individual preparation
• A review report is produced

Which of the following review types is MOST likely being used?

options.a: Informal review
options.b: Walkthrough
options.c: Technical review
options.d: Inspection

explanation:
Considering the attributes:
• A scribe is specified for walkthroughs, technical reviews, and inspections; thus, the reviews being performed cannot be informal reviews.
• Evaluating quality is one of the most important objectives of a walkthrough.
• The author leading the meeting is not allowed for inspections and is typically not done in technical reviews; it is allowed in walkthroughs and informal reviews.
• All types of reviews can include individual preparation (even informal reviews).
• All types of reviews can produce a review report, although informal reviews do not require documentation.
Thus b) Walkthrough is correct.

stem:
Given the following review types:
1. Technical review
2. Informal review
3. Inspection
4. Walkthrough

And the following descriptions:
A. Includes objectives such as gaining consensus, generating new ideas, and motivating authors to improve
B. Includes objectives such as educating reviewers, gaining consensus, generating new ideas and detecting potential defects
C. The main objective is detecting potential defects and it requires metrics collection to support process improvement
D. The main objective is detecting potential defects and it generates no formal documented output

Which of the following BEST matches the review types and the descriptions?
explanation:
1. Technical review - performed by technically qualified reviewers and led by a moderator. Objectives are to gain consensus and make decisions on technical problems, while also evaluating quality and building confidence, generating new ideas, motivating and enabling authors to improve, and detecting anomalies (A).
2. Informal review - the main objective is to detect anomalies. The process is not defined and does not require formal documented output (D).
3. Inspection - the most formal review type, following the complete generic review process. The primary objective is to find the most anomalies; other objectives include collecting metrics that can be used to enhance the SDLC, including the inspection process (C).
4. Walkthrough - led by the author; objectives include evaluating quality, educating reviewers, gaining consensus, generating new ideas, motivating and enabling authors to improve, and detecting anomalies (B).
Thus: b) Is correct (1A, 2D, 3C, 4B). a), c), d) Are not correct.

stem:
A team uses a review type with the following characteristics: it follows the complete generic review process, the author may not act as review leader or scribe, metrics are collected to improve the SDLC, and the main objective is to find the maximum number of anomalies. Which review type is this?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Technical review
options.b: Inspection
options.c: Walkthrough
options.d: Informal review

explanation:
a) Is not correct. A technical review is led by a moderator and mainly aims at consensus and decisions on technical problems.
b) Is correct. These are the defining characteristics of an inspection, the most formal review type.
c) Is not correct. A walkthrough is led by the author, which is not allowed here.
d) Is not correct. An informal review does not follow a defined process and has no formal documented output.

stem:
Match the review types (1-4) with their descriptions (A-D).

1. Informal review
2. Walkthrough
3. Technical review
4. Inspection

A. Led by the author; objectives include educating reviewers and gaining consensus
B. Performed by technically qualified reviewers and led by a moderator; aims to make decisions about a technical problem
C. Does not follow a defined process and does not require a formal documented output
D. Most formal type; main objective is to find the maximum number of anomalies

Select ONE option.
explanation:
a) Is not correct. Swaps walkthrough and technical review; walkthroughs are led by the author.
b) Is not correct. Swaps informal review and walkthrough; informal reviews have no defined process.
c) Is correct. Informal = no defined process (C); walkthrough = author-led, education/consensus (A); technical review = qualified reviewers led by moderator (B); inspection = most formal (D).
d) Is not correct. Swaps technical review and inspection; the inspection is the most formal type.

stem:
A senior architect wants to present a new design to junior developers so that they learn about it and so that the team agrees on the approach. Preparation by reviewers before the meeting is optional. Which review type is MOST appropriate?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Inspection
options.b: Technical review
options.c: Informal review
options.d: Walkthrough

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Inspections are formal, require individual preparation and aim to find the maximum number of anomalies.
b) Is not correct. Technical reviews are performed by technically qualified reviewers led by a moderator, not mainly for educating juniors.
c) Is not correct. Informal reviews mainly aim at detecting anomalies; education and consensus are walkthrough objectives.
d) Is correct. Walkthroughs are led by the author and have objectives such as educating reviewers and gaining consensus; individual preparation is optional.

stem: Which of these statements is NOT a factor that contributes to successful reviews?

options.a: Participants should dedicate adequate time for the review
options.b: Splitting large work products into small parts to make the required effort less intense
options.c: Participants should avoid behaviors that might indicate boredom, exasperation, or hostility to other participants
options.d: Failures found should be acknowledged, appreciated, and handled objectively

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Adequate time for individuals is a success factor.
b) Is not correct. Splitting work products into small adequate parts is a success factor.
c) Is not correct. Avoiding behaviors that might indicate boredom, exasperation, etc. is a success factor.
d) Is correct. During reviews one can find defects, not failures.

stem: Which of the following is a factor that contributes to a successful review?

options.a: Ensure management participate as reviewers
options.b: Split large work products into smaller parts
options.c: Set reviewer evaluation as an objective
options.d: Plan to cover one document per review

explanation:
a) Is not correct. It is important to secure management's support for the review process, but that does not mean that they should participate as reviewers.
b) Is correct. It is important to break the work product into parts that are small enough to be reviewed in a reasonable timescale to prevent reviewers from losing focus during individual reviews or review meetings.
c) Is not correct. It is important to clearly define objectives and measurable exit criteria, without evaluating participants.
d) Is not correct. The review should be broken down into smaller chunks to prevent reviewers from losing focus, so you should not plan to cover one document per review.

stem:
Which of the following is a factor that contributes to a successful review?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Conducting reviews on small chunks so that reviewers do not lose concentration
options.b: Using the review findings to evaluate the performance of the author
options.c: Reviewing the whole document in a single long meeting to save time
options.d: Limiting training to the review leader only

explanation:
a) Is correct. Reviewing small chunks is a listed success factor.
b) Is not correct. Evaluation of participants should never be an objective of a review.
c) Is not correct. Long sessions on large work products reduce concentration and effectiveness.
d) Is not correct. Adequate training should be provided for all participants.

stem:
Which TWO of the following are success factors for reviews?

Select TWO options.

options.a: Including the evaluation of participants as a review objective
options.b: Using the most formal review type for every work product
options.c: Providing adequate time for participants to prepare
options.d: Keeping review feedback away from the authors to avoid conflicts
options.e: Support from management for the review process

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Evaluation of participants should never be an objective.
b) Is not correct. Success depends on choosing the appropriate review type, not always the most formal one.
c) Is correct. Adequate preparation time is a listed success factor.
d) Is not correct. Feedback should be provided to stakeholders and authors so that they can improve.
e) Is correct. Management support is a listed success factor.

stem:
An organization notices that its reviews find few defects and participants consider them a waste of time. Which action is MOST likely to improve the success of its reviews?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Ask the manager to rank reviewers by the number of anomalies they find
options.b: Define clear objectives and measurable exit criteria for each review
options.c: Increase the size of each reviewed work product to make better use of meeting time
options.d: Remove the moderator role so that discussions are less restricted

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Evaluating participants damages the review culture and is never an appropriate objective.
b) Is correct. Clear objectives and measurable exit criteria are key success factors.
c) Is not correct. Larger chunks reduce concentration; small chunks are recommended.
d) Is not correct. Facilitated meetings are a success factor; removing facilitation tends to reduce effectiveness.

stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of experience-based test techniques?

options.a: Test cases are created based on detailed design information
options.b: Items tested within the interface code section are used to measure coverage
options.c: The test techniques heavily rely on the tester’s knowledge of the software and the business domain
options.d: The test cases are used to identify deviations from the requirements

explanation:
a) Is not correct. This is a common characteristic of white-box test techniques: test conditions, test cases and test data are derived from a test basis that may include code, software architecture, detailed design, or other information about the structure of the software.
b) Is not correct. This is a common characteristic of white-box test techniques: coverage is measured based on the items tested within a selected structure.
c) Is correct. This is a common characteristic of experience-based test techniques. Knowledge and experience (expected use of the software, its environment, likely defects and their distribution) are used to define tests.
d) Is not correct. This is a common characteristic of black-box test techniques: test cases may be used to detect gaps between requirements and their implementation, and deviations from the requirements.

stem: Which of the following statements BEST describes the difference between decision table testing and branch testing?

options.a: In decision table testing, the test cases are derived from the decision statements in the code. In branch testing, the test cases are derived from knowledge of the control flow of the test object.
options.b: In decision table testing, the test cases are derived from the specification that describes the business logic. In branch testing the test cases are based on anticipation of potential defects in the source code.
options.c: In decision table testing, the test cases are derived from knowledge of the control flow of the test object. In branch testing, test cases are derived from the specification that describes the business logic.
options.d: In decision table testing, the test cases are independent of how the software is implemented. In branch testing, test cases can be created only after the design or implementation of the code.

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Decision table testing is a black-box test technique – test cases are not based on decisions in the source code. (In branch testing, test cases are derived from knowledge of the control flow.)
b) Is not correct. Anticipation of potential defects is used in error guessing (an experience-based technique), not in branch testing (a white-box technique).
c) Is not correct. Basing test cases on knowledge of the control flow makes a technique white-box; decision table testing is typically based on analysis of business logic (black-box). Branch testing is white-box, with test cases derived from the source code structure, not the specification.
d) Is correct. Decision table testing is black-box, based on the specified behavior without reference to internal structure, so the test cases are independent of the implementation. Branch testing is white-box, based on the internal structure and processing; as the test cases depend on how the software is designed and coded, they can only be created after the design or implementation of the test object.

stem: What is the MAIN difference between black-box test techniques and experience-based test techniques?

options.a: The test object
options.b: The test level at which the test technique is used
options.c: The test basis
options.d: The software development lifecycle (SDLC) in which the test technique can be used

explanation:
a) Is not correct. In most cases both black-box and experience-based test techniques can be used for the same test objects.
b) Is not correct. Both black-box and experience-based test techniques can be used at all test levels.
c) Is correct. Black-box (specification-based) test techniques are based on an analysis of the specified behavior of the test object, so the test basis is usually a specification. Experience-based test techniques use the knowledge and experience of testers, so the tester may not use the specification at all.
d) Is not correct. Experience-based test techniques are complementary to black-box and white-box test techniques, and both black-box and experience-based test techniques can be used in all SDLCs.

stem:
You perform system testing of an e-commerce web application and are provided with the following requirement:

REQ 05-017. If the total cost of purchases exceeds $100, the customer gets a 5% discount on subsequent purchases. Otherwise, the customer does not receive a discount.

Which test techniques will be MOST helpful in designing test cases based on this requirement?

options.a: White-box test techniques
options.b: Black-box test techniques
options.c: Experience-based test techniques
options.d: Risk-based test techniques

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The document does not refer to the test object's internal structure but specifies the desired behavior of the test object. Therefore, white-box test techniques will not be helpful in designing test cases.
b) Is correct. The document is a requirement that specifies the desired behavior of the test object. Therefore, the most suitable test techniques are black-box test techniques (e.g., Boundary Value Analysis or Decision Table Testing).
c) Is not correct. Although experience-based test techniques can be used, black-box test techniques will be more suitable. The document describes a precise business rule and wording like "exceeds $100" suggests important equivalence partition boundaries that should be tested using black-box techniques like Boundary Value Analysis.
d) Is not correct. Risk-based test techniques are not a recognized type of test technique.

stem:
Which of the following is a typical characteristic of white-box test techniques?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Coverage is measured as the proportion of items of the implemented structure, such as statements, exercised by the tests
options.b: Test cases are derived from the specified behavior of the test object without reference to how it is implemented
options.c: Test cases are derived from the tester's knowledge of where defects were found in similar applications
options.d: Test cases remain valid when the implementation changes, as long as the required behavior does not change

explanation:
a) Is correct. White-box techniques derive tests from the internal structure (code, architecture, detailed design) and measure coverage against items of that structure.
b) Is not correct. This describes black-box test techniques, which are based on the specified behavior, not on the internal structure.
c) Is not correct. This describes experience-based test techniques such as error guessing.
d) Is not correct. This is a property of black-box test cases; white-box test cases depend on the implementation and may need updating when the code changes.

stem:
Match the following test techniques (1–4) with the category of test techniques (A–C) they belong to:

1. Decision table testing
2. Error guessing
3. Branch testing
4. State transition testing

A. Black-box test technique
B. White-box test technique
C. Experience-based test technique

Select ONE option.
explanation:
a) Is not correct. Error guessing is not white-box and branch testing is not experience-based.
b) Is not correct. Decision table testing is black-box, not experience-based, and state transition testing is black-box, not white-box.
c) Is correct. Decision table and state transition testing are black-box techniques, branch testing is white-box and error guessing is experience-based.
d) Is not correct. Branch testing is white-box (its coverage items are branches of the code) and state transition testing is black-box.

stem:
Which TWO of the following statements about black-box test techniques are correct?

Select TWO options.

options.a: They require access to the source code to derive the test conditions
options.b: They can detect gaps between the requirements and their implementation
options.c: Their coverage is measured against the control flow graph of the test object
options.d: They are mainly intended for situations where no specification is available
options.e: They are also called specification-based techniques because tests are derived from a test basis describing the required behavior

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Black-box techniques are based on the specification of behavior; no access to the code is needed.
b) Is correct. Black-box test cases check the specified behavior, so they can reveal deviations from, and gaps between, requirements and implementation.
c) Is not correct. Measuring coverage against a control flow graph is typical of white-box techniques.
d) Is not correct. Lack of (adequate) specification is the typical situation for experience-based techniques; black-box techniques need a test basis that describes behavior.
e) Is correct. This is the definition of black-box (specification-based) test techniques.

stem:
A test manager plans to complement the black-box and white-box tests of a release with some experience-based testing.

Which of the following statements about experience-based test techniques is CORRECT?

Select ONE option.

options.a: They can detect defects that may be missed by black-box and white-box techniques, so they complement those techniques
options.b: They provide precisely measurable coverage, because coverage items are derived systematically from the test basis
options.c: They should replace black-box techniques whenever a detailed specification is available
options.d: They are equally effective no matter who applies them, because they follow a defined procedure

explanation:
a) Is correct. This is exactly why experience-based techniques are recommended as a complement to the systematic techniques.
b) Is not correct. Coverage of experience-based techniques is difficult to measure; there are no systematically derived coverage items.
c) Is not correct. They complement, not replace, the other techniques.
d) Is not correct. Their effectiveness depends heavily on the tester's knowledge, skills and experience.

stem:
You are testing a simplified apartment search form which has only two search criteria:

• floor (with three possible options: ground floor; first floor; second or higher floor)
• garden type (with three possible options: no garden; small garden; large garden)

Each of the apartment on the ground floor has a garden, apartments on higher floors don’t. The form has a built-in validation mechanism that will not allow you to use the search criteria which violate this rule.

Each test has two input values: floor and garden type. You want to apply equivalence partitioning (EP) to cover each floor and each garden type in your tests.

What is the minimal number of test cases to achieve 100% EP coverage for valid partitions?
explanation:
This situation is described in the syllabus as “each choice” coverage. “Small garden” and “large garden” can go only with “ground floor”, so we need two test cases with “ground floor” covering these two garden-type partitions. We need two more test cases to cover the two other floor partitions; the remaining “no garden” partition is covered by these tests. Total of four test cases:
TC1 (ground floor, small garden)
TC2 (ground floor, large garden)
TC3 (first floor, no garden)
TC4 (second or higher floor, no garden)
Thus b) is correct.

stem:
Customers of the TestWash car wash chain have cards with a record of the number of washes they have bought so far. The initial value is 0. After entering the car wash, the system increases the number on the card by one. This value represents the number of the current wash. Based on this number the system decides what discount the customer is entitled to.

For every tenth wash the system gives a 10% discount, and for every twentieth wash, the system gives a further 40% discount (i.e., a 50% discount in total).

Which of the following sets of input data (understood as the numbers of the current wash) achieves the highest equivalence partition coverage?
explanation:
a) Is correct. 19 covers the "no discount" partition, 20 covers the "50% discount" partition, and 30 covers the "10% discount" partition. These three values cover all three valid equivalence partitions.
b) Is not correct. 11 and 12 cover "no discount" and 20 covers "50% discount" – two of the three valid partitions.
c) Is not correct. 1 covers "no discount", while 10 and 50 cover "10% discount". The "50% discount" partition is not covered – two of three.
d) Is not correct. 29 and 31 cover "no discount", while 10 and 30 cover "10% discount". The "50% discount" partition is not covered – two of three.

stem:
You are testing a PIN validator, which accepts valid PINs and rejects invalid PINs. A PIN is a sequence of digits. A PIN is valid if it consists of four digits, which are not all the same digit. You have identified the following valid equivalence partitions:

Variable: PIN code length
- The partition "length correct" - four-digit PINs
- The partition "length incorrect" - PINs with length other than 4

Variable: Number of different digits
- The partition "number of different digits correct" - PINs with at least two different digits
- The partition "number of different digits incorrect" - PINs with all digits being the same

Which of the following is the BEST set of input test data to cover the identified equivalence partitions?
explanation:
a) Is correct. "12" covers "length incorrect, too few digits"; "1111" covers "length correct" and "number of different digits incorrect"; "1234" covers "length correct" and "number of different digits correct"; "12345" covers "length incorrect, too many digits".
b) Is not correct. All partitions are covered, however it only covers the lower side of "length incorrect".
c) Is not correct. There is no value covering a correct PIN.
d) Is not correct. There is no value covering "number of different digits" incorrect.

stem:
The system for selling cinema tickets calculates the discount type based on the client's birth year (BY) and on the current year (CY) as follows:

Let D be the difference between CY and BY, that is, D = CY – BY
• If D < 0 then print the error message "birth year cannot be greater than current year"
• If 0 ≤ D < 18 then apply the student discount
• If 18 ≤ D < 65 then apply no discount
• If D ≥ 65 then apply the pensioner discount

Your test suite already contains two test cases:
• BY = 1990, CY = 2020, expected result: no discount
• BY = 2030, CY = 2029, expected result: print the error message

Which of the following test data sets should be added to achieve full valid equivalence partitioning coverage for the discount type?
explanation:
There are two equivalence partitions that are not yet covered, which correspond to "student discount" and "pensioner discount".
a) Is not correct. CY – BY = 64, so these inputs correspond to the already covered "no discount" partition.
b) Is correct. CY – BY = 65, so these inputs correspond to a partition that is not yet covered ("pensioner discount").
c) Is not correct. CY – BY = –65, so these inputs correspond to the already covered "error message" partition.
d) Is not correct. CY – BY = 18, so these inputs correspond to the already covered "no discount" partition.
e) Is correct. CY – BY = 0, so these inputs correspond to a partition that is not yet covered ("student discount").

stem:
A car park payment machine calculates the fee from the parking duration, entered in whole minutes:

• 0 – 30 minutes: free
• 31 – 120 minutes: standard rate
• 121 – 480 minutes: extended rate
• more than 480 minutes: daily rate

A negative duration is rejected as invalid.

Which of the following sets of test inputs achieves 100% equivalence partitioning (EP) coverage?

Select ONE option.
explanation:
There are five partitions: invalid {…, -1}, free {0–30}, standard {31–120}, extended {121–480} and daily {481, …}. 100% EP coverage requires at least one value from each.
a) Is not correct. These values cover only the free, standard and extended partitions (3 of 5); the invalid and daily-rate partitions are missed.
b) Is correct. One value from each of the five partitions: invalid (-5), free (15), standard (60), extended (300) and daily (600).
c) Is not correct. No value from the standard-rate partition (31–120): 130 and 450 are both in the extended partition.
d) Is not correct. The invalid partition (negative duration) is not covered.

stem:
A museum ticketing system determines the ticket price from the visitor's age (an integer number of years):

• 0 – 5: free
• 6 – 17: child ticket
• 18 – 64: adult ticket
• 65 – 120: senior ticket

Ages below 0 or above 120 are rejected as invalid. Assume one invalid partition for each side.

The following test inputs for age have been executed: 3, 12, 15, 70, 99, 125.

What equivalence partitioning (EP) coverage has been achieved?

Select ONE option.
explanation:
There are six partitions: <0 (invalid), 0–5, 6–17, 18–64, 65–120, >120 (invalid). The tests cover 0–5 (3), 6–17 (12, 15), 65–120 (70, 99) and >120 (125) – 4 partitions. 18–64 and <0 are not covered: 4/6 = 66.7%.
a) Is not correct. This would correspond to 3 of 6 partitions.
b) Is not correct. This is 4/7; there are six partitions, not seven.
c) Is correct. 4 of 6 partitions are covered.
d) Is not correct. This would require 5 of 6 partitions; the adult partition and the lower invalid partition are both missing.

stem:
A parcel booking form has two input fields, each with a drop-down list:

• destination: domestic, EU, international
• packaging: envelope, small box, large box, pallet, crate

The form only allows large box, pallet and crate for domestic shipments; envelope and small box can be selected for any destination. Combinations that violate this rule cannot be entered.

You treat each list option as a valid equivalence partition and want every partition of both fields to be covered (each choice coverage).

What is the MINIMUM number of test cases needed?

Select ONE option.
explanation:
Large box, pallet and crate can only be combined with domestic, so three domestic tests are needed for them. EU and international need two further tests, which can use envelope and small box, e.g. (domestic, large box), (domestic, pallet), (domestic, crate), (EU, envelope), (international, small box). Five packaging options also mean at least five tests are needed. Minimum = 5.
a) Is not correct. Four tests would suffice only without the constraint (the largest field has five options, so even then four is too few).
b) Is not correct. Three tests cover the three destinations but cannot cover five packaging types.
c) Is not correct. Six tests are more than needed; the two non-domestic tests can cover envelope and small box.
d) Is correct. Five tests are the minimum.

stem:
An insurance company calculates the premium band from the engine capacity of a car, entered as an integer in cm³:

• 1 – 1000: band A
• 1001 – 1600: band B
• 1601 – 2500: band C
• above 2500: band D

A value of 0 or less is rejected.

Which pair of test values belongs to the SAME equivalence partition?

Select ONE option.

options.d: 0 and 600

explanation:
The partitions are: invalid {…, 0}, A {1–1000}, B {1001–1600}, C {1601–2500}, D {2501, …}.
a) Is correct. Both values are in band C (1601–2500).
b) Is not correct. 1000 is in band A and 1001 is in band B.
c) Is not correct. 2500 is in band C and 2501 is in band D.
d) Is not correct. 0 is in the invalid partition, 600 is in band A.

stem:
You are testing a system that calculates the final course grade for a given student.

The final grade is assigned based on the final result, according to the following rules:

• 0 – 50 points: failed
• 51 – 60 points: fair
• 61 – 70 points: satisfactory
• 71 – 80 points: good
• 81 – 90 points: very good
• 91 – 100 points: excellent

You have prepared the following set of test cases:

| | Final result | Final grade |
|---|---|---|
| TC1 | 91 | excellent |
| TC2 | 50 | failed |
| TC3 | 81 | very good |
| TC4 | 60 | fair |
| TC5 | 70 | satisfactory |
| TC6 | 80 | good |

What is the 2-value boundary value analysis (BVA) coverage for the final result that is achieved with the existing test cases?
explanation: There are 12 boundary values for the final result: 0, 50, 51, 60, 61, 70, 71, 80, 81, 90, 91 and 100. The test cases cover six of them (TC1 – 91, TC2 – 50, TC3 – 81, TC4 – 60, TC5 – 70, TC6 – 80). Therefore, the test cases cover 6/12 = 50%. Thus a) is correct.

stem:
A wine storage system uses a control device that measures the wine cell temperature T (measured in °C, rounded to the nearest degree) and alarms the user if it deviates from the optimal value of 12, according to the following rules:

• if T = 12, the system says, “optimal temperature”
• if T < 12, the system says, “temperature is too low!”
• if T > 12, the system says, “temperature is too high!”

You want to use the 3-point boundary value analysis (BVA) to verify the behavior of the control device. A test input is a temperature in °C provided by the device.

What is the MINIMAL set of test inputs that achieves 100% of the desired coverage?
explanation: There are three equivalence partitions: {..., 10, 11}, {12}, and {13, 14, ...}. The boundary values are 11, 12 and 13. In 3-point BVA, for each boundary we test the boundary and both its neighbors: for 11 → 10, 11, 12; for 12 → 11, 12, 13; for 13 → 12, 13, 14. Altogether: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14. Thus c) is correct.

stem:
You are testing a form that verifies the correctness of the length of the password given as input. The form accepts a password with the correct length and rejects a password that is too short or too long. The password length is correct if it has between 6 and 12 characters inclusive. Otherwise, it is considered incorrect.

At first, the form is empty (password length = 0). You apply boundary value analysis to the “password length” variable.

Your set of test cases achieves 100% 2-value boundary value coverage. The team decided that due to the high risk of this component, test cases should be added to ensure 100% 3-value boundary value coverage.

Which additional password lengths should be tested to achieve this?

A developer was asked to implement the following business rule:

```
INPUT: value (integer number)
IF (value ≤ 100 OR value ≥ 200) THEN write "value incorrect"
ELSE write "value OK"
```

You design the test cases using 2-value boundary value analysis.

Which of the following sets of test inputs achieves the greatest coverage?
explanation:
The equivalence partitions are: {..., 99, 100}, {101, 102, ..., 198, 199}, {200, 201, ...}. Thus, there are 4 boundary values: 100, 101, 199 and 200. In 2-value BVA, for each boundary value there are two coverage items (the boundary value and its closest neighbor belonging to the adjacent partition). As the closest neighbors are also boundary values in the adjacent partition, there are just four coverage items.
a) Is not correct. Only 100 and 200 are valid coverage items, so we achieve 50% coverage.
b) Is not correct. Only 100 and 200 are valid coverage items, so we achieve 50% coverage.
c) Is not correct. Only 100 and 101 are valid coverage items, so we achieve 50% coverage.
d) Is correct. 101, 199 and 200 are valid coverage items, so we achieve 75% coverage.

stem:
You are testing a temperature control system for a horticultural cold storage facility. The system receives the temperature (in full degrees Celsius) as the input. If the temperature is between 0 and 2 degrees inclusive, the system displays the message "temperature OK". For lower temperatures, the system displays the message "temperature too low" and for higher temperatures it displays the message "temperature too high".

Using two-value boundary value analysis, which of the following sets of test inputs provides the highest level of boundary value coverage?
explanation:
There are three equivalence partitions: {…, –2, –1}, {0, 1, 2}, {3, 4, …}. For 2-value BVA all the boundary values for all the equivalence partitions must be covered. The boundary values are –1 (for the "temperature too low" partition), 0, 2 (for the "temperature OK" partition) and 3 (for the "temperature too high" partition).
Thus:
a) Is not correct.
b) Is not correct.
c) Is correct. The correct option is: –1, 0, 2, 3.
d) Is not correct.

stem:
A courier service classifies parcels by weight, entered in whole kilograms:

• 1 – 5 kg: standard
• 6 – 20 kg: heavy
• 21 – 30 kg: freight

Weights of 0 kg or less, and weights above 30 kg, are rejected.

The following test inputs have been executed: 0, 5, 6, 12, 21, 25, 31.

What 2-value boundary value analysis (BVA) coverage has been achieved?

Select ONE option.
explanation:
The partitions are {…, 0}, {1–5}, {6–20}, {21–30}, {31, …}, so the boundary values (coverage items) are 0, 1, 5, 6, 20, 21, 30, 31 – eight in total. The tests cover 0, 5, 6, 21 and 31 (12 and 25 are not boundary values): 5/8 = 62.5%.
a) Is not correct. This would correspond to 4 of 8 boundary values.
b) Is correct. 5 of 8 boundary values are covered.
c) Is not correct. This is 5/7, i.e. dividing by the number of tests instead of the number of coverage items.
d) Is not correct. This would require 6 of 8 boundary values; 1, 20 and 30 are missing.

stem:
The temperature of a water heater can be set in whole degrees Celsius:

• 30 – 45: eco mode
• 46 – 60: normal mode
• 61 – 75: boost mode

Any setting below 30 or above 75 is rejected.

What is the MINIMUM number of test inputs needed to achieve 100% 3-value boundary value analysis (BVA) coverage?

Select ONE option.
explanation:
Boundary values: 29, 30, 45, 46, 60, 61, 75, 76. In 3-value BVA each boundary value is tested together with both its neighbours. The distinct values are 28, 29, 30, 31, 44, 45, 46, 47, 59, 60, 61, 62, 74, 75, 76, 77 – 16 test inputs.
a) Is not correct. 24 = 8 boundary values × 3, but many neighbours coincide with other coverage items and need to be tested only once.
b) Is not correct. 12 ignores some neighbours, e.g. 28 and 77 (neighbours of the boundary values 29 and 76 of the invalid partitions).
c) Is correct. There are 16 distinct test inputs.
d) Is not correct. 18 counts some coinciding values twice.

stem:
A hotel loyalty program assigns a status based on the number of nights stayed during the year (an integer; the input field cannot hold negative numbers):

• 0 – 9 nights: Silver
• 10 – 24 nights: Gold
• 25 or more nights: Platinum

Your existing test cases achieve 100% 2-value boundary value analysis (BVA) coverage using the inputs 0, 9, 10, 24 and 25. Because the status determines discounts, the team decides to achieve 100% 3-value BVA coverage.

What is the MINIMAL set of ADDITIONAL inputs needed?

Select ONE option.
explanation:
Boundary values are 0, 9, 10, 24 and 25 (Platinum has no upper boundary). 3-value BVA adds the neighbours of each boundary value: 0 → 1 (−1 is impossible), 9 → 8, 10, 10 → 9, 11, 24 → 23, 25, 25 → 24, 26. All required values: 0, 1, 8, 9, 10, 11, 23, 24, 25, 26. Already tested: 0, 9, 10, 24, 25, so 1, 8, 11, 23 and 26 must be added.
a) Is correct. These are exactly the missing neighbours.
b) Is not correct. The neighbour 1 of boundary value 0 is missing.
c) Is not correct. The neighbours 8 and 23 (below boundary values 9 and 24) are missing.
d) Is not correct. -1 cannot be entered in the field, so it is not a coverage item; the set is not minimal.

stem:
An online shop charges a shipping fee for orders below 50.00 EUR; orders with a total of 50.00 EUR or more are shipped free of charge. Order totals are calculated to the cent (two decimal places).

Which test inputs are the 2-value boundary value analysis (BVA) coverage items for the boundary between "shipping fee charged" and "free shipping"?

Select ONE option.

options.a: 49 and 50

explanation:
The partitions are 'fee charged' {…, 49.99} and 'free shipping' {50.00, …}, with a step of 0.01. In 2-value BVA the coverage items are the boundary value and its closest neighbour in the adjacent partition: 49.99 and 50.00.
a) Is not correct. The values are stored to the cent, so the closest neighbour of 50.00 is 49.99, not 49.
b) Is not correct. Both values lie in the same partition (free shipping); 50.01 is the 3-value neighbour, not a 2-value coverage item.
c) Is not correct. These are the 3-value BVA test inputs for this boundary, not the 2-value coverage items.
d) Is correct. 49.99 is the largest value of the 'fee' partition and 50.00 the smallest value of the 'free' partition.

stem:
Your favorite bicycle daily rental store has just introduced a new Customer Relationship Management system and asked you, one of their most loyal members, to test it.

The implemented features are as follows:

• Anyone can rent a bicycle, but members receive a 20% discount
• However, if the return deadline is missed, the discount is no longer available
• After 15 rentals, members get a gift: a T-Shirt

Decision table describing the implemented features looks as follows:

| Conditions | R1 | R2 | R3 | R4 | R5 | R6 | R7 | R8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Being a member | T | T | T | T | F | F | F | F |
| Missed deadline | T | F | T | F | T | F | F | T |
| 15th rental | F | F | T | T | F | F | T | T |
| **Actions** | | | | | | | | |
| 20% discount | | X | | X | | | | |
| Gift T-Shirt | | | X | X | | | | X |

Based ONLY on the feature description of the Customer Relationship Management system, which of the above rules describes an impossible situation?

options.a: R4
options.b: R2
options.c: R6
options.d: R8

explanation:
a) Is not correct. A member without a missed deadline can get a discount and a gift T-Shirt after 15 bicycle rentals.
b) Is not correct. A member without a missed deadline can get a discount but no gift T-Shirt until they rented a bicycle 15 times.
c) Is not correct. Non-members cannot get a discount, even if they did not miss a deadline yet.
d) Is correct. No discount as a non-member that has also missed a deadline, but only members can receive a gift T-Shirt. Hence, the action is not correct.

stem:
The following decision table contains the rules for determining the risk of atherosclerosis.

| | Rule 1 | Rule 2 | Rule 3 | Rule 4 | Rule 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Conditions** | | | | | |
| Cholesterol (mg/dl) | ≤ 124 | ≤ 124 | 125 – 200 | 125 – 200 | ≥ 201 |
| Blood pressure (mm Hg) | ≤ 140 | > 140 | ≤ 140 | > 140 | – |
| **Action** | | | | | |
| Risk level | very low | low | medium | high | very high |

You designed the test cases with the following input data:

TC1: Cholesterol = 125 mg/dl, Blood pressure = 141 mm Hg
TC2: Cholesterol = 200 mg/dl, Blood pressure = 201 mm Hg
TC3: Cholesterol = 124 mg/dl, Blood pressure = 201 mm Hg
TC4: Cholesterol = 109 mg/dl, Blood pressure = 200 mm Hg
TC5: Cholesterol = 201 mg/dl, Blood pressure = 140 mm Hg

What is the decision table coverage achieved by these test cases?
explanation:
There are five columns in the decision table. Each test case covers one of them.
TC1 and TC2 both cover Rule 4.
TC3 and TC4 both cover Rule 2.
TC5 covers Rule 5.
So these five test cases cover three out of five columns, achieving (3/5)*100% = 60% coverage.
Thus a), c), d) are not correct; b) is correct.

stem:
You are working on a project to develop a system to analyze driving test results. You have been asked to design test cases based on the following decision table.

| | R1 | R2 | R3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1: First attempt at the exam? | - | - | F |
| C2: Theoretical exam passed? | T | F | - |
| C3: Practical exam passed? | T | - | F |
| Issue a driving license? | X | | |
| Request additional driving lessons? | | | X |
| Request to take the exam again? | | X | |

What test data will show that there are contradictory rules in the decision table?

options.a: C1 = T, C2 = T, C3 = F
options.b: C1 = T, C2 = F, C3 = T
options.c: C1 = T, C2 = T, C3 = T and C1 = F, C2 = T, C3 = T
options.d: C1 = F, C2 = F, C3 = F

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The combination (T, T, F) does not match any rule. This is an example of omission, not a contradiction.
b) Is not correct. The combination (T, F, T) matches only one column, R2, so there is no contradiction.
c) Is not correct. Both combinations (T, T, T) and (F, T, T) match only one column, R1, so there is no contradiction.
d) Is correct. The combination (F, F, F) matches both R2 and R3, but R2 and R3 have different actions, so this shows a contradiction between R2 and R3.

stem:
You are designing test cases based on the following decision table.

| | R1 | R2 | R3 | R4 | R5 | R6 | R7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1: Age | 0-18 | 19-65 | 19-65 | >65 | 0-18 | 19-65 | >65 |
| C2: Experience | - | 0-4 | >4 | - | - | - | - |
| C3: Registered? | NO | NO | NO | NO | YES | YES | YES |
| Category | A | A | B | B | B | D | C |

So far you have designed the following test cases:
• TC1: 19-year-old, unregistered man with no experience; expected result: category A
• TC2: 65-year-old, unregistered woman with 5 years of experience; expected result: category B
• TC3: 66-year-old, registered man with no experience; expected result: category C
• TC4: 65-year-old, registered woman with 4 years of experience; expected result: category D

Which of the following test cases, when added to the existing set of test cases, will increase the decision table coverage?

options.a: 66-year-old, unregistered man with no experience; expected result: category B
options.b: 55-year-old, unregistered woman with 2 years of experience; expected result: category A
options.c: 19-year-old, registered woman with 5 years of experience; expected result: category D
options.d: No additional test case can increase the already achieved decision table coverage

explanation:
Test cases TC1, TC2, TC3 and TC4 cover, respectively, rules R2, R3, R7 and R6 in the decision table.
a) Is correct. The conditions "66-year-old", "unregistered" and "no experience" match rule R4, which is not covered by the existing test cases, so after adding this test case, the decision table coverage will increase.
b) Is not correct. The conditions "55-year-old", "unregistered" and "2 years of experience" match rule R2, already covered by TC1.
c) Is not correct. The conditions "19-year-old", "registered" and "5 years of experience" match rule R6, already covered by TC4.
d) Is not correct. The existing test cases cover only 4 out of 7 columns of the decision table. The coverage can be increased by adding test cases that cover yet uncovered columns, that is, R1, R4 and R5.

stem:
A car rental system uses the following decision table to determine additional charges.

| Conditions | R1 | R2 | R3 | R4 | R5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Driver younger than 25? | T | T | T | F | F |
| Premium car? | T | F | F | T | F |
| Credit card includes insurance? | – | T | F | – | – |
| **Actions** | | | | | |
| Young driver fee | X | | X | | |
| Premium deposit | X | | | X | |
| Insurance offer | X | | X | X | X |

The following test cases have been designed:

| | Driver age | Car | Card insurance |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC1 | 22 | premium | no |
| TC2 | 30 | economy | yes |
| TC3 | 24 | premium | yes |
| TC4 | 25 | premium | no |
| TC5 | 21 | economy | yes |
| TC6 | 60 | economy | no |

What decision table coverage is achieved by these test cases?

Select ONE option.
explanation:
TC1 and TC3 → R1 (younger than 25, premium; card insurance is irrelevant). TC2 and TC6 → R5. TC4: a 25-year-old is NOT younger than 25, premium car → R4. TC5 → R2. R3 is not covered. Coverage = 4/5 = 80%.
a) Is not correct. This underestimates the result: four of the five columns are covered.
b) Is not correct. This is 4/6, i.e. covered rules divided by the number of test cases instead of the number of columns.
c) Is correct. 4 of 5 columns are covered.
d) Is not correct. R3 (young driver, economy car, no card insurance) is not exercised by any test.

stem:
A ticketing application decides on the price reduction using three conditions:

• Is the customer a member? (yes / no)
• Payment method (credit card / bank transfer / voucher)
• Is the order value above 100 EUR? (yes / no)

You create a full decision table (before any minimization) listing every combination of condition values.

How many columns (rules) does the full decision table have?

Select ONE option.
explanation:
The number of columns of a full decision table is the product of the number of values of each condition: 2 × 3 × 2 = 12.
a) Is correct. 2 × 3 × 2 = 12 combinations.
b) Is not correct. 7 is the sum of the values (2 + 3 + 2), not the number of combinations.
c) Is not correct. 8 = 2³ would be correct only if all three conditions were Boolean; payment method has three values.
d) Is not correct. 6 ignores one of the Boolean conditions.

stem:
The following decision table specifies the discount granted by a web shop.

| Conditions | R1 | R2 | R3 | R4 | R5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1: Registered customer? | T | T | F | F | T |
| C2: Cart value ≥ 200 EUR? | T | F | – | T | F |
| C3: Promo code entered? | – | T | T | F | F |
| **Action** | | | | | |
| Discount | 10% | 5% | 5% | none | none |

During test design you want to check whether the decision table is complete.

Which combination of condition values shows that a rule is MISSING from the table?

Select ONE option.

options.a: C1 = T, C2 = F, C3 = F
options.b: C1 = F, C2 = T, C3 = T
options.c: C1 = F, C2 = F, C3 = F
options.d: C1 = T, C2 = T, C3 = F

explanation:
Expanding the '–' entries: R1 covers TTT and TTF, R2 covers TFT, R3 covers FTT and FFT, R4 covers FTF, R5 covers TFF. That is 7 of the 8 possible combinations; FFF is not covered by any rule.
a) Is not correct. This combination matches R5 only.
b) Is not correct. This combination matches R3 only (C2 is irrelevant in R3).
c) Is correct. No column matches this combination, so the table is incomplete (omission).
d) Is not correct. This combination matches R1 only (C3 is irrelevant in R1).

stem:
A cinema introduces the following rules:

• Students pay a reduced ticket price.
• On Tuesdays, every customer pays the reduced ticket price.
• Loyalty-program members who have collected 10 stamps receive free popcorn.

A developer has created the following decision table from these rules:

| Conditions | R1 | R2 | R3 | R4 | R5 | R6 | R7 | R8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Student? | T | T | F | T | F | T | F | F |
| Tuesday? | T | F | F | T | T | F | T | F |
| Member with 10 stamps? | T | F | T | F | F | T | T | F |
| **Actions** | | | | | | | | |
| Reduced ticket price | X | X |  | X |  | X | X |  |
| Free popcorn | X |  | X |  |  | X | X |  |

Based ONLY on the rules above, which column of the decision table contains an INCORRECT action?

Select ONE option.

options.a: R3
options.b: R5
options.c: R6
options.d: R8

explanation:
Expected actions: reduced price = Student OR Tuesday; free popcorn = member with 10 stamps.
a) Is not correct. Not a student, not Tuesday → normal price; member with 10 stamps → free popcorn. Correct.
b) Is correct. On a Tuesday every customer pays the reduced price, but R5 does not mark the reduced price action.
c) Is not correct. A student pays the reduced price and a member with 10 stamps gets popcorn. Correct.
d) Is not correct. No condition is true, so no action applies. Correct.

stem:
You test a system whose lifecycle is modeled by the state transition diagram shown below. The system starts in the INIT state and ends its operation in the OFF state.

What is the MINIMAL number of test cases to achieve valid transitions coverage?
figure:
State transition diagram. States: INIT (initial), DEBUG MODE, IN OPERATION, ON HOLD, OFF (final). 7 valid transitions (source --event--> target):
1. INIT --test--> DEBUG MODE
2. INIT --run--> IN OPERATION
3. IN OPERATION --error--> DEBUG MODE
4. DEBUG MODE --done--> OFF
5. IN OPERATION --pause--> ON HOLD
6. ON HOLD --resume--> IN OPERATION
7. ON HOLD --done--> OFF
There are no other transitions (no transition leaves OFF; DEBUG MODE only goes to OFF).
explanation:
“test” and “error” transitions cannot occur in one test case. Neither can both “done” transitions. This means we need at least three test cases to achieve transition coverage. For example:
TC1: test, done
TC2: run, error, done
TC3: run, pause, resume, pause, done
Thus d) is correct.

stem:
A storage system can store up to three elements and is modeled by the following state transition diagram. The variable N represents the number of currently stored elements.

Which of the following test cases, represented as sequences of events, achieves the highest level of valid transitions coverage?
figure:
State transition diagram. States: START (initial), NOT FULL, FULL. N = number of stored elements. 5 valid transitions (source --event [guard] / action--> target):
E1. START --Add / N := 1--> NOT FULL
E2. NOT FULL --Add [N < 2] / N := N + 1--> NOT FULL (self-loop)
E3. NOT FULL --Remove [N > 0] / N := N – 1--> NOT FULL (self-loop)
E4. NOT FULL --Add [N = 2] / N := N + 1--> FULL
E5. FULL --Remove / N := N – 1--> NOT FULL
There are no other transitions (in particular, no Add transition leaves FULL). The labels E1–E5 are used in the official answer, not in the question's diagram.

options.a: Add, Remove, Add, Add, Add
options.b: Add, Add, Add, Add, Remove, Remove
options.c: Add, Add, Add, Remove, Remove
options.d: Add, Add, Add, Remove, Add

explanation:
Label the transitions E1…E5 (see figure). Each "Add" increases N by 1 and each "Remove" decreases it by 1. When "Add" occurs in NOT FULL, the state changes to FULL only if N=2; if N<2 the system stays in NOT FULL. If N=0, no "Remove" is possible; if N=3, no "Add" is possible.
a) Is not correct. The test can be written as E1, E3, E2, E2, E4 (the official answer prints "E1, E3, E3, E2, E4", which appears to be a typo), covering 4 of 5 valid transitions = 80%.
b) Is not correct. The test is infeasible: after the first three "Add" events the system is in FULL and there is no valid transition from FULL triggered by "Add". After the first three transitions only 60% valid transitions coverage is achieved.
c) Is correct. The test can be written as E1, E2, E4, E5, E3, covering 5 of 5 valid transitions = 100%.
d) Is not correct. The test can be written as E1, E2, E4, E5, E4, covering 4 of 5 valid transitions = 80%.

stem:
You are designing test cases based on the following state transition diagram:

What is the MINIMUM number of test cases required to achieve 100% valid transitions coverage?
figure:
State transition diagram (hotel room booking). States: START (initial), REQUESTING, WAITING LIST, CONFIRMED, END (final). 6 valid transitions (source --event--> target):
1. START --Room request--> REQUESTING
2. REQUESTING --Available--> CONFIRMED
3. REQUESTING --Not available--> WAITING LIST
4. WAITING LIST --Available--> CONFIRMED
5. WAITING LIST --Cancel--> END
6. CONFIRMED --Pay--> END
There are no other transitions (no loops, no transitions out of END).
explanation:
The following three transitions: "REQUESTING -> CONFIRMED", "WAITING LIST -> CONFIRMED" and "WAITING LIST -> END" cannot appear in the same test case, which suggests that at least three test cases are required. All the other transitions can appear in combination with one or more of these three transitions, so we need a minimum of three test cases. In fact, only three sequences are possible:
TC1: START (Room request) -> REQUESTING (Available) -> CONFIRMED (Pay) -> END
TC2: START (Room request) -> REQUESTING (Not available) -> WAITING LIST (Available) -> CONFIRMED (Pay) -> END
TC3: START (Room request) -> REQUESTING (Not available) -> WAITING LIST (Cancel) -> END
Thus: a) Is correct. b), c), d) Are not correct.

stem:
You are applying state transition testing to the hotel room reservation system modeled by the following state transition table, with 4 states and 5 different events (an empty cell means there is no valid transition for that event in that state):

| State | Available | NotAvailable | ChangeRoom | Cancel | Pay |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1: Requesting | S2 | S3 | | | |
| S2: Confirmed | | | S1 | S4 | S4 |
| S3: Waiting list | S2 | | | S4 | |
| S4: End | | | | | |

Assuming all test cases start in the 'Requesting' state, which of the following test cases, represented as sequences of events, achieves the highest valid transitions coverage?

options.a: NotAvailable, Available, ChangeRoom, NotAvailable, Cancel
options.b: Available, ChangeRoom, NotAvailable, Available, Pay
options.c: Available, ChangeRoom, Available, ChangeRoom, NotAvailable
options.d: NotAvailable, Cancel, ChangeRoom, Available, Pay

explanation:
There are 7 valid transitions: S1-Available->S2, S1-NotAvailable->S3, S2-ChangeRoom->S1, S2-Cancel->S4, S2-Pay->S4, S3-Available->S2, S3-Cancel->S4.
a) Is not correct. This sequence covers 4 different valid transitions (both "NotAvailable" events correspond to the same transition between S1 and S3), i.e., 4 out of 7 valid transitions.
b) Is correct. This sequence covers 5 different transitions (the first "Available" event corresponds to the transition S1 to S2, the second "Available" event to the transition S3 to S2, so two different transitions are covered). It covers 5 out of 7 valid transitions and achieves the highest valid transitions coverage.
c) Is not correct. This sequence covers 3 different transitions (both "Available" events correspond to the same transition S1 to S2; both "ChangeRoom" events to the same transition S2 to S1), i.e., 3 out of 7.
d) Is not correct. This sequence is not a feasible test case, because after "Cancel" the system ends up in the End state and no further valid transitions can be executed.

stem:
A VoIP call component is modeled by the following state transitions. Each test case starts in the IDLE state and ends when the ENDED state is reached (ENDED has no outgoing transitions).

| # | Source state | Event | Target state |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | IDLE | dial | DIALING |
| 2 | DIALING | answer | CONNECTED |
| 3 | DIALING | busy signal | BUSY |
| 4 | DIALING | hang up | ENDED |
| 5 | BUSY | redial | DIALING |
| 6 | BUSY | hang up | ENDED |
| 7 | CONNECTED | hold | ON HOLD |
| 8 | ON HOLD | resume | CONNECTED |
| 9 | CONNECTED | hang up | ENDED |

What is the MINIMUM number of test cases needed to achieve 100% valid transitions coverage?

Select ONE option.
explanation:
Transitions 4, 6 and 9 all end in ENDED, and each test case ends when ENDED is reached, so each of them needs its own test – at least 3 test cases.
