Three are also sufficient, e.g. TC1: dial, busy signal, redial, answer, hold, resume, hang up (1, 3, 5, 2, 7, 8, 9); TC2: dial, hang up (1, 4); TC3: dial, busy signal, hang up (1, 3, 6).
a) Is not correct. Two tests cannot cover three different transitions into ENDED.
b) Is correct. Three test cases are the minimum.
c) Is not correct. Four tests are more than necessary, because the loops (BUSY → DIALING, ON HOLD → CONNECTED) can be included in the same test.
d) Is not correct. One test per transition is not required; a test case can cover many transitions.

stem:
A media player is modeled by the following state transition table. An empty cell means that the event is not valid in that state.

| State | play | pause | stop | next |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| STOPPED | PLAYING | | | |
| PLAYING | | PAUSED | STOPPED | PLAYING |
| PAUSED | PLAYING | | STOPPED | |

All test cases start in the STOPPED state.

Which of the following test cases, given as sequences of events, achieves the HIGHEST valid transitions coverage?

Select ONE option.

options.a: play, pause, play, stop
options.b: play, next, pause, play, stop
options.c: play, stop, play, stop, play
options.d: play, pause, stop, play, next

explanation:
There are 6 valid transitions (filled cells).
a) Is not correct. Covers 4 of 6 valid transitions (66.7%).
b) Is correct. Covers 5 of 6 valid transitions (83.3%): STOPPED-play, PLAYING-next, PLAYING-pause, PAUSED-play, PLAYING-stop.
c) Is not correct. Repeats the same two transitions: 2 of 6 (33.3%).
d) Is not correct. Covers 4 of 6 valid transitions (66.7%).

stem:
A ticket machine is modeled by the following state transition table. An empty cell represents an invalid transition.

| State | coin | select | print | fault | repair |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IDLE | PAID |  |  | OUT OF SERVICE |  |
| PAID | PAID | SELECTED |  | OUT OF SERVICE |  |
| SELECTED |  |  | IDLE | OUT OF SERVICE |  |
| OUT OF SERVICE |  |  |  |  | IDLE |

How many coverage items are there for valid transitions coverage and for all transitions coverage, respectively?

Select ONE option.

options.a: 8 and 12
options.b: 8 and 20
options.c: 4 and 20
options.d: 12 and 20

explanation:
The table has 4 states × 5 events = 20 cells. 8 cells contain a target state (valid transitions); the remaining 12 are invalid transitions. Valid transitions coverage has 8 coverage items; all transitions coverage covers all valid and invalid transitions, i.e. 20 coverage items.
a) Is not correct. 12 is the number of invalid transitions only; all transitions coverage includes the valid ones as well.
b) Is correct. 8 valid transitions; 8 valid + 12 invalid = 20 transitions for all transitions coverage.
c) Is not correct. 4 is the number of states (coverage items for all states coverage), not of valid transitions.
d) Is not correct. 12 is the number of invalid transitions, not of valid transitions.

stem:
A door controller has four states: CLOSED (initial state), OPEN, LOCKED and ALARM. Its valid transitions are:

• CLOSED --open--> OPEN
• OPEN --close--> CLOSED
• CLOSED --lock--> LOCKED
• LOCKED --unlock--> CLOSED
• LOCKED --force--> ALARM
• ALARM --reset--> LOCKED
• OPEN --timeout--> ALARM

A single test case is executed, starting in CLOSED, with the event sequence: open, close, lock, unlock.

What all states coverage and valid transitions coverage does this test case achieve?

Select ONE option.

options.a: All states coverage 100%, valid transitions coverage 57.1%
options.b: All states coverage 75%, valid transitions coverage 50%
options.c: All states coverage 75%, valid transitions coverage 66.7%
options.d: All states coverage 75%, valid transitions coverage 57.1%

explanation:
The test visits CLOSED, OPEN, CLOSED, LOCKED, CLOSED – 3 of 4 states (ALARM is missed): 75%. It exercises 4 different valid transitions (open, close, lock, unlock) of 7: 57.1%.
a) Is not correct. ALARM is never visited, so all states coverage is not 100%.
b) Is not correct. 4 of 7 transitions are covered, which is 57.1%, not 50%.
c) Is not correct. 66.7% would need more covered transitions; only 4 of 7 are covered.
d) Is correct. 3/4 states and 4/7 valid transitions.

stem: Your test suite achieved 100% statement coverage. What is the consequence of this fact?

options.a: Each instruction in the code that contains a defect has been executed at least once
options.b: Any test suite containing more test cases than your test suite will also achieve 100% statement coverage
options.c: Each path in the code has been executed at least once
options.d: Every combination of input values has been tested at least once

explanation:
a) Is correct. Since 100% statement coverage is achieved, every statement, including the ones with defects, must have been executed and evaluated at least once.
b) Is not correct. Coverage depends on what is tested, not on the number of test cases. E.g., for code “if (x==0) y=1”, one test case (x=0) achieves 100% statement coverage, but two test cases (x=1) and (x=2) together achieve only 50%.
c) Is not correct. If there is a loop in the code there may be an infinite number of possible paths, so it is not possible to execute all possible paths.
d) Is not correct. Exhaustive testing is not possible. E.g., for code “input x; print x” any single test achieves 100% statement coverage but covers one input value.

stem:
You run two test cases, T1 and T2, on the same code. Test T1 achieved 40% statement coverage and test T2 achieved 65% statement coverage.

Which of the following sentences must be necessarily true?

options.a: The test suite composed of tests T1 and T2 achieves 105% statement coverage
options.b: There exists at least one statement that must have been executed by both T1 and T2
options.c: At least 5% of the statements in the code that was tested are non-executable
options.d: The test suite composed of tests T1 and T2 achieves full branch coverage

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Coverage is always defined as the percentage of covered elements, so it cannot exceed 100%.
b) Is correct. If the statements executed by T1 and T2 were disjoint, the coverage of the suite {T1, T2} would be 105%, which is impossible. Therefore, at least 5% of executable statements must have been executed by both T1 and T2.
c) Is not correct. Statement coverage does not tell us anything about the number of non-executable statements in the code.
d) Is not correct. Even if a test suite achieves full statement coverage, this does not imply full branch coverage.

stem:
Your test suite S for a program P achieves 100% statement coverage. It consists of three test cases, each of which achieves 50% statement coverage.

Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

options.a: Executing S will cause all possible failures in P
options.b: S achieves 100% branch coverage for P
options.c: Every executable statement in P containing a defect has been run at least once during the execution of S
options.d: After removing one test case from S, the remaining two test cases will still achieve 100% statement coverage

explanation:
a) Is not correct. A statement with a defect, when executed, does not have to cause a failure. For example, a statement x := y / z will cause a failure only when z equals 0.
b) Is not correct. 100% statement coverage does not guarantee 100% branch coverage. For example, a test case with x=0 for the code "1. IF (x=0) THEN 2. A; 3. ENDIF" achieves 100% statement coverage but does not cover the branch from 1 to 3.
c) Is correct. 100% statement coverage means that each executable statement was executed at least once.
d) Is not correct. The removed test case may provide coverage of some statements that are not covered by either of the other two test cases, in which case the remaining two test cases together will not achieve 100% statement coverage.

stem:
Which of the following statements about statement testing is CORRECT?

Select ONE option.

options.a: When 100% statement coverage is achieved, all defects in the code have been detected
options.b: In statement testing, the coverage items are the decision outcomes in the code
options.c: 100% statement coverage always implies 100% branch coverage
options.d: When 100% statement coverage is achieved, every executable statement has been executed at least once, but not every decision outcome has necessarily been exercised

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Executing a statement does not guarantee that a defect in it causes a failure, e.g. data-dependent defects.
b) Is not correct. Coverage items in statement testing are executable statements; decision outcomes relate to branch testing.
c) Is not correct. It is the other way round: 100% branch coverage implies 100% statement coverage.
d) Is correct. Statement coverage ensures each executable statement is executed, but e.g. the 'false' outcome of an IF without ELSE may never be taken.

stem:
Consider the following pseudocode:

```
read amount, isVip
if amount > 1000 then
    fee = 0
else
    fee = 5
endif
if isVip then
    fee = fee / 2
endif
print fee
```

A single test has been executed with amount = 1500 and isVip = true.

Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

Select ONE option.

options.a: At least one more test, with amount of at most 1000, is needed to achieve 100% statement coverage
options.b: The test achieves 100% statement coverage because both IF statements were executed
options.c: A test with isVip = false is needed to achieve 100% statement coverage
options.d: 100% statement coverage requires testing all four combinations of the two decisions

explanation:
a) Is correct. Only a test with amount ≤ 1000 executes 'fee = 5'; the second decision does not need its false outcome for statement coverage.
b) Is not correct. The statement 'fee = 5' in the ELSE part was not executed.
c) Is not correct. The second IF has no ELSE, so the false outcome executes no additional statement; it matters for branch coverage, not statement coverage.
d) Is not correct. Two tests are enough for 100% statement coverage, e.g. (1500, true) and (500, true).

stem:
A function computes an average as total / count. The unit tests achieve 100% statement coverage of the function and all pass. In production, the function fails when count is 0.

Which of the following is the BEST explanation of why statement testing did not reveal this defect?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Statement coverage tools cannot measure arithmetic statements
options.b: The defect is in a statement that was never executed by the tests
options.c: Executing a statement does not guarantee that defects in it are detected, as some defects only cause failures with specific data values
options.d: 100% statement coverage can only be achieved when all decision outcomes are exercised

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Coverage tools measure arithmetic statements like any other executable statement.
b) Is not correct. With 100% statement coverage, the division statement was executed.
c) Is correct. The division was executed, but only with non-zero counts; statement coverage does not require specific data values.
d) Is not correct. This is a requirement of branch coverage, not of statement coverage, and would not have required count = 0 anyway.

stem: Which of the following statements about branch testing is CORRECT?

options.a: If a program includes only unconditional branches, then 100% branch coverage can be achieved without executing any test cases
options.b: If the test cases exercise all unconditional branches in the code, then 100% branch coverage is achieved
options.c: If 100% statement coverage is achieved, then 100% branch coverage is also achieved
options.d: If 100% branch coverage is achieved, then all decision outcomes in each decision statement in the code are exercised

explanation:
a) Is not correct. One test case is still needed since there is at least one (unconditional) branch to be covered.
b) Is not correct. Covering only unconditional branches does not imply covering all conditional branches.
c) Is not correct. 100% branch coverage implies 100% statement coverage, not the other way round. E.g., for an IF without ELSE, one test achieves 100% statement coverage but only 50% branch coverage.
d) Is correct. Each decision outcome corresponds to a conditional branch, so 100% branch coverage implies 100% coverage of decision outcomes.

stem:
Let the branch coverage metric be defined as BCov = (X / Y) * 100%.

What do X and Y represent in this formula?

options.a:
X = number of decision outcomes exercised by the test cases
Y = total number of decision outcomes in the code
options.b:
X = number of conditional branches exercised by the test cases
Y = total number of branches in the code
options.c:
X = number of branches exercised by the test cases
Y = total number of branches in the code
options.d:
X = number of conditional branches exercised by the test cases
Y = total number of decision outcomes in the code

explanation:
Branch testing is a white-box test technique in which the coverage items are branches. A branch is a transfer of control between two nodes in the control flow graph; it can be unconditional (straight-line code) or conditional (a decision outcome). Coverage is the number of branches exercised by the test cases divided by the total number of branches, expressed as a percentage.
a) Is not correct. A decision outcome is a conditional branch; for branch testing, X counts not only conditional but also unconditional branches.
b) Is not correct. Branch coverage counts not only conditional, but also unconditional branches.
c) Is correct. Branch coverage is the number of branches exercised by the test cases divided by the total number of branches, expressed as a percentage.
d) Is not correct. Both X and Y count only conditional branches and ignore unconditional branches.

stem:
You want to apply branch testing to the code represented by the following control flow graph.

How many coverage items do you need to test?
figure:
Control flow graph with 7 unlabeled nodes (numbered here N1-N7 for reference) and 8 directed edges:
1. N1 -> N2 (entry node to the decision node of a loop)
2. N2 -> N3 (loop body)
3. N3 -> N2 (back edge closing the loop)
4. N2 -> N4 (loop exit)
5. N4 -> N5 (if-branch)
6. N4 -> N6 (else-branch)
7. N5 -> N7
8. N6 -> N7 (N7 is the exit node)
N2 and N4 are decision nodes (two outgoing edges each); all other nodes have at most one outgoing edge.
explanation:
In branch testing the coverage items are branches, which are represented by the edges of a control flow graph. There are 8 edges in the control flow graph.
Thus: c) Is correct. a), b), d) Are not correct.

stem:
Which TWO of the following statements about branch testing are correct?

Select TWO options.

options.a: Branches include both conditional and unconditional transfers of control between nodes of the control flow graph
options.b: Achieving 100% branch coverage implies achieving 100% statement coverage
options.c: Achieving 100% statement coverage implies achieving 100% branch coverage
options.d: In branch testing, the coverage items are the executable statements
options.e: A single test case can never achieve 100% branch coverage of code that contains a decision

explanation:
a) Is correct. A branch is any transfer of control between two nodes; conditional branches correspond to decision outcomes.
b) Is correct. Every statement lies on some branch, so exercising all branches executes all statements; the opposite is not true.
c) Is not correct. An IF without ELSE can be fully statement-covered by one test while its false branch remains unexercised.
d) Is not correct. The coverage items in branch testing are branches.
e) Is not correct. A loop decision can take both outcomes within one test case (iterate, then exit), so one test can be enough.

stem:
Consider the following pseudocode:

```
read temperature
if temperature > 30 then
    switchFanOn()
endif
log(temperature)
```

A single test is executed with temperature = 35.

Which of the following statements is CORRECT?

Select ONE option.

options.a: The test achieves 100% branch coverage, because all statements are executed
options.b: The test achieves neither 100% statement coverage nor 100% branch coverage
options.c: A single test with temperature = 30 would achieve both 100% statement and 100% branch coverage
options.d: The test achieves 100% statement coverage but not 100% branch coverage, because the false outcome of the decision is not exercised

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Executing all statements does not mean all branches are exercised.
b) Is not correct. All statements, including switchFanOn(), are executed, so statement coverage is 100%.
c) Is not correct. With 30 the decision is false, so switchFanOn() is not executed and the true branch is not covered.
d) Is correct. All statements are executed, but the branch taken when temperature ≤ 30 is not.

stem:
The control flow graph of a component has the following nodes (N1–N8) and directed edges:

• N1 → N2
• N2 → N3 and N2 → N4 (N2 is an IF decision)
• N3 → N5 and N4 → N5
• N5 → N6 and N5 → N7 (N5 is the decision of a WHILE loop)
• N6 → N5 (end of the loop body)
• N7 → N8 (N8 is the exit node)

How many branches must be exercised to achieve 100% branch coverage, and how many of them are conditional branches?

Select ONE option.

options.a: 9 branches, 4 of them conditional
options.b: 8 branches, 4 of them conditional
options.c: 9 branches, 5 of them conditional
options.d: 4 branches, 4 of them conditional

explanation:
In branch testing the coverage items are branches, i.e. the edges of the control flow graph.
a) Is correct. Each edge of the control flow graph is a branch: 9 in total; the 4 outgoing edges of the decision nodes N2 and N5 are conditional.
b) Is not correct. There are 9 edges; the back edge N6 → N5 or the edge N7 → N8 has probably been missed.
c) Is not correct. Only the outgoing edges of the two decision nodes (2 + 2) are conditional.
d) Is not correct. Branch coverage counts unconditional branches as well, not only decision outcomes.

stem: Which of the following is NOT true for white-box testing?

options.a: During white-box testing the entire software implementation is considered
options.b: White-box coverage metrics can help identify additional tests to increase code coverage
options.c: White-box test techniques can be used in static testing
options.d: White-box testing can help identify gaps in requirements implementation

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The fundamental strength of white-box test techniques is that the entire software implementation is taken into account during testing.
b) Is not correct. White-box coverage measures provide an objective measure of coverage and the information needed to generate additional tests to increase it.
c) Is not correct. White-box test techniques can be used to perform reviews (static testing).
d) Is correct. This is the weakness of white-box test techniques: they cannot identify missing implementation, because they are based solely on the test object structure, not on the requirements specification.

stem: How can white-box testing be useful in support of black-box testing?

options.a: White-box coverage measures can help testers evaluate black-box tests in terms of the code coverage achieved by these black-box tests
options.b: White-box coverage analysis can help testers identify unreachable fragments of the source code
options.c: Branch testing subsumes black-box test techniques, so achieving full branch coverage guarantees achieving full coverage of any black-box technique
options.d: White-box test techniques can provide coverage items for black-box techniques

explanation:
a) Is correct. Performing only black-box testing does not provide a measure of actual code coverage. White-box coverage measures provide an objective measurement of coverage and provide the information to allow additional tests to be generated to increase this coverage, and subsequently increase confidence in the code.
b) Is not correct. This statement is correct, but it has nothing to do with black-box testing.
c) Is not correct. In general there are no relationships between white-box test techniques and black-box test techniques.
d) Is not correct. White-box test techniques design tests based on the test object itself, while black-box test techniques design tests based on the specification. Therefore, there is no relation between coverage items derived from these two types of test techniques.

stem: Why does white-box testing facilitate defect detection even when the software specification is vague, outdated or incomplete?

options.a: Test cases are designed based on the structure of the test object rather than the specification
options.b: For each white-box test technique the coverage can be well-defined and easily measured
options.c: White-box test techniques are very well designed to detect omissions in the requirements
options.d: White-box test techniques can be used in both static testing and dynamic testing

explanation:
a) Is correct. A fundamental strength of all white-box test techniques is that the entire software implementation is taken into account during testing, which facilitates defect detection even when the specification is vague, outdated or incomplete. White-box testing can find defects such as an extra feature added to the code (accidentally or deliberately) that is not supposed to be there, which black-box testing cannot detect.
b) Is not correct. The fact that the coverage can be precisely defined is not the right reason. The achieved level of coverage would have much more impact than the possibility to measure the coverage.
c) Is not correct. If the software does not implement one or more requirements, white-box testing is unlikely to detect the resulting defects of omission.
d) Is not correct. While this is true, there is no connection between the capability to be used in both static and dynamic testing and the claim that white-box testing facilitates defect detection with poor specifications.

stem:
Which of the following is a benefit of white-box test techniques?

Select ONE option.

options.a: They reliably detect requirements that have not been implemented at all
options.b: The entire implementation is taken into account, which supports defect detection even when the specification is vague or outdated
options.c: They can be applied without any knowledge of the code or its structure
options.d: Achieving full structural coverage proves that the code is free of defects

explanation:
a) Is not correct. This is a weakness: if a requirement is not implemented, there is no code to cover, so white-box testing may miss the omission.
b) Is correct. Because tests are derived from the code itself, white-box testing is useful even with an inadequate specification.
c) Is not correct. White-box techniques require knowledge of the internal structure.
d) Is not correct. Coverage measures thoroughness; it cannot prove the absence of defects (testing shows the presence of defects).

stem:
A team relies only on black-box testing for a safety-related component. A reviewer recommends adding white-box testing and measuring code coverage.

Which of the following is the BEST justification for this recommendation?

Select ONE option.

options.a: White-box testing will replace the need for acceptance testing by business representatives
options.b: White-box testing can detect defects of omission, which black-box testing cannot find
options.c: Black-box testing alone cannot measure how much of the actual code has been exercised, so some code may remain untested
options.d: White-box testing requires no further test design once a coverage tool is installed

explanation:
a) Is not correct. White-box testing does not validate business needs.
b) Is not correct. The reverse is closer to the truth: missing functionality is a weakness of white-box testing.
c) Is correct. Code coverage gives an objective measurement of thoroughness that black-box testing cannot provide.
d) Is not correct. Tests still have to be designed; a tool only measures coverage.

stem:
Which of the following statements about the use of white-box test techniques is CORRECT?

Select ONE option.

options.a: They can only be used in dynamic testing, because coverage requires the code to be executed
options.b: They are suitable mainly for acceptance testing, because they focus on business processes
options.c: They make black-box techniques unnecessary once 100% branch coverage has been achieved
options.d: They can also be used in static testing, e.g. during dry runs of code or when reviewing pseudocode that is not yet ready for execution

explanation:
a) Is not correct. White-box techniques can also be used in static testing.
b) Is not correct. Their focus is the internal structure, typically at the component level.
c) Is not correct. Branch coverage says nothing about missing requirements; black-box testing remains necessary.
d) Is correct. White-box techniques can be applied in static testing, for example dry runs of code, pseudocode or other logic that can be modeled with a control flow graph.

stem: Which of the following BEST describes the concept behind error guessing?

options.a: Error guessing involves using your knowledge and experience of defects found in the past and typical errors made by developers
options.b: Error guessing involves using your personal experience of development and the errors you made as a developer
options.c: Error guessing requires you to imagine that you are the user of the test object and to guess errors the user could make interacting with it
options.d: Error guessing requires you to rapidly duplicate the development task to identify the sort of errors a developer might make

explanation:
a) Is correct. The basic concept behind error guessing is that the tester tries to guess what errors may have been made by the developer and what defects may be in the test object based on past experience (and sometimes checklists).
b) Is not correct. Although a tester who used to be a developer may use their personal experience, the technique is not based on prior knowledge of development.
c) Is not correct. Error guessing is not a usability technique for guessing how users may fail to interact with the test object.
d) Is not correct. Duplicating the development task is impractical (equivalent skills, time) and is not error guessing.

stem:
Consider the following list:
- Correct input not accepted
- Incorrect input accepted
- Wrong output format
- Division by zero

What test technique is MOST PROBABLY used by the tester who uses this list when performing testing?

options.a: Exploratory testing
options.b: Fault attack
options.c: Checklist-based testing
options.d: Boundary value analysis

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Exploratory testing uses test charters, not a list of possible defects/failures. Although exploratory testing can incorporate other test techniques, a fault attack is the most likely option here.
b) Is correct. This is a list of possible failures. Fault attacks are a methodical approach to the implementation of error guessing and require the tester to create or acquire a list of possible errors, defects and failures, and to design tests that will identify defects associated with the errors, expose the defects, or cause the failures.
c) Is not correct. Both error guessing and checklist-based testing use such lists; however, the list here is of possible failures, not test conditions, and so the MOST PROBABLE test technique is fault attack.
d) Is not correct. BVA is based on an analysis of boundary values of equivalence partitions. The list does not mention equivalence partitions or their boundaries.

stem: Which of the following is NOT anticipated by the tester while applying error guessing?

options.a: The developer misunderstood the formula in the user story for calculating the interest
options.b: The developer wrote "FA = A*(1+IR^N)" instead of "FA = A*(1+IR)^N" in the source code
options.c: The developer missed the seminar on new compound interest rate legislation
options.d: The accuracy of the interest calculated by the system is not precise enough

explanation:
Error guessing is about anticipating the errors, defects and failures based on the tester's knowledge.
a) Is not correct. This is an example of anticipating the developer's error.
b) Is not correct. This is an example of anticipating the defect.
c) Is correct. This is an example of a potential root cause of a defect, which is neither an error, defect nor failure, and difficult for the tester to anticipate.
d) Is not correct. This is an example of anticipating a failure, perhaps based on experience of previous systems in this application domain.

stem:
Which of the following BEST describes error guessing?

Select ONE option.

options.a: A technique in which the tester anticipates errors, defects and failures based on knowledge such as past failures, typical developer errors and failures in similar applications
options.b: A technique in which tests are derived from the partitions of the input domain specified in the requirements
options.c: A technique in which a tester simultaneously designs, executes and evaluates tests while learning about the test object
options.d: A technique in which tests are designed to cover a list of test conditions defined in advance

explanation:
a) Is correct. This is the definition of error guessing.
b) Is not correct. This describes equivalence partitioning.
c) Is not correct. This describes exploratory testing.
d) Is not correct. This describes checklist-based testing.

stem:
A tester is about to test a new file-upload function. Which of the following activities is an example of a fault attack?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Running the tests of the previous release unchanged to check that nothing has been broken
options.b: Compiling a list of likely errors and failures (e.g. empty file, huge file, unsupported file type, name with special characters) and designing tests to provoke each of them
options.c: Measuring which branches of the upload code have been exercised by the existing tests
options.d: Asking the product owner to confirm the acceptance criteria of the upload user story

explanation:
a) Is not correct. This is regression testing.
b) Is correct. A fault attack is a methodical approach to error guessing: create a list of possible errors, defects and failures and design tests to expose them.
c) Is not correct. This is branch coverage measurement (white-box).
d) Is not correct. This relates to collaboration-based approaches, not error guessing.

stem:
Which of the following are typical sources of knowledge used for error guessing?

i. How the application has worked in the past
ii. The types of errors developers tend to make
iii. Failures that have occurred in similar applications
iv. The statement coverage achieved by the unit tests
v. The number of test cases per requirement in the traceability matrix

Select ONE option.

options.a: i, iv, v
options.b: ii, iii, iv
options.c: i, ii, iii
options.d: i, iii, v

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Coverage achieved (iv) and test case counts (v) are measurements, not knowledge about likely errors.
b) Is not correct. Statement coverage (iv) is a white-box measurement, not a source for error guessing.
c) Is correct. Error guessing builds on knowledge of past behavior (i), typical developer errors (ii) and failures in similar applications (iii).
d) Is not correct. The number of test cases per requirement (v) says nothing about likely errors.

stem:
In your project there has been a delay in the release of a brand-new application and test execution started late, but you have very detailed domain knowledge and good analytical skills. The full list of requirements has not yet been shared with the team, but management is asking for some test results to be presented.

Which test technique fits BEST in this situation?

options.a: Checklist-based testing
options.b: Error guessing
options.c: Exploratory testing
options.d: Branch testing

explanation:
a) Is not correct. This is a new product. You probably do not have a checklist yet and test conditions might not be known due to missing requirements.
b) Is not correct. This is a new product. You probably do not have enough information to make correct error guesses.
c) Is correct. Exploratory testing is most useful when there are few known specifications and/or there is a pressing timeline for testing.
d) Is not correct. Branch testing is time-consuming, and management is asking for results now. Also, branch testing does not involve domain knowledge.

stem: Which TWO of the following statements provide the BEST rationale for using exploratory testing?

options.a: Testers have not been allocated enough time for test design and test execution
options.b: The existing test strategy requires that testers use formal, black-box test techniques
options.c: The specification is written in a formal language that can be processed by a tool
options.d: Testers are the members of an agile team and have good programming skills
options.e: Testers are experienced in the business domain and have good analytical skills

explanation:
Exploratory testing is useful when there are few or inadequate specifications or there is significant time pressure on the testing. It is also useful to complement other more formal test techniques. It will be more effective if the tester is experienced, has domain knowledge and has a high degree of essential skills, like analytical skills, curiosity and creativeness.
a) Is correct. Exploratory testing is useful when there is significant time pressure on the testing.
b) Is not correct. Exploratory testing is not a black-box test technique.
c) Is not correct. Exploratory testing is useful when the specifications are poorly written.
d) Is not correct. Programming skills have nothing to do with exploratory testing in principle.
e) Is correct. Exploratory testing will be more effective if the tester is experienced, has domain knowledge and good analytical skills.

stem: Which of the following is true about exploratory testing?

options.a: Test cases are designed before the exploratory testing session starts
options.b: The tester can perform test execution, but cannot perform test design
options.c: Exploratory testing results are good predictors of the number of remaining defects
options.d: During exploratory testing the tester may use black-box test techniques

explanation:
a) Is not correct. In exploratory testing, test cases are usually created during the exploratory testing session, alongside test analysis, test implementation and test execution.
b) Is not correct. In exploratory testing, tests are simultaneously designed, executed, and evaluated while the tester learns about the test object.
c) Is not correct. Exploratory test results depend heavily on the tester's experience. Even if they can be used as a predictor of risk and to assess whether there will be fewer or more defects compared to the previous session, they are not reliable defect prediction models that can predict the number of remaining defects.
d) Is correct. During exploratory testing, the testers can use any test techniques that they find useful.

stem:
In which of the following situations is exploratory testing MOST useful?

Select ONE option.

options.a: When the specification is detailed and complete and tests must be repeatable for regulatory audits
options.b: When the goal is to achieve a precisely measured level of branch coverage
options.c: When testers have no domain knowledge and no experience with similar applications
options.d: When there are few or inadequate specifications or significant time pressure on testing

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Detailed specifications and repeatability requirements favor scripted, systematic techniques.
b) Is not correct. Branch coverage is measured with white-box testing.
c) Is not correct. Exploratory testing is most effective with experienced testers who have domain knowledge.
d) Is correct. Exploratory testing is useful when specifications are sparse or inadequate or when time pressure is high, and to complement more formal techniques.

stem:
Which of the following BEST describes session-based exploratory testing?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Testing is done within a defined time-box, guided by a test charter with test objectives, and followed by a debriefing
options.b: The tester follows a detailed test script prepared in advance and records deviations from the expected results
options.c: A developer measures code coverage after each test session to decide which tests to automate
options.d: The tester creates a checklist of test conditions and checks each one without designing further tests

explanation:
a) Is correct. Session-based exploratory testing uses time-boxed sessions, a test charter and a debriefing between tester and stakeholders.
b) Is not correct. This is scripted testing, not exploratory testing.
c) Is not correct. This has nothing to do with session-based exploratory testing.
d) Is not correct. This describes checklist-based testing.

stem:
During a 90-minute exploratory session on a booking app, a tester notices that the "number of guests" field accepts unusual values. She briefly applies boundary value analysis to this field before continuing her exploration.

Which statement about this approach is CORRECT?

Select ONE option.

options.a: This is wrong: formal test techniques must not be used during exploratory testing
options.b: This is acceptable: exploratory testing can incorporate other test techniques, such as boundary value analysis
options.c: This turns the session into scripted testing, so the results must not be documented
options.d: This is acceptable only if the test cases were specified in full detail before the session started

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The syllabus explicitly allows other techniques within exploratory testing.
b) Is correct. Exploratory testing may use other black-box, white-box or experience-based techniques within the session.
c) Is not correct. Using a technique does not make testing scripted, and session results are documented (e.g. session sheets).
d) Is not correct. In exploratory testing tests are designed, executed and evaluated simultaneously.

stem: You are testing a mobile application that allows customers to access and manage their bank accounts. You are running a test suite that involves evaluating each screen, and each field on each screen, against a general list of user interface best practices derived from a popular book on the topic that maximizes usability for such applications. Which of the following options BEST categorizes the test technique you are using?

options.a: Black-box
options.b: Exploratory
options.c: Checklist-based
options.d: Error guessing

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The book provides general guidance, and is not a formal requirements document, a specification, or a set of use cases, user stories, or business processes.
b) Is not correct. While you could consider the list as a set of test charters, it more closely resembles a list of test conditions to be checked.
c) Is correct. The list of user interface best practices is the list of test conditions to be systematically checked.
d) Is not correct. The tests are not focused on failures that could occur, but on knowledge about what is important for the user in terms of usability.

stem: Which of the following BEST fits as an element of the checklist used in checklist-based testing?

options.a: “The developer made an error when implementing the code”
options.b: “The achieved statement coverage exceeds 85%”
options.c: “The program works correctly regarding functional and non-functional requirements”
options.d: “The error messages are written in language that the user can understand”

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Checklists should contain test conditions to be verified. This is an example of an error, not a test condition, and is too general.
b) Is not correct. Checklists should not contain items better suited as exit criteria. This is an example of an exit criterion.
c) Is not correct. Checklists should not contain items that are too general. This item practically describes a test objective.
d) Is correct. This is an example of a test condition that can be checked by a human.

stem: Which of the following BEST describes how using checklist-based testing can result in increased coverage?

options.a: Checklist items can be defined at a sufficiently low level of detail, so the tester can implement and execute detailed test cases based on these items
options.b: Checklists can be automated, so each time an automated test execution covers the checklist items, it results in additional coverage
options.c: Each checklist item should be tested separately and independently, so the elements cover different areas of the software
options.d: Two testers designing and executing tests based on the same high-level checklist items will typically perform the testing in slightly different ways

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The tester can implement and execute detailed test cases based on the checklist, but this does not explain how it would result in increased coverage.
b) Is not correct. Checklist items should not be automated. Even if they are, automated test scripts always execute the tests in the same way, which usually does not result in increased coverage.
c) Is not correct. Testing each checklist item separately and independently impacts the test execution order, not the achieved coverage.
d) Is correct. If the checklists are high-level, some variability in the actual testing is likely to occur, resulting in potentially greater coverage but less repeatability. Two testers may use different test data, test steps, etc., so one tester will probably cover some areas not covered by the other.

stem:
A tester prepares a checklist for checklist-based testing of web forms. Which of the following items is MOST appropriate for this checklist?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Is the overall quality of the form good enough?
options.b: Has the static analysis tool reported zero warnings?
options.c: Does every mandatory field display an error message when it is left empty?
options.d: Have all entry criteria for system testing been fulfilled?

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Too general; checklist items should be checkable separately and directly.
b) Is not correct. Items that can be checked automatically should not be in the checklist.
c) Is correct. A specific question that can be checked separately and directly.
d) Is not correct. Entry and exit criteria should not be included in a test checklist.

stem:
Which of the following statements about checklist-based testing is CORRECT?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Checklists should contain as many items as possible to guarantee full coverage
options.b: Checklist-based testing can only be used for non-functional testing
options.c: Once created, a checklist should remain unchanged so that results stay comparable
options.d: High-level checklists lead to some variability in the actual testing, which may result in greater coverage but less repeatability

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Checklists should not be too long.
b) Is not correct. Checklists can support both functional and non-functional testing.
c) Is not correct. Checklists should be updated regularly based on defect analysis.
d) Is correct. Without detailed test cases, testers interpret high-level items differently, which increases coverage but reduces repeatability.

stem:
A team has used the same checklist for testing invoices for two years. Recently, testing with this checklist has found hardly any defects, although customers still report invoice failures.

Which of the following is the MOST likely explanation and the appropriate response?

Select ONE option.

options.a: The developers have learned to avoid the errors on the checklist; the checklist should be updated based on analysis of recent defects
options.b: Checklist-based testing is not suited to invoices; the team should switch to white-box testing only
options.c: The checklist is too short; the team should add all test cases from the test management tool to it
options.d: The customers are using the system incorrectly; no change to the checklist is needed

explanation:
a) Is correct. Checklists can become less effective over time as developers avoid the same errors; they should be refreshed based on defect analysis.
b) Is not correct. Nothing indicates the technique is unsuitable; dropping it and relying only on white-box testing would miss defects of omission.
c) Is not correct. Checklists should not become long lists of test cases.
d) Is not correct. Customer-reported failures indicate gaps in testing that should be analyzed.

stem: Which of the following BEST describe the collaborative approach to user story writing?

options.a: User stories are created by testers and developers and then accepted by business representatives
options.b: User stories are created by business representatives, developers, and testers together
options.c: User stories are created by business representatives and verified by developers and testers
options.d: User stories are created in a way that they are independent, negotiable, valuable, estimable, small, and testable

explanation:
Collaborative user story writing means that all stakeholders create the user stories collaboratively, to obtain a shared vision. Thus b) is correct and a) and c) are not.
d) Is not correct. This is the list of properties (INVEST) each user story should have, not the description of the collaboration-based approach.

stem: Which collaborative user story writing practice enables the team to achieve a collective understanding of what needs to be delivered?

options.a: Planning poker, so that a team can achieve consensus on the effort needed to implement a user story
options.b: Reviews, so that a team can detect inconsistencies and contradictions in a user story
options.c: Iteration planning, so that user stories with the highest business value for a customer can be prioritized for implementation
options.d: Conversation, so that team members can understand how the software will be used

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Planning poker can estimate effort for a user story that is already written. It does not help in understanding what should be delivered.
b) Is not correct. Reviews are not a collaborative user story writing practice.
c) Is not correct. Iteration planning is a project-related practice, used to plan the work, not to understand what needs to be delivered.
d) Is correct. Conversation explains how the software will be used and often allows the team to define meaningful acceptance criteria, thus obtaining a shared vision of what should be delivered.

stem:
User stories are often described using the "3 C's". Which of the following correctly describes the "Conversation" aspect?

Select ONE option.

options.a: The medium describing the user story, such as an index card or an entry in an electronic board
options.b: The discussion, documented or verbal, in which business representatives, developers and testers explain how the software will be used
options.c: The acceptance criteria that confirm the story has been implemented correctly
options.d: The formal sign-off of the user story by the product owner at the end of the iteration

explanation:
a) Is not correct. This describes the Card.
b) Is correct. Conversation explains how the software will be used and can be documented or verbal.
c) Is not correct. This describes the Confirmation.
d) Is not correct. Sign-off is not one of the 3 C's.

stem:
During backlog refinement, a business representative proposes the user story: "As a customer, I want the checkout to be user-friendly, so that I enjoy shopping." The tester points out that nobody could decide whether the implemented story is done.

Which INVEST characteristic does the tester consider to be violated, and what is the BEST way to address it?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Independent – the story should be split so that it no longer depends on other stories
options.b: Small – the story should be estimated in story points before discussing it further
options.c: Testable – the team should agree together on concrete, verifiable acceptance criteria, e.g. a maximum number of steps to complete checkout
options.d: Valuable – the developer should rewrite the story alone in technical terms

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The concern is not dependency between stories but the lack of verifiable criteria.
b) Is not correct. Size is not the issue raised; estimation does not make the story verifiable.
c) Is correct. A story is testable when clear acceptance criteria exist; writing them collaboratively (business, development, testing) addresses this.
d) Is not correct. The value is stated; user stories should be written collaboratively and from the user's perspective, not technically by one person.

stem: Which of the following BEST describes the way acceptance criteria can be documented?

options.a: Performing retrospectives to determine the actual needs of the stakeholders regarding a given user story
options.b: Using the given/when/then format to describe an example test condition related to a given user story
options.c: Using verbal communication to reduce the risk of misunderstanding the acceptance criteria by others
options.d: Documenting risks related to a given user story in a test plan to facilitate the risk-based testing of a given user story

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Retrospectives are used to capture lessons learned and improve the development and testing process, not to document acceptance criteria.
b) Is correct. This is the standard way to document acceptance criteria.
c) Is not correct. Verbal communication does not physically document the acceptance criteria as part of a user story (the “card” aspect in the 3C’s model).
d) Is not correct. Acceptance criteria are related to a user story, not a test plan; they are conditions to be fulfilled to decide if the user story is complete. Risks are not such conditions.

stem:
Consider the following acceptance criteria for a user story written from the perspective of an online store owner.

Given that the user is logged in and on the homepage,
When the user clicks on the "Add Item" button,
Then the "Create Item" form should appear,
And the user should be able to input a name and price for the new item.

In what format is this acceptance criteria written?

options.a: Rule-oriented
options.b: Scenario-oriented
options.c: Product-oriented
options.d: Process-oriented

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The rule-oriented format includes bullet-point verification lists or tabulated input-output mappings. Given/When/Then is scenario-oriented because it describes a scenario to be verified.
b) Is correct. This is a Given/When/Then format, which is scenario-oriented.
c) Is not correct. There is no "product-oriented" format of acceptance criteria.
d) Is not correct. There is no "process-oriented" format of acceptance criteria.

stem: Which of the following provides the BEST example of a scenario-oriented acceptance criterion?

options.a: The application must allow users to delete their account and all associated data upon request
options.b: When a customer adds an item to their cart and proceeds to checkout, they should be prompted to log in or create an account if they haven't already done so
options.c: IF (contain(product(23).Name, cart.products())) THEN return FALSE
options.d: The website must comply with the ICT Accessibility 508 Standards and ensure that all content is accessible to users with disabilities

explanation:
a) Is not correct. This describes what rules or regulations the system must adhere to (the right to be forgotten). This is a rule-oriented acceptance criterion.
b) Is correct. This acceptance criterion describes an example scenario that must be realized by the system. This is a scenario-oriented acceptance criterion.
c) Is not correct. This looks like a line of code implementing a business rule. Acceptance criteria should be written in language business representatives understand.
d) Is not correct. This describes rules or regulations the system must adhere to and how compliance will be ensured - a rule-oriented acceptance criterion.

stem:
Which of the following acceptance criteria is written in the scenario-oriented format?

Select ONE option.

options.a:
• Password has at least 10 characters
• Password contains at least one digit
• Password is not equal to the user name
options.b:
| Order value | Shipping fee |
|---|---|
| < 50 EUR | 4.90 EUR |
| ≥ 50 EUR | 0 EUR |
options.c: The checkout page shall be implemented in the existing payment microservice
options.d: Given a registered user with a locked account, when the user requests a password reset, then a reset link is sent to the registered e-mail address

explanation:
a) Is not correct. This is a bullet-point verification list, a rule-oriented format.
b) Is not correct. A tabulated input-output mapping is a rule-oriented format.
c) Is not correct. This is a design constraint, not an acceptance criterion in either common format.
d) Is correct. The Given/When/Then structure (used in BDD) is the scenario-oriented format.

stem:
Which of the following are purposes of acceptance criteria?

i. Defining the scope of the user story
ii. Reaching consensus among the stakeholders
iii. Replacing the need for test cases
iv. Providing the basis for the user story acceptance testing
v. Specifying the internal design of the implementation

Select ONE option.

options.a: i, ii, iv
options.b: i, iii, v
options.c: ii, iii, iv
options.d: i, iv, v

explanation:
a) Is correct. Acceptance criteria define scope (i), help reach consensus (ii) and form the basis for acceptance testing (iv).
b) Is not correct. Acceptance criteria do not replace test cases (iii) and do not define the internal design (v).
c) Is not correct. Acceptance criteria are the basis for test cases, not a replacement for them (iii).
d) Is not correct. Specifying the internal design (v) is not a purpose of acceptance criteria.

stem:
Match the following acceptance criteria examples (1–4) with their format (A–B):

1. "Given the cart is empty, when the user opens the checkout, then the message 'Your cart is empty' is shown"
2. A table mapping each customer category to its discount percentage
3. A bulleted list: "Login fails after 3 wrong passwords; account unlocks after 30 minutes; user is informed by e-mail"
4. "Given the user is logged in, when the session is idle for 15 minutes, then the user is logged out"

A. Scenario-oriented
B. Rule-oriented

Select ONE option.
explanation:
a) Is not correct. A table (2) is rule-oriented, and Given/When/Then (4) is scenario-oriented.
b) Is correct. Given/When/Then examples (1, 4) are scenario-oriented; the tabulated mapping (2) and the bulleted verification list (3) are rule-oriented.
c) Is not correct. Given/When/Then (1) is scenario-oriented and a bullet list (3) is rule-oriented.
d) Is not correct. A bulleted verification list (3) is rule-oriented and Given/When/Then (4) is scenario-oriented.

stem:
Which of the following statements about the format of acceptance criteria is CORRECT?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Only the Given/When/Then format may be used when the team applies ATDD
options.b: Rule-oriented acceptance criteria must always be written as bullet points; tables are not allowed
options.c: Teams may use a custom format, as long as the acceptance criteria are well-defined and unambiguous
options.d: Acceptance criteria should be written by business representatives after the story has been implemented

explanation:
a) Is not correct. ATDD does not prescribe a single format.
b) Is not correct. A tabulated input-output mapping is one of the rule-oriented forms.
c) Is correct. Most criteria fit the scenario- or rule-oriented format, but other formats are acceptable if well-defined and unambiguous.
d) Is not correct. Acceptance criteria are defined collaboratively, before implementation.

stem:
Consider the following user story:

As an Editor
I want to review content before it is published
so that I can ensure the grammar is correct

and its acceptance criteria:

• The user can log in to the content management system with "Editor" role
• The editor can view existing content pages
• The editor can edit the page content
• The editor can add markup comments
• The editor can save changes
• The editor can reassign to the "content owner" role to make updates

Which of the following is the BEST example of an ATDD test for this user story?

options.a: Test if the editor can save the document after edit the page content
options.b: Test if the content owner can log in and make updates to the content
options.c: Test if the editor can schedule the edited content for publication
options.d: Test if the editor can reassign to another editor to make updates

explanation:
a) Is correct. This test covers two acceptance criteria: one about editing the document and one about saving changes.
b) Is not correct. Acceptance criteria cover the editor activities, not the content owner activities.
c) Is not correct. Scheduling the edited content for publication may be a nice feature, but it is not covered by the acceptance criteria.
d) Is not correct. Acceptance criteria state reassigning from an editor to the content owner, not to another editor.

stem:
Your team analyzes the following user story in order to define the acceptance criteria:

As a registered customer, I want to be able to view my previous orders on the company's website, so that I can keep track of my purchases.

Which of the following test cases will NOT be relevant for this user story?

options.a:
Input: the customer logs into their account on the website and clicks the “see order history” button
Expected result: the system shows a list of all the customer’s previous orders, including the date, order number, and total cost
options.b:
Input: the customer clicks on an order from the order list
Expected result: the system displays the individual items purchased, along with their prices and quantities
options.c:
Input: the customer clicks “Sort ascending” button on the order history screen
Expected result: the system shows the order history sorted by order number in ascending order
options.d:
Input: an unregistered customer registers as a new customer with a valid e-mail address that does not already exist in the customer database
Expected result: the system accepts the registration and creates the account

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The test case is related to viewing previous orders in the order history.
b) Is not correct. The test case is related to viewing previous orders.
c) Is not correct. The test case is related to viewing previous orders in the order history.
d) Is correct. The test case is related to the registration process, which is not discussed in the user story. The user story is about viewing previous orders.

stem:
You are using acceptance test-driven development and designing test cases based on the following user story:

As a Regular or Special user, I want to be able to use my electronic floor card, to access specific floors.

Acceptance Criteria:
AC1: Regular users have access to floors 1 to 3
AC2: Floor 4 is only accessible to Special users
AC3: Special users have all the access rights of Regular users

Which test case is the MOST reasonable one to test AC3?

options.a: Check that a Regular user can access floors 1 and 3
options.b: Check that a Regular user cannot access floor 4
options.c: Check that a Special user can access floor 5
options.d: Check that a Special user can access floors 1, 2 and 3

explanation:
a) Is not correct. We want to check that Special users have the rights of Regular users, so we need to test access rights for a Special user, not a Regular user.
b) Is not correct. Same reason as a): we need to test a Special user, not a Regular user.
c) Is not correct. There is no floor 5 described in the acceptance criteria; test cases should not extend the scope of the user story. Even as negative testing, this is not directly related to AC3.
d) Is correct. This is the way we can check if a Special user can access floors which are accessible to a Regular user.

stem:
You have just started designing test cases for the following user story.

As a customer,
I want to be able to filter search results by price range, so that I can find products within my budget more easily.

Acceptance criteria:
1. The filter should work for all versions of the application from version 3.0 upwards
2. The filter should allow the customer to set a price range with a minimum and a maximum price
3. The search results should update dynamically as the customer adjusts the price range filter

In all test cases the precondition is as follows: there are only two products available, products A and B. Product A costs $100 and product B costs $110.

Which of the following is the BEST example of a test case for this user story?

options.a: Enter webpage and set filter to show prices between $90 and $100. Expected result: results show product A only. Set maximum price to $110. Expected result: results now include both products A and B
options.b: Enter webpage. Expected result: the default minimum and maximum prices are $100 and $110 respectively. Add product C to stock, with price $120. Refresh the client's webpage. Expected result: the default maximum price changes to $120
options.c: Enter webpage and set filter to show prices between $90 and $115. Expected result: results show both products A and B. Change currency from USD to EUR. Expected result: the filter range changes correctly to EUR values, according to the current exchange rate
options.d: Enter webpage with three different browsers: Edge, Chrome and Opera. In each browser set filter between $90 and $110. Expected result: results include both products A and B and the results layout is the same in all three browsers

explanation:
a) Is correct. This test case is related to acceptance criteria 2 and 3, because it checks if we can set a price range (acceptance criterion 2) and if the results update dynamically after adjusting the price range filter (acceptance criterion 3).
b) Is not correct. This test case is not related to any of the acceptance criteria. It checks if the filter dynamically sets the default minimum and maximum price range, and not that a customer can do it.
c) Is not correct. This test case is not related to any of the acceptance criteria. It checks the currency exchange feature, which is not discussed in this user story.
d) Is not correct. This test case is not related to any of the acceptance criteria. It checks the application's compatibility with different browsers, which is not discussed in this user story.

stem:
Your team uses acceptance test-driven development (ATDD) for the following user story:

As a library member,
I want to renew a borrowed book online,
so that I can avoid late fees.

Acceptance criteria:
AC1: A book can be renewed at most twice.
AC2: A book reserved by another member cannot be renewed.
AC3: Each renewal extends the due date by 14 days, counted from the current due date.

Which of the following test cases is the BEST one to test AC3?

Select ONE option.

options.a: On 5 March, the member renews a book due on 10 March. Expected result: the new due date is 19 March
options.b: The member tries to renew a book that is reserved by another member. Expected result: the renewal is rejected
options.c: The member tries to renew a book for the third time. Expected result: the renewal is rejected
options.d: The member renews a book due on 10 March for the first time. Expected result: the new due date is 24 March

explanation:
a) Is not correct. This counts 14 days from the renewal date, not from the current due date, so the expected result contradicts AC3.
b) Is not correct. This is a valid test, but for AC2, not AC3.
c) Is not correct. This is a valid test, but for AC1, not AC3.
d) Is correct. 10 March + 14 days = 24 March, counted from the current due date as AC3 requires.

stem:
Your team uses ATDD for the following user story:

As a mobile banking user,
I want to set a daily spending limit for my debit card,
so that I can control my expenses.

Acceptance criterion AC1: The daily limit can be set between 50 EUR and 2000 EUR (inclusive) in steps of 10 EUR. Values outside this range are rejected. The input field only accepts multiples of 10.

You derive positive and negative test cases for AC1 using 2-value boundary value analysis.

Which set of limit values should be used?

Select ONE option.
explanation:
With a step of 10 EUR, the partitions are {…, 40} (rejected), {50, …, 2000} (accepted) and {2010, …} (rejected). 2-value BVA gives positive tests 50 and 2000 and negative tests 40 and 2010.
a) Is not correct. The field only accepts multiples of 10, so 49 and 2001 cannot be entered; the closest neighbours are 40 and 2010.
b) Is not correct. These are all valid values; the negative test cases (40 and 2010) are missing.
c) Is not correct. 0 and 2500 are invalid values, but not the boundary values of the invalid partitions.
d) Is correct. The boundary values of the valid partition (50, 2000) and their closest neighbours in the invalid partitions (40, 2010).

stem:
For the debit card user story of your team, the following acceptance criterion has been agreed:

AC2: A card payment that exceeds the remaining daily limit (daily limit minus amount already spent today) is declined, and the user receives a notification. Other payments are accepted.

Which of the following scenarios is a CORRECT test case for AC2?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Given a daily limit of 300 EUR and 250 EUR already spent today, when a payment of 60 EUR is made, then the payment is declined and a notification is sent
options.b: Given a daily limit of 300 EUR and 250 EUR already spent today, when a payment of 50 EUR is made, then the payment is declined and a notification is sent
options.c: Given a daily limit of 300 EUR and 200 EUR already spent today, when a payment of 60 EUR is made, then the payment is declined and a notification is sent
options.d: Given 250 EUR already spent today, when a payment of 40 EUR is made, then the payment is declined and a notification is sent

explanation:
a) Is correct. The remaining limit is 50 EUR; 60 EUR exceeds it, so the payment is declined with a notification.
b) Is not correct. 50 EUR equals the remaining limit of 50 EUR and does not exceed it, so the payment should be accepted.
c) Is not correct. The remaining limit is 100 EUR, so a 60 EUR payment should be accepted.
d) Is not correct. The daily limit is not specified in the Given part, and with the 300 EUR limit a 40 EUR payment would be accepted.

stem:
Your team uses ATDD for the following user story:

As a commuter,
I want to save my favorite train connections in the travel app,
so that I can find them quickly.

Acceptance criteria:
AC1: A logged-in user can save a connection as a favorite from the search results.
AC2: A user can store at most 5 favorites; saving a 6th one shows the message "Favorites list full".
AC3: Favorites are listed on the start screen in the order in which they were saved.

Which of the following test cases is NOT relevant for this user story?

Select ONE option.

options.a: A logged-in user with 5 favorites saves another connection. Expected result: the message "Favorites list full" is shown
options.b: A logged-in user buys a ticket for a saved favorite connection. Expected result: the ticket is issued and paid by credit card
options.c: A logged-in user saves connections A, then B. Expected result: the start screen lists A before B
options.d: A logged-in user saves a connection from the search results. Expected result: the connection appears in the favorites list

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Relevant: this is a negative test for AC2.
b) Is correct. Buying tickets is not part of this user story or its acceptance criteria.
c) Is not correct. Relevant: this tests AC3.
d) Is not correct. Relevant: this tests AC1.

stem:
Consider the following part of a test plan.

> Testing will be performed using component testing and component integration testing. The regulations require to demonstrate that 100% branch coverage is achieved for each component classified as critical.

Which part of the test plan does this part belong to?

options.a: Communication
options.b: Risk register
options.c: Context of testing
options.d: Test approach

explanation: The paragraph contains information on test levels and exit criteria, which are part of the test approach. Thus d) is correct; a), b) and c) are not.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a purpose of a test plan?

options.a: To define test data and expected results for component tests and component integration tests
options.b: To define as exit criteria from the component test level that "100% statement coverage and 100% branch coverage must be achieved"
options.c: To describe what fields the test progress report shall contain and what should be the form of this report
options.d: To explain why system integration testing will be excluded from testing, although the test strategy requires this test level

explanation:
a) Is correct. The test plan may include test data requirements (as part of the test approach), but not the detailed test data for test cases. Test data is part of the test cases, not the test plan. It is also usually impossible to define such data when the test plan is created.
b) Is not correct. A test plan helps ensure that test activities meet established criteria by including entry and exit criteria; code coverage criteria are an example of such criteria for the component test level.
c) Is not correct. Documentation templates are typical content of a test plan, defining a standard way of communicating or reporting.
d) Is not correct. One purpose of a test plan is to demonstrate that testing will adhere to the existing test policy and test strategy, or to explain why testing will deviate from them.

stem:
A test manager is drafting the test plan for the upgrade of a payroll system. Which of the following items would MOST appropriately be documented in the test approach section of that test plan?

Select ONE option.

options.a: The stakeholders of the upgrade and the training they need before testing starts
options.b: The product risks and project risks identified so far, together with their risk levels
options.c: The test levels, test types and test techniques to be used, and the entry criteria and exit criteria
options.d: How often status meetings are held and which templates are used for reporting to the steering committee

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Stakeholders, their roles and their hiring/training needs belong to the stakeholders part of the test plan.
b) Is not correct. Identified risks and their levels are documented in the risk register.
c) Is correct. The test approach covers test levels, test types, test techniques, test deliverables, entry and exit criteria, independence of testing, metrics, and test data and test environment requirements.
d) Is not correct. Meeting frequency and reporting templates belong to the communication part of the test plan.

stem:
Which of the following BEST describes a purpose of a test plan?

Select ONE option.

options.a: To specify, for every test case, the detailed steps, the test data and the expected results
options.b: To document the means and schedule for achieving the test objectives, and to serve as a means of communication with team members and other stakeholders
options.c: To give a final evaluation of the quality of the test object against the exit criteria once testing has ended
options.d: To record which version of every configuration item was used in each test run

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Detailed steps, test data and expected results are documented in test cases and test procedures, not in the test plan.
b) Is correct. A test plan describes the test objectives and how and when they will be achieved, helps ensure the test activities meet the established criteria, and is a communication vehicle for stakeholders.
c) Is not correct. A final evaluation against exit criteria is the content of a test completion report.
d) Is not correct. Recording versions of configuration items is a task of configuration management.

stem: How do testers add value to iteration and release planning?

options.a: Testers determine the priority of the user stories to be developed
options.b: Testers focus only on the functional aspects of the system to be tested
options.c: Testers participate in the detailed risk identification and risk assessment of user stories
options.d: Testers guarantee the release of high-quality software through early test design during the release planning

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Priorities for user stories are determined by the business representative together with the development team.
b) Is not correct. Testers focus on both functional and non-functional aspects of the system to be tested.
c) Is correct. According to the syllabus, this is one of the ways testers add value to iteration and release planning.
d) Is not correct. Early test design is not part of release planning, and it does not automatically guarantee the release of quality software.

stem:
Which of the following is a way in which testers add value to release planning?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Testers decide which user stories are included in the release, based on business value
options.b: Testers implement the unit tests for all user stories planned for the release
options.c: Testers sign off the release as soon as all user stories have been implemented
options.d: Testers take part in writing testable user stories and acceptance criteria

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The content and priority of a release are decided by business representatives (e.g., the product owner) together with the team.
b) Is not correct. Unit tests are normally written by developers, and this is not a release planning activity.
c) Is not correct. Release decisions are not made by testers alone, and implementation alone does not justify a release.
d) Is correct. In release planning, testers participate in writing testable user stories and acceptance criteria, in risk analyses, in test effort estimation and in planning the testing for the release.

stem:
During iteration planning, which of the following contributions is a tester MOST likely to make?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Determining the testability of the user stories selected for the iteration and estimating the effort for the testing tasks
options.b: Setting the business priorities of the user stories in the product backlog
options.c: Agreeing the overall release date with the customer
options.d: Defining the organization's test policy for future projects

explanation:
a) Is correct. In iteration planning testers take part in detailed risk analysis of user stories, determine their testability, break them down into (testing) tasks and estimate the test effort for those tasks.
b) Is not correct. Business priorities are set by the business representatives / product owner.
c) Is not correct. The release date is a release-level business and management decision, not part of iteration planning.
d) Is not correct. The test policy is an organization-level document and is not created during iteration planning.

stem: Which TWO of the following options are the exit criteria for testing a system?

options.a: Test environment readiness
options.b: The ability to log in to the test object by the tester
options.c: Estimated defect density is reached
options.d: Requirements are translated into given/when/then format
options.e: Regression tests are automated

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Test environment readiness is a resource availability criterion; hence it belongs to the entry criteria.
b) Is not correct. This is a resource availability criterion; hence it belongs to the entry criteria.
c) Is correct. Estimated defect density is a measure of diligence; hence it belongs to the exit criteria.
d) Is not correct. Requirements translated into a given format result in testable requirements; hence it belongs to the entry criteria.
e) Is correct. Automation of regression tests is a completion criterion; hence it belongs to the exit criteria.

stem:
Your team follows the process that uses the DevOps delivery pipeline. The first three steps of this process are:

(1) Code development
(2) Submit code into a version control system and merge it into the “test” branch
(3) Perform component testing for the submitted code

Which of the following is BEST suited to be the entry criterion for step (2) of this pipeline?

options.a: Static analysis returns no high severity warnings for the submitted code
options.b: System version control reports no conflicts when merging code into the “test” branch
options.c: Component tests are compiled and ready to be executed
options.d: Statement coverage is at least 80%

explanation:
a) Is correct. This is something that can (and should) be checked before the code is submitted to version control.
b) Is not correct. This can be checked after step (2) is performed, because merge conflict reporting can be done after the code is submitted and merged.
c) Is not correct. This fits better as the entry criterion for step (3).
d) Is not correct. This fits better as the exit criterion for step (3).

stem: Which of the following BEST define EXIT criteria in a testing project?

options.a: Budget is approved
options.b: Budget runs out
options.c: Test basis is available
options.d: Test cases achieved at least 80% statement coverage
options.e: All test analysts are ISTQB certified at the Foundation Level

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The approval of the budget is an example of an entry criterion. It would make no sense to approve the budget for some activity that has already been done.
b) Is correct. Running out of budget can be viewed as a valid exit criterion.
c) Is not correct. Availability of resources is an example of an entry criterion for testing.
d) Is correct. Coverage is a measure of thoroughness, so it is a typical exit criterion.
e) Is not correct. This is an example of an entry criterion, checked before the project starts.

stem:
A team is preparing to start system testing of an insurance portal. Which of the following is an ENTRY criterion for this test level?

Select ONE option.

options.a: At least 95% of the identified product risks are covered by executed tests
options.b: The test environment is set up and the smoke tests on the delivered build have passed
options.c: No open defects with severity "critical" remain
options.d: All planned regression tests have been automated

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Achieved risk coverage is a measure of thoroughness, i.e., an exit criterion.
b) Is correct. Availability of resources (the test environment) and an initial quality level of the test object (smoke tests passed) are typical entry criteria.
c) Is not correct. The number of unresolved defects is a measure of thoroughness and therefore an exit criterion.
d) Is not correct. Automation of all regression tests is a completion criterion, i.e., an exit criterion.

stem:
Which TWO of the following are examples of exit criteria?

Select TWO options.

options.a: Statement coverage of at least 85% has been achieved
options.b: Test data for all planned test cases is available
options.c: The budget for the test level has been approved
options.d: Fewer than three high-severity defects remain unresolved
options.e: The user stories meet the Definition of Ready

explanation:
