d) Is not correct. iii should not be included and i is missing.

stem: Which test activity does a data preparation tool support?

options.a: Test monitoring and test control
options.b: Test analysis
options.c: Test design and test implementation
options.d: Test completion

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Test monitoring is ongoing checking of activities and comparing actual progress against the test plan; test control is taking actions to meet the test objectives. No test data are prepared during these activities.
b) Is not correct. Test analysis includes analysis of the test basis to identify and prioritize test conditions. Test data are not prepared during this activity.
c) Is correct. Test design and implementation can both include the identification, creation or acquisition of the testware necessary for test execution (e.g., test data).
d) Is not correct. Test completion activities occur at project milestones (e.g., release, end of iteration), so it is too late for preparing test data.

stem:
Given the following descriptions:

1. Support workflow tracking
2. Facilitate communication
3. Virtual machines
4. Support reviews

And the following test tool categories:

A. Static testing tools
B. Tools supporting scalability and deployment standardization
C. DevOps tools
D. Collaboration tools

Which of the following BEST matches the descriptions and categories?
explanation:
A. Static testing tools – support the tester in performing reviews and static analysis (4).
B. Tools supporting scalability and deployment standardization – e.g., virtual machines, containerization tools (3).
C. DevOps tools – support the DevOps delivery pipeline, workflow tracking, automated build process(es), CI/CD (1).
D. Collaboration tools – facilitate communication (2).
Thus a), b), d) are not correct; c) is correct: 1C, 2D, 3B, 4A.

stem: Tools from which of the following categories help with the organization of test cases, detected defects and configuration management?

options.a: Test execution and coverage tools
options.b: Test design and implementation tools
options.c: Defect management tools
options.d: Test management tools

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Test execution and coverage tools facilitate automated test execution and coverage measurement, but do not help with the organization of defects and configuration management.
b) Is not correct. Test design and implementation tools facilitate the generation of test cases, test data and test procedures, but do not help with the organization of defects and configuration management.
c) Is not correct. Defect management tools are used to manage defects but are not used to organize test cases or configuration management.
d) Is correct. Test management tools increase test process efficiency by facilitating the management of the SDLC, requirements, tests, defects, and configuration management.

stem:
Given the following test tool categories:

i. Collaboration tools
ii. DevOps tools
iii. Management tools
iv. Non-functional testing tools
v. Test design and implementation tools

Tools from which of the categories are MOST likely to facilitate test execution?

options.a: i, v
options.b: ii, iv
options.c: i, iii, v
options.d: ii, iii, iv

explanation:
i. Collaboration tools – facilitate communication. Communication does not include the facilitation of test execution.
ii. DevOps tools – support the DevOps delivery pipeline, workflow tracking, automated build process(es) and CI/CD. The delivery pipeline and CI/CD both include the facilitation of test execution, such as component testing for CI.
iii. Management tools – increase test process efficiency by facilitating management of the SDLC, requirements, tests, defects and configuration. This does not include the facilitation of test execution.
iv. Non-functional testing tools – allow the tester to perform non-functional testing that is difficult or impossible to perform manually. Non-functional testing can include both static and dynamic testing, including test execution.
v. Test design and implementation tools – facilitate generation of test cases, test data and test procedures. This does not include the facilitation of test execution.
Thus:
a) Is not correct.
b) Is correct. Both DevOps tools (ii) and Non-functional testing tools (iv) facilitate test execution.
c) Is not correct.
d) Is not correct.

stem:
Consider the following tools (1-4) and tool categories (A-D):

1. A tool that tracks requirements, test cases and defects and their relationships
2. A tool that checks source code against coding standards without executing it
3. A containerization tool used to create identical test environments on demand
4. A tool that generates load by simulating thousands of concurrent users

A. Management tools
B. Static testing tools
C. Non-functional testing tools
D. Tools supporting scalability and deployment standardization

Which option matches the tools to the correct categories?

Select ONE option.
explanation:
Tracking requirements, tests and defects is done by management tools (1A); checking code against standards without execution is static analysis (2B); containers support scalability and deployment standardization (3D); load generation is non-functional testing (4C).
a) Is not correct. 2 and 4 are mismatched.
b) Is not correct. 1, 2 and 3 are mismatched.
c) Is correct.
d) Is not correct. 1 and 3 are mismatched.

stem:
A team uses a tool that derives test cases from a state transition model and creates the corresponding test data. To which tool category does this tool BEST belong?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Test execution and coverage tools
options.b: Test design and implementation tools
options.c: DevOps tools
options.d: Collaboration tools

explanation:
a) Is not correct. These tools run tests automatically and measure coverage; they do not derive tests from models.
b) Is correct. Test design and implementation tools facilitate the generation of test cases, test data and test procedures.
c) Is not correct. DevOps tools support the delivery pipeline, workflow tracking, automated builds and CI/CD.
d) Is not correct. Collaboration tools facilitate communication.

stem:
Which of the following BEST describes how DevOps tools support testing?

Select ONE option.

options.a: They support the DevOps delivery pipeline, workflow tracking, automated build processes and CI/CD, so that automated tests can run on every change
options.b: They analyze work products such as requirements and code without executing them
options.c: They measure response times and resource usage under load
options.d: They provide chat and video conferencing for distributed testers

explanation:
a) Is correct. DevOps tools support the pipeline, workflow tracking, automated builds and CI/CD, enabling continuous testing.
b) Is not correct. This describes static testing tools.
c) Is not correct. This describes non-functional testing tools.
d) Is not correct. This describes collaboration tools.

stem:
A tool runs the automated regression tests overnight and reports which statements and branches of the code were exercised. To which tool category does it BEST belong?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Management tools
options.b: Static testing tools
options.c: Test design and implementation tools
options.d: Test execution and coverage tools

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Management tools increase efficiency of the test process by managing the SDLC, requirements, tests, defects and configuration.
b) Is not correct. Static testing tools do not execute the code.
c) Is not correct. Test design and implementation tools generate test cases, test data and test procedures but do not execute them.
d) Is correct. Test execution and coverage tools facilitate automated test execution and coverage measurement.

stem: Which item correctly identifies a potential risk of performing test automation?

options.a: It may introduce unknown regressions in production
options.b: Sufficient efforts to maintain testware may not be properly allocated
options.c: Testing tools and associated testware may not be sufficiently relied upon
options.d: It may reduce the time allocated for manual testing

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Test automation does not introduce unknown regressions in production.
b) Is correct. Wrong allocation of effort to maintain testware is a risk.
c) Is not correct. Test tools must be selected so that they and their testware can be relied upon.
d) Is not correct. The primary goal of test automation is to reduce manual testing. So, this is a benefit, not a risk.

stem: Which of the following is MOST likely to be a benefit of test automation?

options.a: It provides coverage measures that are too complicated for humans to derive
options.b: It shares responsibility for the testing with the tool vendor
options.c: It removes the need for critical thinking when analyzing test results
options.d: It generates test cases from an analysis of the program code

explanation:
a) Is correct. Test automation can provide measures that are too complicated for humans to derive, such as white-box coverage measures for all but the most trivial code.
b) Is not correct. Responsibility for testing is NOT shared with the tool vendor, which is not involved in the testing; it is the tester's responsibility. The only possible vendor responsibility is if the tool fails to work as expected and gives incorrect results.
c) Is not correct. Testers still need to apply critical thinking when analyzing anomalies in the test results to determine their likely cause.
d) Is not correct. Neither testers nor tools can generate test cases simply from analysis of the program code, as the code provides no information on the expected results, which must come from another part of the test basis, such as the design specification.

stem: Which of the following is MOST likely to be a benefit of test automation?

options.a: The capability of generating test cases without access to the test basis
options.b: The achievement of increased coverage through more objective assessment
options.c: The increase in test execution times available with higher processing power
options.d: The prevention of human errors through greater consistency and repeatability

explanation:
a) Is not correct. This is not possible. The generation of test cases by either testers or tools requires access to the test basis.
b) Is not correct. Test automation provides more objective assessment of coverage, but that assessment will not itself increase coverage; only using the results to write further test cases can increase coverage.
c) Is not correct. This is contradictory: higher processing power would normally reduce execution times, and increased execution times are not a benefit.
d) Is correct. Test automation prevents human errors through greater consistency and repeatability; e.g., tests are consistently derived from requirements, test data is created systematically, and tests are executed by a tool in the same order with the same frequency.

stem: Which of the following is MOST likely to be a risk of test automation?

options.a: The detection of additional high-severity defects
options.b: Providing measures that are too complicated for humans to derive
options.c: Incompatibility with the development platform
options.d: Substantially reduced test execution times

explanation:
a) Is not correct. The detection of additional high-severity defects would be a benefit of test automation, rather than a risk.
b) Is not correct. The provision of measures that are too complicated for humans to derive themselves is normally considered to be a benefit of test automation.
c) Is correct. If the test automation is incompatible with the development platform, then it will not be able to integrate with it and, for instance, pass test inputs to the test object and receive test results from the test object.
d) Is not correct. Substantially reduced test execution times would normally be considered a benefit that is provided by test automation.

stem:
Which of the following is a benefit of test automation?

Select ONE option.

options.a: It removes the need for test design because the tool creates all necessary tests
options.b: Automation is always cheaper than manual testing from the first iteration onwards
options.c: Tool vendors guarantee long-term support for their tools
options.d: Reduced test execution times, which enable earlier defect detection and faster feedback

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Test design is still needed; automation executes tests, it does not replace test design.
b) Is not correct. Introducing automation requires significant initial investment; underestimating it is a risk.
c) Is not correct. Dependency on a vendor that may stop supporting a tool is a risk of automation.
d) Is correct. Faster test execution provides earlier defect detection, faster feedback and faster time to market.

stem:
Which of the following is a risk of test automation?

Select ONE option.

options.a: More objective assessment, such as coverage measurement
options.b: Easier access to information about testing for test management and reporting
options.c: Greater consistency and repeatability of test execution
options.d: An open-source tool used by the team may be abandoned, so no further updates are available

explanation:
a) Is not correct. Objective assessment is a benefit.
b) Is not correct. Easier access to test information is a benefit.
c) Is not correct. Consistency and repeatability, preventing simple human errors, is a benefit.
d) Is correct. Abandonment of an open-source tool is a listed risk of test automation.

stem:
Which TWO of the following are risks of test automation?

Select TWO options.

options.a: Prevention of simple human errors through consistent execution
options.b: Underestimating the effort needed to maintain the test scripts
options.c: Relying too much on the tool and neglecting human critical thinking
options.d: More time for testers to design new, deeper tests
options.e: Less repetitive manual work, e.g., when executing regression tests

explanation:
a) Is not correct. This is a benefit.
b) Is correct. Inaccurate estimation of time, costs and effort, including script maintenance, is a risk.
c) Is correct. Over-reliance on a tool is a risk.
d) Is not correct. This is a benefit.
e) Is not correct. This is a benefit.

stem:
Which of the following is MOST likely a benefit of test automation?

Select ONE option.

options.a: Testers gain more time to design new, deeper and more effective tests
options.b: The tool can replace human judgement when evaluating usability
options.c: Automated test scripts no longer need maintenance once written
options.d: Automation guarantees that the software is free of defects

explanation:
a) Is correct. Freeing testers from repetitive work so they can design better tests is a benefit.
b) Is not correct. Usability evaluation requires human judgement; using a tool where manual testing is more appropriate is a risk.
c) Is not correct. Scripts require maintenance; underestimating this is a risk.
d) Is not correct. Testing (automated or not) cannot prove the absence of defects.
